Routed 2 drained signals.
decision_journal.root-cause: writeForeignFlowToOhlcv (apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/ohlcvForeignFlowStore.ts L58-69) BYPASSES writeOhlcvBatch and INSERTs a stub row open/high/low/close=0,volume=0 ON CONFLICT(code,date) when the foreign-flow fetch (gated to VN market open 02:00Z) arrives BEFORE the real OHLCV bar. taAlertScanJob/bbAlertScanJob CANDLE_SQL (SELECT close FROM daily_ohlcv WHERE date>=-60d ORDER BY day ASC) read that C=0 stub as TODAY latest candle: Wilder RSI with a final 0 after a ~27000 real close collapses to single-digit across ALL tickers simultaneously (CTG 3.4 / SSI 6.8 / VCB 3.7 on a +0.48% day = statistically impossible), and close=Math.round(0)=0 yields gia 0 duoi BB spam (msg 783-790, 02:15-03:15Z). Later the real OHLCV bar UPSERTs over the stub so canonical reads clean by 04:30Z. This is feedback_ohlcv_startup_purge_defeated_by_backfill_seeder: a re-seeding WRITER defeats the repair; fix the WRITER not the residue; trace ALL writers into daily_ohlcv (this was the un-migrated straggler).
decision_journal.what-considered: (1) re-open the closed OHLCV-seeder P0 — REJECTED: those fixes were real + done_verified; the bug is a DIFFERENT writer (foreign-flow store) they never covered; re-opening would hide that it is a coverage gap not a regression. (2) straight FIX to dev-alert-engine — REJECTED: 4th recurrence, owner zone proven WRONG twice (real root is a WRITER in apps/mcp-server, not alert-engine); recurring-bug-escalation mandates architect for the durable writer-SSOT root. (3) only patch the consumer scan guard — REJECTED as the SOLE fix: it stops the spam but leaves a fake C=0 OHLCV bar in the served table (poisons get_price_history / every other reader); the producer must stop writing fake 0-bars too (/goal#1 no-fake-data: illiquid means honest gap, never a 0 seed). (4) architect durable producer root (writer-SSOT across ALL bypass writers) PLUS dev consumer defense-in-depth guard, BOTH P0 — CHOSEN: kill the fake bar at the writer AND fail-closed at the reader.
decision_journal.why-change: Router LIVE-RAW-verified the symptom (msg 783-790) and the canonical-clean-by-04:30Z repair window; PO code-traced the SPECIFIC writer (writeForeignFlowToOhlcv C=0 stub) the migrated-writer set missed, and confirmed neither scan job rejects a C=0 / zero-volume latest bar. No change from router hypothesis — confirmed at code level and named the exact writer.

rows.summary: RETRACTED as detector output - emitted at crashRestarts=1 against a documented WARN threshold of >=2; underlying crash restart is real
rows.po_disposition_20260729T0625: RETRACTED, NOT DELETED. RULING: the row is withdrawn as a DETECTOR SIGNAL while the observation it carries is preserved in this field. TRIGGER PROVENANCE - THIS ROW IS NOT DETECTOR OUTPUT: it was produced by router spawn-prompt prose ('If A-21 now returns >=1, that is a TRUE POSITIVE - emit it') that contradicted the agent's own flow spec at docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:135-137 (crashRestarts>=2 -> WARN; crashRestarts<2 -> PASS, no emit). The router disclosed its own authorship. Recording it here because the emitted row carried no provenance field and was otherwise indistinguishable from ordinary detector output, and because the notebook prose that recorded the override sits on a retention path that deletes itself. WHY RETRACT RATHER THAN KEEP: retracting costs nothing that matters. crashRestarts=1 is BELOW the threshold, so A-21 remains ARMED - if a second crash restart lands in the 4h window the detector fires legitimately and on its own. Keeping the row would have left a WARN in po's inbox that the fleet reads as spec-compliant detector output, which is precisely the unreviewability defect being filed. WHAT IS REAL AND IS PRESERVED: the mcp-server crash restart at 2026-07-29T05:43:21Z (container restart 05:43:17Z) genuinely occurred; crashRestarts=1 in the 4h window is a true measurement. The agent's measurement was correct; only the emit decision was not. NOT VERIFIED BY PO and deliberately not relied upon: the router's added context that this follows a suppressed CRITICAL and an outage. Anyone citing that must verify it first. SUCCESSOR: FIX-AUDITOR-CALLER-PROSE-OVERRIDES-DOCUMENTED-DETECTOR-THRESHOLD (P1, architect) carries the generalisable defect. NOT A DETECTOR BUG - do not open a row against A-21 or ALERT_THRESHOLD; commit 2f956f1c5 set that threshold deliberately at parity with restartCadenceAlertJob.ts ALERT_THRESHOLD=2 and it behaved correctly here.
rows.po_disposition_amend_20260729T0632: AMENDMENT to the NOT-VERIFIED hedge above, and it makes the retraction STRONGER not weaker. The router context I declined to rely on IS corroborated - by PO's own immediately-prior cycle at 2026-07-29T05:55Z, recorded in docs/agent-memory/notebooks/po.md independently of this triage: Tier-1 at 05:41:23Z measured MemPerc 99.15% with verdict=ESCALATE reason peak-over-97%, and clause 4 of tier1-probe.md:167-171 downgraded it to PASS with signals_posted=0; the container went down at 05:43:16.520Z with RestartCount 3->4 during VN market hours. So a suppressed CRITICAL did precede this crash restart and the outage was real. WHY THIS DOES NOT REVIVE THE SIGNAL: the material event is ALREADY OWNED by three rows dispositioned in that 05:55Z cycle - FIX-AUDITOR-A30-VMHWM-VETO-TAUTOLOGY-FALSE-NEGATIVE (the suppressor, P1), OPS-MCP-RESTART-CHURN-UNCLEAN-SHUTDOWN and FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAK (both given next_agent=dev-mcp-server in that same cycle). A-21 measures crash CADENCE (2+ in a 4h window), which is a different question from this single crash and is not the vehicle for tracking it. Retracting this row therefore drops NOTHING: the outage is tracked on three rows, and A-21 stays armed for a genuine second crash. The correct reading of the whole episode is that the fleet had a REAL problem it had already detected and correctly filed, and the A-21 emit added an out-of-spec fourth artifact to it rather than new information.
rows.po_amend_20260729T0721: AMENDMENT (PO 2026-07-29T07:21Z, triage-20260729T0719). THE RETRACTION STANDS - the 06:09Z emit was caller-prose-driven and out of spec, and ALERT_THRESHOLD=2 remains deliberate and correct. TWO CLAIMS IN THE DISPOSITION ABOVE ARE NOW FALSIFIED AND MUST NOT BE CITED. (1) 'NOT A DETECTOR BUG - do not open a row against A-21': a detector bug HAS since been measured, and a row IS now open - FIX-A21-CRASH-WINDOW-PREDECESSOR-BOUND-FALSE-NEGATIVE (P1, architect). It is filed against the COUNTING QUERY at docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:112-131, NOT against ALERT_THRESHOLD or the verdict mapping, which this disposition correctly defended and which that row leaves untouched. (2) THE MORE SERIOUS ONE - the retraction's safety argument is void. It reasoned 'retracting costs nothing that matters ... crashRestarts=1 is BELOW the threshold, so A-21 remains ARMED - if a second crash restart lands in the 4h window the detector fires legitimately and on its own.' A-21 was NOT armed in that sense. PO re-measured the same query read-only at 07:16:51Z: it now returns crashRestarts=0 for the SAME unchanged ground truth, because the 2026-07-28 22:58:42 predecessor aged out of the fixed 8h fetch window at 06:58:42Z while the 05:43:21 crash was still 2h20m inside its own 4h alert window. The count does not hold and then fire on a second crash - it decays to 0 on its own, and reaching 2 requires THREE startups inside 8h rather than the documented two crashes in 4h. So the observation this row preserved was, at retraction time, the only surviving record of that crash in the detector plane. The preservation was therefore load-bearing, not merely tidy. NO ACTION NEEDED ON THIS SIGNAL: the crash itself remains owned by OPS-MCP-RESTART-CHURN-UNCLEAN-SHUTDOWN and FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAK, and the blindness that hid it is now owned by the new row.

rows.summary: chef-evening RETRY (re-dispatched 2026-08-05 ~19:52Z after original session death/marker-leak) actually executed ~10h43m later, at 2026-08-06T06:34-06:37Z. chef.md pins publish-date from wall-clock-at-execution (publish_date_basis=utc_date), so the retry targeted TODAY (2026-08-06) instead of backfilling the missed day (2026-08-05). Result: (1) 2026-08-05 evening dish permanently unfilled -- never published, confirmed via get_market_message_digest, no mcp-user chef post in the 08-05 evening window; (2) a premature, degraded-quality (0 clusters, 5 gap tokens) dish posted to MARKET under marker published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 at 06:37Z, 13h before the real 19:45 UTC scheduled fire; that marker is now a TOMBSTONE (publish confirmed, msg id 1129, per feedback_chef_leaks_published_marker_on_silent_exit invariant it must NOT be released) and will suppress tonight legitimate higher-quality scheduled chef-evening dispatch for 08-06 unless someone intervenes before 19:45 UTC today. Root cause is 2-fold: (a) chef.md / cowork-slot marker scheme has no way to target a specific backfill date on manual retry -- it always derives date from actual wall-clock; (b) the background Agent() retry itself sat queued roughly 10h43m before actually starting execution (the agent own runtime was only 175909ms) -- a possible session/scheduler stall during the same auth-outage window this session already hit 3x, worth checking separately. Recommend: po decide whether to manually release published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 before 19:45Z today to let the real slot fire (risk: near-duplicate post) vs accept this as the day dish (risk: degraded content stands, 08-05 gap stays permanent) -- and route the structural date-pinning gap to architect for a chef.md backfill-target-date parameter, or a router-side guard that refuses/relabels a retry once 2-3h have elapsed since the original intended slot.
rows.po_disposition:
PO 2026-08-06T06:54Z (corrected 07:02Z). (a) ACTED: released published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 at 06:53Z (RAW-verified gone from task_list_held) so tonight's real 19:45Z fire can run on fresh end-of-day data. Justified against feedback_chef_leaks_published_marker_on_silent_exit: the tombstone rule protects a marker whose KEY matches the content window it published. The date-drift defect broke exactly that binding -- msg 1129 carries 2026-08-05 session data under the 2026-08-06 key -- so the marker asserted a 08-06 evening publication that never happened, which is the lesson's OWN stated harm condition ("a published marker asserts a publication that never occurred -> it lies to the next tick's dedup gate and silently suppresses a legitimate later dish"). Double-publish exposure assessed ~0: catchup_raw has no consumer, chef-evening's cron "45 19 * * *" cannot re-match before 19:45Z, and tonight's dish will carry 08-06 session content, not a duplicate of 1129. Reader-facing collision nil -- 1129 landed 13:37 ICT 06 Aug, tonight's lands ~02:50 ICT 07 Aug, different VN-local days.
(b) ROUTED WITHOUT MINTING A NEW ROW -- prior art already existed and the correct action was to unstrand it, not duplicate it. FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-WINDOW-ANCHOR (P0, open since 2026-07-22, whose own title literally predicted this failure: "the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the [next] 19:45Z dish") promoted BACKLOG -> READY -> architect with full evidence and a concrete fix shape. TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3 (the stranded catchup_raw consumer) annotated with today's measured cost.
(c) FIELD CHANGE THAT MATTERS: the anchor row's inline `supervised:true` was REMOVED on promotion, deliberately. scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-ready-lane-consumer.jq:124-125 rejects any ready[] row whose effective_supervised is true, so promoting it with that flag intact would have re-stranded it in ready[] instead of backlog[] -- a strictly worse outcome, since it would then look dispatchable while being unreachable. PO grants the supervision go-ahead up front instead (feedback_po_autonomy); the row has been P0 for 15 days and has now cost a real MARKET dish, so no extra gate is warranted.
(d) CORRECTED THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE: the ~10h43m retry stall was macOS HOST SLEEP, not a session/scheduler stall inside the auth-outage window as this signal speculated. pmset -g log shows MAGICWAKE at 2026-08-06 08:34 CEST = 06:34Z, matching the retry's start instant exactly, and the agent's own runtime was only 175909ms. Do NOT open a scheduler/auth investigation on that basis.
(e) NOT FIXED, STILL OPEN: today's chef-morning (05:15Z) was also lost to the same sleep window and is still recoverable per catchup_raw but nothing consumes it; and the 2026-08-05 evening dish was never published as such -- msg 1129 carries its data but is labelled and keyed as 08-06.

rows.mechanism_hypothesis: This is distinct from the already-tracked feedback_preclaim_ttl_600s_expires_under_long_agent_runs.md mechanism (TTL expiring mid-run) and from feedback_pipeline_resume_stale_placeholder_duplicate_spawn_risk.md (PO's own triage_key). Here the board row already showed claimed_at/claimed_by IN_PROGRESS stamps (written by router at 18:36:54Z, BEFORE agent-father was even spawned) yet a peer session still dispatched its own agent-father onto the identical task_id shortly after — meaning either (a) the peer's dispatch path does not board-status-check a manually-router-claimed task before spawning, checking only its own PRE-CLAIM intent-key lock (which is scoped per-agent+intent, not per-task_id, so two peers each doing 'router manual dispatch' under different intent-keys would never collide on the lock itself), or (b) an extremely narrow TOCTOU window between the write and the peer's read. (a) is the more actionable hypothesis: PRE-CLAIM's task_id namespace is 'intent:<agent>:<intent-key>', which does not encode the specific task_id being dispatched, so it cannot prevent two different router sessions from both manually-dispatching the SAME underlying task_id under two DIFFERENT intent-keys (e.g. one from a PO-BATCH pass, one from a peer's own independent BOUNDED-1/triage pass) — only same-intent-key collisions are caught. Worth a root-cause check: should manual dev-team dispatch also claim a task-level lock keyed literally to the task_id (task:<task_id>), not just the intent-key, before spawning? Self-resolved with zero harm this occurrence (complementary work, no duplicate final state) but is architecturally reproducible any time two peer sessions independently decide to manually-dispatch the same backlog/ready row within the same short window.
rows.triage_note: INFO, self-resolved with zero harm, but the mechanism_hypothesis (a) is correct and actionable: PRE-CLAIM's task_id namespace is 'intent:<agent>:<intent-key>', which does not encode the task_id being dispatched, so two peer router sessions manually-dispatching the SAME task_id under DIFFERENT intent-keys never collide on the lock. Same family as memory feedback_router_intent_path_double_dispatches_cowork_slots. NOT minted this tick - the remedy (claim task:<task_id> in addition to the intent key before any manual dev-team dispatch) belongs with the orphan/coordination-lock FR set already sitting in ready[] (FIX-ORPHAN-FR1-FR2-INFRA-HEARTBEAT-LADDER, FIX-ORPHAN-FR1-FR3-FR6-SKILL-DISPATCH-CLAIM), and FR-4/FR-5 was folded into this tick's BATCH. entries.vision: Make /dashboard/prediction-claims update DAILY, not weekly. User: page not update many day, wants update continue day by day. ROOT CAUSE (router RAW-confirmed + PO-verified live): page + /api/prediction-claims + predictionClaimsHandler are HEALTHY — do NOT touch them. The DATA PRODUCER is starved: prediction_claims has only 9 rows, newest 2026-06-14 (agentId 08-prediction-synthesizer). The synthesis flow (digest-predict/flow/monday.md, P-3..P-5 create_prediction_claim) was DISABLED by Sprint 1949-T5 (Monday prediction synthesis removed — Sunday weekly covers full scope); the Sunday weekly.md flow only READS get_prediction_accuracy, it never calls create_prediction_claim. So NO active flow has produced a claim since 1949-T5 — the 06-14 batch was the last routed run. Live confirm: get_prediction_accuracy(30d)=no results; calibration Brier=0.1379 healthy (product is SOUND, just unfed).
entries.product_decision: Option (a) chosen: re-enable prediction synthesis on a DAILY cadence by routing digest-predict to a daily prediction sub-flow + a new daily cowork slot, WITHOUT disturbing the Sunday weekly calibration report. Daily update = a daily synthesis run that CREATES new high-conviction claims when fresh evidence appears AND lets existing open claims keep accruing toward their multi-day/weekly horizon (e.g. W26). It is NOT a forced 5-claims-every-day spam. GUARDRAILS (designed by architect first): (1) per-DAY cap (small, e.g. 2-3) replacing the monday max_prediction_claims_per_week:5, with a weekly ceiling so cadence cannot inflate claim volume; (2) same-day idempotency marker via task_claim (TTL ~20h) keyed on day+slot so a re-fire never double-creates; (3) NO-OP cleanly when no ticker passes the bullish/bearish>0.6 high-conviction filter (do NOT lower the bar to manufacture daily claims — standing no-fake-data directive); (4) Sunday weekly.md calibration report stays unchanged + un-regressed.
entries.success_metric: LIVE: prediction_claims gains new rows on consecutive (high-conviction) days; /dashboard/prediction-claims generatedAt + rows reflect them day-over-day; daily/weekly caps honored; flat-market day no-ops without fabricating claims; Sunday weekly MARKET calibration dish still fires unchanged. (3) BCTC pivot (B): if at S6 gate the extractor still can't hold 2 weeks health or deferred_infra can't drop below ~30% of queue -> abandon in-house structured extraction for historical quarters, downgrade B to vnstock-only fundamentals, reserve PEK for current-quarter filings.

entries.root_cause: PROVEN on two planes. (1) The host —France/CEST— lost its caffeinate wake-lock at ~05:00-05:13Z (pmset: multiple `caffeinate ClientDied`) when the interactive CLI session holding the */15 CronCreate cowork dispatcher ended; the host then entered standby/darkwake. (2) The launchd StartInterval guaranteed-slot firer provably did NOT execute for ~11.5h (05:58Z->17:34Z): the firer logs a line whenever it MATCHES a guaranteed slot, and chef-eod(08:45Z)+fb-daily(09:15Z) had last_fired=07-21 which does NOT suppress them, so had launchd run the firer in-window it WOULD have logged+fired them — their total absence from the 07-22 log proves StartInterval never ran (host not rebooted: uptime 11d; job not unloaded: resumed same-day 17:34Z). Both coverage planes were dark. On resume at 17:34Z the matcher only offers slots within +/-2min of the CURRENT nominal tick — the 08:45/09:00/09:15/11:00/14:00Z windows were hours gone and NEVER re-offered. `guaranteed:true` is therefore a false promise across any host-standby/session-down window: neither plane has look-back/catch-up.
entries.vision: Make cowork `guaranteed:true` an HONORED contract, not a false promise. A guaranteed slot whose firing window elapsed while the host was in standby or the session was down must, on the next live tick/startup, either be recovered exactly once within a bounded freshness-safe catch-up window, OR record a structured (non-silent) miss when the VN trading day has already rolled past its window — and the `guaranteed` label must be corrected wherever it overstates real coverage.
entries.scope_in: TRACK A (PRIMARY, dev-team chain): add look-back/catch-up to the guaranteed-slot firing path shared by all 3 callers (scripts/agents-flow/cowork-match-slots.js matcher, scripts/agents-flow/cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.sh launchd firer, and the live */15 dispatcher startup). On each tick/startup, in addition to the +/-2min current-tick match, detect guaranteed slots DUE earlier in the current VN trading day but never fired (last_fired < today scheduled-fire epoch) and re-offer them IF now is within a bounded, per-dish-type catch-up window that keeps the deliverable meaningful (tight for market/FB posts, looser for chef/digest). Dedup STRICTLY via the existing published:<slot_id>:<VN-work-date> task_claim marker so a late catch-up never double-posts and never labels stale data as fresh. VN-date rollover is explicit: if the VN day rolled past the slot window, DO NOT retro-post under a new date — skip + record miss. CONSOLIDATES the existing cluster (subsume together, do NOT re-litigate): SPIKE-DEAD-WINDOW-20260722-EIGHT-HOUR-SILENCE (root-caused by this triage — its `already_ruled_out: machine sleep` note is INCORRECT, corrected here), SPIKE-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-SUPERSEDE-WIRING (root-caused), FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION (the 07-22 chef-morning exit_code=143 SIGTERM at the 1800s bound / 600s subagent kill truncates guaranteed dishes — catch-up re-firing must complete, not re-truncate), FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-DUAL-PLANE-DOUBLE-FIRE (catch-up adds a 3rd fire path — published-marker arbitration must be verified airtight), FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY (catch-up detects a miss via last_fired, so last_fired MUST reflect DELIVERY not just spawn-dispatch). DOC-HONESTY: update cowork-schedule.json `guaranteed` semantics + docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/*.md + docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-07-cowork-guaranteed-slot-durability.md + docs/protocols/cowork-master-cron-runbook.md to state the true coverage envelope.

entries.vision: An agent CANNOT persist incomplete or malformed data anywhere in the project. Every agent write surface is schema-validated; a rejected write throws a descriptive error naming exactly which required field is missing/invalid so the agent understands and self-corrects. Stored data is guaranteed-complete and future-proof.
entries.scope_in: Uniform STRICT-schema coverage + a standardized per-field descriptive-error contract across three write-surface classes: (A) MCP write-tools in mcp-server (~150 tool files, partial Zod today); (B) script-gated JSON (orch-state via orch-apply.sh — the proven template); (C) the ~77 docs/data/*.json + agent notebooks + docs/handoffs written DIRECTLY via Write/Edit with NO runtime gate. Generalize the agentSignalTools GOLD error message + audit-log rejection; strict Zod (no .passthrough(), no silent partial writes).
entries.scope_out: Fetch-side completeness recon (already separate FRED/SBV/news tasks); rewriting the proven validators already DONE (signalTypes/agentSignalTools/foreignFlowValidator/signalBuilders/orch-validate). No new business logic — validation coverage + standardization only.
entries.success_metric: Every surface in the A/B/C inventory either enforces a strict schema at write time or is explicitly waived with rationale; a deliberately-incomplete write to each class is REJECTED with a per-field error naming the missing field; enforcement is FAIL-CLOSED (a crashed validator blocks, never silently passes — closes UC-CRITIC-HOOKS-ENFORCEMENT).

entries.vision: When any frontend data surface goes stale AT REST, the system automatically DECIDES the root cause and ROUTES a remediation: mint a dev FIX task if the fetch/writer CODE is broken, OR call the responsible refresh agent (market-watcher / news-scout / the cron fetchers) to re-run if the data merely wasn't refreshed — with NO alert spam. This is the auto-REMEDIATE layer (conceptually FFT-L6) sitting ON TOP of L4 detection. Detection already exists and emits SLA-breach signals, but today they DEAD-END: alert-commander suppresses freshness-sla-monitor urgent_news every cycle as infra noise (DS-OBS-01-FIX note in freshnessSlaMonitorJob.ts lines 538-548), so a genuine stale-page breach never mints a fix and never re-runs a fetcher — the user's 'many frontend pages show non-updated data' persists because the signal has no remediation consumer.
entries.scope_in: THREE genuinely-new pieces ON TOP of L4: (1) REMEDIATION-TRIAGE decision-layer — for each breaching surface, read its coverage-map .writer + .cadence, probe the writer's live runtime (generalize queryBctcPipelineRuntimeState's queueDepth+serviceActive idle-vs-crash reader across ALL coverage-map surfaces, not just bctc), and CLASSIFY broken-code (writer service down / erroring / never-scheduled) vs not-refreshed (writer healthy+idle, just didn't run) → route to dev FIX vs refresh-agent re-invoke. (2) ANTI-SPAM gating — REUSE apps/alert-engine dedup-key-builder + cooldown-gate primitives (Go) plus the existing sla_breach_audit 60-min cooldown table; key dedup by (surface, breach-class); SUPPRESS repeat signals while a remediation task/signal is already OPEN for that surface; keep the isVnMarketHours() market-hours gate. (3) ORCHESTRATION integration — REDIRECT the breach signal OFF the dead-end alert-commander addressee ONTO the po/dev-team signal_queue drain (the existing anomaly→BACKLOG bridge: emit-audit-signal.sh + po-s* drain-mint jq library) so remediation is AUTO-picked-up, not a dead alert. Detection-completeness input: coverageMapFreshnessChecker.ts currently maps only 5 of 50 surfaces to DB queries (ENDPOINT_DB_QUERY) — the other 45 are silently skipped, so 'many pages' cannot even be detected yet; widening endpoint→DB coverage is an input the architect must scope for the triage layer to be effective.
entries.scope_out: NOT re-building L4 detection (FIX-L4-FRESHNESS-SLA-MONITOR-SELF-POLICING owns verify-live + wire-if-missing of the detector/emitter — stays a separate READY task, do NOT widen it). NOT the frontend badge / auto-revalidate display layer (L3 = FIX-L3-FRONTEND-AUTOREFRESH-FRESHNESS-BADGE + FE-PG-*-FRESH-FIX — that shows staleness to the USER; this ACTS on it). NOT the input-validation sprint (that gates bad writes at input-time; this catches data going stale over time). NOT rebuilding alert-engine dedup/cooldown (REUSE the Go primitives). NOT overlapping system-auditor's two-layer fetch-vs-analysis freshness audit (coordinate, don't duplicate).
entries.success_metric: A forced real breach on a watched surface (a) is CLASSIFIED broken-code-vs-not-refreshed by a live runtime probe (RAW: scheduler log shows the classification), (b) produces EITHER a minted dev FIX task in task_board.backlog (broken-code) OR a re-invoke call to the named refresh agent (not-refreshed) — verified live, not self-report, (c) does NOT re-emit while that remediation is still OPEN (dedup/cooldown proven by a second tick producing no duplicate), (d) the breach signal lands in the po/dev-team signal_queue drain, NOT the suppressed alert-commander path. DoD gate is RAW live evidence per each, not unit-test-only.
entries.product_decision: PO decision: COMPANION sprint, NOT widening FIX-L4. L4 stays the 'does the detector fire + emit' gate (READY, dev-mcp-server, about to execute); this sprint owns 'what happens when it fires'. Widening L4 would bloat a verify-live FIX into a multi-week build and risk the health-recheck stale-duplicate footgun. First concrete step is an architect SPIKE (design-gated) because the broken-code-vs-not-refreshed classifier is genuine technical design (PO not_my_job). Implementation tasks are decomposed by architect/PM/BA AFTER the spike — mint minimally now.

Verified by reading source, not inferring: (A) WRITER = docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/eod.md:29 (Step B 'SIGNAL FILE'), schema literal at :33, output contract declared at :13. (B) CONSUMER = docs/agents/unified-agent/flow/chef.md:116 — 'Collect file groups: price_anomaly_* — from market-watcher'. Chef reads by DIRECT PATH GLOB over docs/signals/ top-level, NOT via the drain. (C) The by-path contract is already written down in THREE places: eod.md:15 ('Chef (unified-agent) reads the signal file at 08:37 UTC EOD dish'), eod.md:61 ('File written atomically; chef reads at 08:37 UTC (24min settle window)'), and docs/agents/market-watcher/init.md:119-121 (sends_to unified-agent, note 'Chef reads price_anomaly_*.json at 05:23/08:37/19:37 UTC'). WHY EVERY PRIOR REPORT MISSED IT: greps were restricted to .js/.ts/.sh and treated .md as 'documentation'. In this system flow docs ARE the executable source for LLM agents — excluding .md from a writer search structurally cannot find any cowork writer. TWO PLANES SHARE THE NAME: the DB/MCP plane (market-watcher/flow/cycle.md:179 post_agent_signal signal_type=price_anomaly -> alert-commander via get_agent_signals; this is what docs/standards/mcp-tools.md:175 documents) is the INTRADAY path; the FILE plane (eod.md -> Chef) is the EOD path and deliberately does NOT call post_agent_signal. ANSWER TO 'where is this analysis supposed to go': already decided, and it is option B of the signal's own framing — a Chef/dish input read directly by path. It is NOT undelivered; it only LOOKS undelivered to a drain that was never its transport.

PO's shape-of-complaint survives; only its mechanism was wrong, and the breach window is ~13.5h per business day, not '47.5 of every 48 hours'. The fix mirrors the NEWS branch at lines 667-673 exactly: inside the isVnSbvBusinessDay(now) arm, return cfg.defaultThresholdMinutes only while within the publish window, else minutesSinceLastSbvWindowEnd(now) + OFF_HOURS_GRACE_MINUTES. This is a ~3-line change to one branch, not a new capability.

backlog.title: PUBLISHED-MARKER LIFECYCLE — one marker-gate skill, publish-state-conditioned immunity; wire into the 6 copy-pasted gates (P0: caused CONFIRMED user-visible MARKET double-publish 2026-07-15 ids 932+933)
backlog.note:
P0-PROMOTED 2026-07-15T20:06Z by po from signal cow-20260715T195545 (CONFIRMED user-visible double publish, MARKET ids 932+933). UMBRELLA — folds FIX-CHEF-PUBLISHED-MARKER-RELEASE + FU-CHEF-MARKER-INFLOW; both set BLOCKED on this row. THEY MUST NOT SHIP INDEPENDENTLY — independent point patches provably OSCILLATE: 07-02 marker released post-publish -> double publish; 07-03 remediation said release-on-every-no-post-exit -> marker LEAKED on silent exit, suppressing legit dishes; 07-15 an agent complied with the 07-03 rule and released after a REAL publish -> double publish again. The two memory lessons feedback_chef_leaks_published_marker_on_silent_exit (release it!) and feedback-chef-releases-published-marker-enables-peer-double-publish (never release it!) are in DIRECT CONTRADICTION and are auto-injected into agent context — so ANY prose-only fix is non-deterministic by construction. ROOT CAUSE (deeper than the release itself): chef.md claims the marker at Step 0.5 line 32, ~650 lines and one full expensive gather/synthesis BEFORE send_telegram. Claiming before the publish decision is what forces a conditional-release rule, and agents get that conditional wrong in BOTH directions. Note the existing UC-CCA-P3 clause mandatory release-on-no-publish is INSUFFICIENT — it encodes the 07-03 half of the pendulum only. REQUIRED INVARIANT (the WHAT — architect/ba own the HOW): marker release-immunity MUST be a function of publish-state, not of agent prose. Publish SUCCEEDED -> marker is an immutable tombstone, TTL is the ONLY expiry path. Publish NOT attempted/failed -> marker must not survive. PO DESIGN RECOMMENDATION (non-binding, architect decides): two-phase gate — (1) early cheap READ-ONLY probe task_list_held(task_id=MARKER_KEY) at Step 0.5 to abort before burning the pipeline, claiming NOTHING so a leak is impossible; (2) task_claim immediately before send_telegram, claimed:false -> EXIT without sending, claimed:true -> send -> NEVER release. Late-claim makes conditional-release logic unnecessary while the early probe preserves the cost optimisation the current early-claim was reaching for. AC-CODE-GATE (assess, do not assume): prose gates have now failed 3x — evaluate a code-enforced backstop at the releaseTask() choke point in apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/system/coordinationTools.ts (single choke point, also guard task_force_release_orphan) refusing release of task_id matching ^published: . Prefer a task_id-prefix guard over a new task_kind enum value: published: markers and cron: election locks TODAY share task_kind cowork-slot with opposite semantics (dispatch-claim SKILL.md §3.1 table literally documents TTL never released vs explicit release at dispatch end for the same kind), and adding an enum member has a known drift class (feedback_preclaim_gate_taskkind_enum_drift: Zod enum + SQLite CHECK + call sites). ALSO IN SCOPE: chef.md Step 0.5 omits owner_client_session entirely — a violation of spawn-fanout.md L56 (REQUIRED, P1-FINAL TASK_1980) and an unfixed repeat of 07-03 defect #2. AC: (1) invariant holds for both single-fire (TTL 100800) and multi-fire (TTL=cadence) slots; (2) a silent/no-post exit leaves NO marker; (3) a successful publish leaves a marker no agent can release; (4) all 6 copy-pasted gates wired to the one skill; (5) RAW-verify via task_list_held after a real evening dish — marker MUST still be held.

[po 2026-07-17T09:28:15Z ABORT-PATH AC EXTENSION — RECURRING] 2nd CONFIRMED live marker leak of this class: published:chef-eod:2026-07-17 HELD (task_list_held: owner_agent unified-agent, owner_client_session d0ec32a5-5f74-4bc0-a076-10d925d061a5, claimed 08:50:19Z, expires 2026-07-18T12:50:19Z) via ABORT-AFTER-CLAIM (chef.md Step 0.5 early-claim, then mid-flow bail before publish — nothing published). The DESIGN RECOMMENDATION already in this note (early READ-ONLY probe + LATE task_claim immediately before send_telegram, claiming NOTHING until publish) STRUCTURALLY eliminates ALL pre-publish exits incl. abort; implementer MUST NOT ship a partial late-fix that re-introduces an early claim with conditional release. CAUTION: the AC-CODE-GATE release-refusal backstop (^published: prefix guard at releaseTask()) guards the WRONG direction for THIS leak — it would block cleanup of a leaked tombstone; the leak is prevented by the late-claim redesign, not the release guard. backlog.key_agreement_20260722T2010Z: [po 2026-07-22T20:10Z, from router intent chef-evening-double-publish; owner/priority/next_agent/scope UNCHANGED] AC EXTENSION — KEY AGREEMENT IS A SEPARATE PRECONDITION, NOT COVERED BY THIS ROW'S ACs. 5th real-world confirmation of the marker-gate cluster and the FIRST with a root cause this row does NOT address. On 2026-07-22 chef-evening published TWICE (19:56:15Z and 20:00:37Z, 4.5 min apart, two CLI sessions) because the two runs derived DIFFERENT marker keys from the SAME wall-clock instant: published:chef-evening:2026-07-22 and published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 were both HELD simultaneously (task_list_held, ttl 100800 each). Cause: chef-evening's cron `45 19 * * *` = 19:45 UTC = 02:45 VN of D+1, so chef.md Step 0.5's WORK_DATE = TZ=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh date +%Y-%m-%d straddles a date boundary. CRITICAL: this row's own DESIGN RECOMMENDATION (early read-only probe + late task_claim immediately before send_telegram + never release) DOES NOT PREVENT IT — both peers compute different keys, both probes read free, both late claims succeed, both publish. Lifecycle and key-agreement are orthogonal. THEREFORE: UC-CCA-P3 MUST NOT be signed off while the key is derived from a wall-clock `date` read at the leaf. Added AC(6): the marker key is window-anchored and timezone-free (derived from the scheduled cron fire-window in UTC, never from a `date` call made by the executing agent), so two peers on the same window derive byte-identical keys. Root cause + full PO ruling on key-vs-label separation tracked in sibling row FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-WINDOW-ANCHOR (P0) — the two MUST ship as ONE design (architect first); neither alone closes the class.

po_triage 2026-07-25T09:27:11Z — ORIGIN DETERMINED + LANDMINE DETONATED (3rd sighting; NO NEW ROW MINTED).

cowork-team signal cwk-20260725T091107-1f13 asked PO to adjudicate between (a) emitter drift — emit_pressure_state produces a literal the policy vocabulary never had — and (b) "closed" is a deliberate fourth state the cadence-policy.json rows were never grown to cover, and warned "do not mint a fix task against a guessed root cause".

VERDICT: NEITHER (a) NOR (b). Traced at source, not inferred:
  - emitPressureStateTool.ts:387 stores `args.calendar_status ?? "unknown"`. calendar_status is CALLER-SUPPLIED. The server never computes it and can never itself emit "closed" — its only self-generated value is "unknown".
  - telemetry.md Step 6.0 L15 passes `"calendar_status": "<CALENDAR_STATUS from Step 4.3>"`.
  - pressure-read.md L65: `CALENDAR_STATUS = PRESSURE_STATE.calendar_status` — read FROM pressure-state.json.
  The dispatcher reads the field out of the very file it then writes back. Closed self-recycling loop, no authoritative producer anywhere in the chain. Whatever literal enters the file once persists forever. This is precisely the "circular" mechanism this row was minted for — so the fix lands in the CALLER + the TOOL BOUNDARY, not in cadence-policy.json.

ENABLER (why an out-of-domain literal survives): the tool's Zod schema is bare `z.string().optional()` (emitPressureStateTool.ts:459) — no enum gate — even though its own describe() text names the 5-value domain 'open'|'weekend'|'holiday'|'half_day'|'unknown'. The correct producer ALREADY EXISTS and is simply not wired: vnTradingCalendar.ts session_status returns exactly {open, weekend, half_day, holiday, unknown} — a perfect match for the policy file's domain.

STATUS CHANGE (this is what is genuinely new, and it is the reason to act):
memory lesson feedback_pressure_state_caller_supplied_fields_dead_server_computed_live named "off_market" and "closed" as an ARMED LANDMINE that was latent ONLY while calendar_status stayed frozen at "unknown". IT IS NO LONGER LATENT.
  - Live docs/data/pressure-state.json at 2026-07-25T09:24:44Z reads calendar_status="closed".
  - Signal files read "unknown" through 2026-07-23, then "closed" from 2026-07-24T17:37Z onward — "closed" is now the recycled steady state, not a one-off.
  - Consequence, live every weekend tick since 07-24: no cadence-policy row matches, slots fall through to the 240-min generic default instead of their declared weekend rate (gatherer-standard 480, bctc-offmarket 1440) — over-firing non-guaranteed slots by up to ~5 extra runs per weekend day.
  - Third out-of-domain literal for the class, historical precedent: "off_market" in docs/signals/processed/cowork-team-2026-06-07T19:47:55Z.json.

SCOPE UNCHANGED — no re-scope needed. This row as written already names all four fix points (compute via vnTradingCalendar isVnTradingDay().session_status; enum-gate the caller override; stop preflight recycling the file value; DELETE the telemetry Step 6.0 arg line). Implementer: do not re-litigate the origin, it is settled above.

CO-SHIP REQUIREMENT STANDS: must ship together with FIX-COWORK-CADENCE-DANGLING-POLICY-ID (policy-domain validation). Fixing the producer without validating the domain re-arms the identical class the next time any caller invents a literal.

backlog.po_do_not_ship_alone_20260725T1649:
po 2026-07-25T16:49:30Z — WARNING ATTACHED, SCOPE UNCHANGED, NO RE-MINT. Read this before implementing: shipping this row as written, on its own, would REMOVE A SYMPTOM AND LEAVE THE DEFECT, which is worse than not shipping it.

A coordinator finding this tick proposed attaching a mislabelled-report case here on the theory that this row's "filename heuristic / pattern-guessing" IS the mechanism. PO traced it and IT IS NOT. Do not absorb that case into this row.

THE FILENAME IS NOT GUESSED FROM NOTHING — IT IS RENDERED FROM THE STORED PERIOD KEY. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:224 calls normaliseFilename(sourceUrl, actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter), and apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 returns canonical ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf unless the source URL's own basename both ends in .pdf and already contains the action code. So the canonical filename is a faithful projection of financial_reports.period_year/period_quarter — the two cannot disagree, and today the filename is the ONLY place a wrong period identity is visible to a human reading a directory listing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S DELIVERABLE. "Derive the real filename from source metadata instead of pattern-guessing" is a reasonable goal on its own terms, but it decouples the filename from the stored period. If the stored period is wrong, the file would then be named correctly while the DB row remains mislabelled — the corruption becomes invisible instead of fixed. The live case that prompted this: report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d is stored as DPM_2025_Q4.pdf while its refined content is unambiguously Q1-2026 across five independent pages. The filename is what exposed it.

SEQUENCING RULE, NOT A SCOPE CHANGE: FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT (backlog/P1) must land FIRST. That row adds the period-vs-content validation the ingest boundary has never had (bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:194-201 validates only that the year is 2000..2099 and the quarter is one of Q1..Q4 — shape, never correspondence). Once a wrong period identity cannot be stored, decoupling the filename from it is safe and this row becomes a clean improvement. Until then, this row's change would delete the tripwire.

ADD TO THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE when it is eventually worked: a real-filename derivation must not be able to mask a period mismatch — either it preserves a period assertion somewhere visible, or the validation row has already landed. Priority and scope otherwise unchanged (P3/backlog); this is a dependency note, not a promotion.
backlog.po_binding_dep_20260725T1700:
po 2026-07-25T17:00:10Z — BINDING GATE ADDED. Supersedes the decorative guard po attached at 16:49Z.

WHAT WAS WRONG. At 16:49Z po wrote `blocks: ["FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES"]` onto FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT and treated that as a sequencing guard. IT WAS NOT ONE. The dev-team 16:37Z tick caught it and po re-verified at source: scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-141 `effective_depends_on` reads ONLY the CANDIDATE row's own `.depends_on` + `.depends` + `.blocked_by` (inline first; falling back to backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows). It never traverses a reverse `blocks` edge from another row. `deps_satisfied` (:161-164) then short-circuits `true` on an empty list. A full grep of scripts/lib/*.jq, scripts/devteam-*.jq, scripts/orch-*.mjs, scripts/orch-*.sh and scripts/agents-flow/*.sh confirms `blocks` is READ BY NOTHING anywhere in the repo — the only textual hits are unrelated test prose ("blocks idle"). This row therefore carried NO dependency at all in either plane (board row and the backlog-detail.json entry both had depends_on/depends/blocked_by = null), and with supervised/plan_only/owner/next_agent all null, status BACKLOG and no children, it was FULLY BOUNDED-1 ELIGIBLE. Only its P3 rank was holding it back, and rank is queue position, not a guard.

WHAT IS NOW TRUE. `depends_on: ["FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT"]` is written INLINE on this board row. Inline is the binding location by construction: `effective_depends_on` takes inline when non-empty and only consults backlog-detail.json when inline is empty. The gate's own semantics work in this row's favour on both axes — per the code comments at :159-164, a dep is satisfied ONLY when it resolves to `DONE_VERIFIED` (plain `DONE` is NOT sufficient), and a dep id found in NO lane is treated as UNSATISFIED (conservative-skip). The blocker is currently backlog/BACKLOG, so this row is gated until the period-validation fix is genuinely verified, not merely marked done.

WHY IT IS WORTH A REAL GATE AND NOT A COMMENT. Shipping this row alone does not merely fail to help — it makes things worse. The filename is RENDERED from the stored period key (bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:224 -> resolvePdfText.ts:45-61, canonical `ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf`), so today it is the only place a wrong period identity is visible to a human reading a directory listing. Deriving "real" filenames from source metadata decouples the two: a mislabelled row would then be named correctly while the corruption persists, invisibly. That is symptom deletion, and it is exactly what a decorative guard would have permitted.

THE REVERSE `blocks` EDGE IS DELIBERATELY RETAINED on the blocker row as human-readable documentation of intent. It is not load-bearing and must not be relied on. The systemic problem — that `blocks` reads as a constraint while binding nothing — is now owned by FIX-ORCHSTATE-BLOCKS-FIELD-WRITE-ONLY-DECORATIVE (backlog/P2).

LATENT HAZARD, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED THE HARD WAY. scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh defaults `STUB_FIELDS="id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref"` — `depends_on`, `depends` and `blocked_by` are NOT in the keep-set. If that migration is ever re-run over the backlog it will strip this inline dep from the hot row. Normally harmless, because `effective_depends_on` falls back to backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows and this row has a detail_ref — EXCEPT that the strip is documented idempotent with "existing cold wins" (docs/policies/dev-standards.md), and the existing cold entry for this id already carries `depends_on: null`. A re-strip could therefore drop the inline value while the stale null survives in cold, silently re-opening this gate. Scope item on the systemic row above; do NOT hand-edit backlog-detail.json to pre-empt it (761KB, outside the orch-apply validation gate — the cure is worse than the risk).

Priority and scope otherwise UNCHANGED (P3/backlog/S). This is a sequencing gate, not a promotion.

backlog.note: EVIDENCE ADDENDUM 2026-08-01 (po/triage-auditor-findings-20260801) — A CLAIM AGAINST THIS ROW WAS TESTED AND FALSIFIED; recorded here so it is not re-raised. THE CLAIM (from a 3-tier auditor brief): "a 24-hour window predicate on agent_signals returns far FEWER rows than the table holds, because the bound datetime(now,-24 hours) is space-separated while alert-engine writes ISO-8601-with-T, so the string comparison silently drops most rows", citing 12 of 116 / 15 of 119 / 20 of 124 from three tiers, and asserting this corrupts C-07 own published output. BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG. (a) DIRECTION IS INVERTED. Measured live 2026-08-01T06:14Z: rows matched by the space bound but NOT by a T bound = 2; rows matched by a T bound but NOT by the space bound = 0. The space-separated bound drops ZERO rows. This is the same direction this row title already states ("T (0x54) > (0x20) at position 11 makes every T row sort AFTER every space row within the same date") -- the defect is FALSE INCLUSION, never exclusion, exactly as the original +61%/60-minute measurement found. (b) THE CITED NUMBERS ARE A DENOMINATOR ERROR, NOT A DEFECT. The denominators 116/119/124 are the WHOLE agent_signals table, which is only partially pruned and spans back to 2026-05-18 (live 2026-08-01: 131 rows total; by month 2026-05:28, 2026-06:52, 2026-07:39, 2026-08:12). A 24h window returning ~20% of a 2.5-month table is correct arithmetic. Format-agnostic ground truth via julianday(replace(replace(created_at,T, ),Z,)) >= julianday(now,-24 hours) = 27; the live space-separated predicate also returns 27 -- i.e. on this data the 24h predicate is currently EXACTLY RIGHT, 0 rows in error. po_triage 2026-07-25T09:27:11Z — THIS ROW'S "(240 genuinely safe)" PREMISE IS NOW REFUTED BY LIVE EVIDENCE.

This row's class statement asks the implementer to "distinguish policy-not-found (config error -> cron fallback per FR-P1-2) from unmatched-rule-in-real-policy (240 genuinely safe)". The parenthetical is wrong, and there is now a live counter-example.

COUNTER-EXAMPLE (observed 2026-07-25, 2 sightings same day — cowork signals cwk-20260725T091107-1f13, tick 08:00Z and 09:00Z): pressure-state.json emits calendar_status="closed" (live at 09:24:44Z, steady since 2026-07-24T17:37Z). Both gatherer-standard and bctc-offmarket are REAL, present policies — so this is NOT policy-not-found, it is exactly the "unmatched-rule-in-real-policy" case this row declares safe. It is not safe: the 240-min generic default silently REPLACES the slot's declared weekend rate (gatherer-standard 480, bctc-offmarket 1440), over-firing non-guaranteed slots by up to ~5 extra runs per weekend day, with the slot's declared policy bypassed and nothing logged.

THE CORRECTED DISTINCTION: unmatched-rule-in-real-policy is safe ONLY when the unmatched axis VALUE is itself in-domain (a legitimate combination the table simply does not enumerate). An OUT-OF-DOMAIN axis value — calendar_status="closed" against the file's 5-value domain {open, half_day, weekend, holiday, unknown} — is a CONFIG ERROR wearing the unmatched-rule costume, and must take the fail-loud path, not the 240 default.

AC ADDITION (do not ship this row without it): the standing `[.slots[].policy_id] - [.policies[].policy_id] diff == []` check is necessary but not sufficient — it validates only the policy_id axis. Add a DOMAIN check on the VALUE axes: every literal the dispatcher can emit for calendar_status (and any other policy-matching axis) MUST be a member of that axis's value set in cadence-policy.json; fail loud on miss instead of silently absorbing it into the 240 default.

CO-SHIP with UC-CDC-P1 (see that row's 2026-07-25 note for the traced root cause: calendar_status is a caller-supplied self-recycling loop with no enum gate). Producer fix without this domain validation re-arms the class; domain validation without the producer fix leaves the value permanently wrong. Neither alone is sufficient.

backlog.po_saturation_evidence_20260725T1625:
po 2026-07-25T16:25:39Z — EVIDENCE FOLDED IN, NO NEW ROW MINTED. This annotation changes what "done" means for this row; read it before implementing.

THIS ROW'S OWN IMPACT ASSESSMENT IS NOW OBSOLETE AND MUST NOT BE ACTED ON AS WRITTEN. The note above says "at the live rate 26110 all three currently agree on direction, which is exactly why this has stayed invisible — the divergence only bites between 25000 and 26500." That framing treats the defect as a LATENT disagreement. It is no longer latent, and the more serious problem is not the disagreement at all.

MEASURED THIS TICK, AT SOURCE: apps/macro-indicators/pkg/primitive/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier.go:34 BearishThreshold = 25000.0, line 37 BullishThreshold = 23000.0, so the NEUTRAL band is 23000-25000 and BULLISH requires < 23000. Live rate 26130. The rate has not been under 25000 in a long time and is not trending back. BEARISH IS THEREFORE THE ONLY REACHABLE OUTPUT OF THIS CLASSIFIER — it is SATURATED, not merely divergent. A three-valued direction classifier has silently become a constant that still reports a verdict on every call, and consumers cannot distinguish "the model assessed the rate and found it bearish" from "the model can only say bearish". news-scout emitted "USDVND 26130 bearish >25000 threshold" from it in both c199 and c200 today.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — THE STATED GOAL IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. "Pick one SSOT" does not fix saturation if the value picked is 25000, and 25000 is the most likely pick precisely because it is the one with a named exported constant in Go. Shipping a single-SSOT refactor on 25000 would close this row while leaving the classifier constant — and would additionally propagate the saturated threshold to the two planes (25500 in macroTools.ts / macroAdjustments.ts) that are currently, by accident, slightly less wrong. AC ADDITION, mandatory: whatever value is chosen, add a test asserting that BOTH the bullish and bearish branches remain reachable at the CURRENT live rate, not at a fixture rate. A classifier whose test suite only exercises synthetic inputs cannot detect that its live input has left the discriminating range.

THE DURABLE FIX IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF THRESHOLD, AND THAT DECISION BELONGS TO WHOEVER WORKS THIS ROW. A fixed absolute threshold on a drifting nominal exchange rate saturates eventually by construction — this is not a mis-set constant, it is a design that has a shelf life. Honest options: [a] make the threshold relative (z-score or percent deviation against a trailing window, so the discriminating range travels with the series); [b] keep absolute levels but bind them to a real policy anchor (e.g. the SBV reference-rate band) that is itself revised, and add a staleness alarm on the anchor; [c] keep 25000 as a deliberate permanent red-line and DELETE the NEUTRAL/BULLISH branches plus the "direction classifier" framing, so the output honestly reads as a single boolean threshold breach rather than an assessment. What is NOT acceptable is shipping one SSOT and leaving three branches of which two are unreachable. po did not choose among these.

That SPIKE does NOT own this fix; this row does. Priority and scope otherwise unchanged.

backlog.title: An agent-side context-budget limit is written into permanent report state as a data failure — failed_ct is indistinguishable between 'source data is bad' and 'worker could not hold a 1.2MB image'
backlog.mechanism: For the final 4 windows of POW_2026_Q1 the refine agent reported the page-28 image fetch returned ~1.2MB of base64 that 'exceeded context token budget'. That is a limit of the SUBAGENT's context window — not a property of the document and not of the pipeline. Per its error-boundary contract the agent pushed FAILED for those windows and called finalize_bctc_refine, producing refine_status=FAILED with failed_ct=28.
backlog.why_it_matters: The failure reason is now indistinguishable, in stored state, from a genuine data defect. A future remediation pass reading failed_ct=28 cannot tell that some windows failed because a transcription worker could not hold a 1.2MB image rather than because the page is unreadable. Combined with the head-of-line row this is also what makes the head row PERMANENTLY dead: the finalization is sticky.
backlog.fix_direction: Introduce a distinct terminal-ish status (e.g. DEFERRED / RESOURCE_EXCEEDED) that does NOT finalize the report and leaves the window re-attemptable by a worker with a larger budget or via an image-downscale path. Do not class it with text_fetch_failed.
backlog.scoping_caution: The agent FOLLOWED its documented graceful-degradation contract — this is NOT filed as agent misbehaviour. The defect is that the contract has no distinct terminal status for 'worker could not process within its own resource envelope' versus 'source data is bad'. Prior art (the BCTC reingest guard: 56/56 FAILED/empty-markdown, data-loss guard refused to wipe bctc_table_rows) shows the downstream cost of that ambiguity is already being paid elsewhere.
backlog.advisory_do_not_chase: The refine agent recommended 'investigate upstream text extraction (get_bctc_page_text) for POW reports'. That is WRONG-ROOTED as a current root cause and must not become a task: the store reports text_status=COMPLETE, cowork-team called get_bctc_page_text(report_id=78b06684..., page_number=1) — one of the 24 pages said to have failed — and got full Vietnamese OCR text with source='sqlite_ocr', and the agent's own report contradicts itself ('Page 28 text retrieved successfully'). LIMIT ON THIS REFUTATION: it does NOT prove text was retrievable when the 24 units failed on 2026-07-19; text may have been backfilled since. It establishes only that pointing an implementer at get_bctc_page_text TODAY sends them at a component that demonstrably works.
backlog.ordering: Sequenced AFTER the head-of-line fix — that one unblocks the live queue and is the urgent half; this one prevents the next sticky-dead head row. Do not merge them: one is a query predicate, the other a status taxonomy, and they must be verifiable independently.
backlog.acceptance: (1) a worker-resource failure records a status distinct from data failure; (2) that status does NOT finalize the report; (3) the affected windows remain re-attemptable; (4) POW_2026_Q1's existing failed_ct=28 is NOT retroactively reinterpreted — historical rows stay as-is unless a separate explicit decision says otherwise.

backlog.title: news-chain BCTC fallback writes an all-zeros balance sheet into financial_reports — the authoritative table — where it is byte-indistinguishable from OCR corruption at serve time; decide whether it should write there AT ALL before guarding arm (b2)
backlog.origin: QA found this sibling writer while approving arm (b2) on parseBctcReport.ts::storeReport(), and explicitly DECLINED to mint or to expand that row (correctly — PO had a scope-hold on it). Router sharpened the finding at source and also declined to mint. Minting is PO's; this is that mint.
backlog.mechanism: newsChainFallback.ts (apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/newsChainFallback.ts) is a SECOND, independently-implemented writer to the same financial_reports (action_code, sort_key) row as storeReport(). It already has arm (b1): lines 264-274 block the write when existingReportRow.total_assets > 0, preserving a previously-good row and logging BLOCKED. What it LACKS is arm (b2): with NO prior row it proceeds to INSERT a brand-new row whose totalAssets is a hardcoded 0 (line 307, bound into the INSERT at line 535), inside an entire all-zeros balance sheet at lines 304-313. Identical defect shape to the one just fixed in storeReport(): refuses to overwrite a good row, but freely CREATES a fresh zero-total row that bctcIdentityGuard.ts then reads at serve time as the OCR-corruption fingerprint. The file's own comment at lines 254-263 already says it 'carried the same two defects' and 'mirrors the identical guard' — the mirror was completed for only one of the two arms.
backlog.po_verified_at_source_20260721T1811: PO RE-READ THE FILE THIS TICK rather than accepting QA's or router's description, and the single decisive fact checks out: `totalAssets: 0` at line 307 is a hardcoded LITERAL and is the ONLY assignment to that field in the whole file (grep: refs at 73, 255, 307, 425, 535 — 307 is the sole write, 535 binds it to the INSERT, 425 is the SQL column list, 255 is the comment, 73 is the summary formatter). There is NO code path in this function that can produce a non-zero balance sheet. The surrounding lines 304-313 are likewise all-zero literals across currentAssets, nonCurrentAssets, liabilities, equity and totalLiabilitiesAndEquity.
backlog.product_question_decide_before_scoping: ANSWER THIS FIRST — the fix does not follow from the defect. Question as router framed it: if a news-inference fallback only ever produces directional hints and never real balance-sheet figures, is writing it into financial_reports — the table bctcIdentityGuard treats as authoritative at serve time — the actual design error, such that guarding arm (b2) alone merely relocates the problem? PO'S STRONG STEER, WITH THE PROOF: YES, IT IS THE DESIGN ERROR, and here is the reductio that settles it. Arm (b1) already blocks every write where a good row exists. Arm (b2), applied literally, blocks every write where NO row exists AND totalAssets<=0. Since totalAssets is hardcoded 0 on EVERY call (verified above — no path produces otherwise), the two arms together block 100% of this function's writes. Adding arm (b2) does not fix the function; it silently converts it into a total no-op while leaving ~600 lines of live, tested, maintained code in place pretending to be a working fallback. A guard that makes its own subject unreachable is not a guard — it is proof that the write target is wrong. CORROBORATING, AND THE PART THAT MAKES THIS USER-FACING RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: (i) the code's OWN comment at lines 254-259 already concedes the whole argument — 'this fallback ALWAYS writes totalAssets=0 ... it reconstructs directional hints from news signals, never real balance-sheet figures — i.e. every call is, by construction, the exact OCR-corruption fingerprint bctcIdentityGuard.ts checks for at serve time.' The codebase has already diagnosed itself; nobody drew the conclusion. (ii) The write is strictly WORSE than not writing, because it destroys an honest signal: an absent row serves 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' ('we do not have this'), whereas a zeros row serves '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0 (OCR extraction failure)' — a false claim that we HAVE the filing and it is broken, which misattributes a defect to the filer. This is the same family of harm as the ngay_nop flip on the parent row: fabricating a state that defames a real-world filing. (iii) buildAnalysisSummary() at line 73 formats this into Vietnamese RAG-retrievable prose — 'Tong tai san: 0 trieu dong.' — a flat factual assertion that the company has zero total assets, written into the retrieval corpus. That is fabricated financial data in a served surface, and it engages feedback_no_fake_data_real_fetch directly. THEREFORE the design target to evaluate is: directional news-inference hints belong in a hints/signals surface, NOT in financial_reports. BA must still evaluate the alternatives honestly (a separate table/column; a nullable-financials sentinel row explicitly marked non-authoritative that bctcIdentityGuard excludes; or deleting the write path entirely and keeping the function as a pure read-side hint producer) — my steer is not a pre-selected implementation, and if BA finds a consumer that genuinely needs these rows in financial_reports, say so and I will revisit.
backlog.six_tests_encode_the_defect: THE HARD PART, AND WHY THIS IS A PO/BA ROW AND NOT A FIXER TICKET. SIX existing tests assert the first-ever zero-total write SUCCEEDING, i.e. they encode the defect as intended behaviour: 1294b-bctc-fallback RED-1 / RED-6 / RED-7 / RED-8-first-call (VCB/VIC/BSR/VJC first-call, all no-prior-row first-ever writes asserting fallback:true + row-exists), and BOTH cases in FIX-BCTC-NEWS-CHAIN-FALLBACK-ID-ORPHAN (run#1 explicitly commented first-ever-write, asserting fallback:true + row-exists for Q1 and Q2 sort_keys). QA adjudicated these individually and confirmed they are genuine intent-assertions, not incidental fixture inconvenience — that adjudication is accepted and must NOT be re-derived. These six are IN SCOPE to be rewritten by this row, and rewriting them is the deliverable that encodes whatever product answer is chosen. They are also the reason a quiet patch is impossible: any honest fix turns six green tests red, and a developer without this row's authority would reasonably read that as 'my change is wrong' and revert — which is EXACTLY what happened once already (see prior_attempt_reverted).
backlog.prior_attempt_reverted: dev-mcp-server ALREADY TRIED the naive fix during the parent row's arm-(b2) work: applied the storeReport guard pattern to tryNewsChainFallback(), broke those 6 tests, and reverted cleanly — documenting it as an open gap in usecases.md rather than folding it in. That was the RIGHT call under a scope-hold and is not a failure; it is corroboration that the naive patch is blocked by design intent, not by a fixable test bug. Do not re-attempt the naive guard.
backlog.containment_do_not_downgrade: BLAST RADIUS IS BOUNDED — THIS IS LATENT, NOT BLEEDING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT P0. Router grep-confirmed the containment independently of QA: enableBctcFallback is declared optional at bctc/types.ts:59, DEFAULTS TO false at fetchParseAndStoreBctc.ts:50 (destructured `enableBctcFallback = false`), and resolvePdfText.ts:228 gates the fallback call behind `if (!enableBctcFallback)`. No non-test caller passes it true. THE FLAG IS THE CONTAINMENT AND MUST BE RECORDED AS SUCH — two failure modes to pre-empt: (1) nobody may downgrade this row on the grounds that 'the flag is false so it is safe' — the flag being false is WHY this is HIGH rather than P0, it is already priced in, and re-applying it is double-counting; (2) NOBODY MAY ENABLE enableBctcFallback ANYWHERE — test, staging or production — UNTIL THIS ROW IS CLOSED. Flipping that flag with arm (b2) open turns a latent hole into live manufacture of corrupt authoritative financial rows, on the exact mechanism the parent row was minted to stop. If a future task needs the fallback enabled, it depends on this row.
backlog.acceptance: (1) A written product decision on where news-chain fallback output belongs, stated on this row before any code is scoped — either 'not in financial_reports' (PO's steer) with the replacement surface named, or a reasoned rebuttal naming the consumer that requires those rows in financial_reports. (2) The chosen design implemented such that no all-zeros row is ever CREATED in financial_reports by this path. (3) The six tests named in six_tests_encode_the_defect rewritten to assert the CHOSEN behaviour, with each rewrite's intent stated — not deleted, not skipped, not left asserting the old contract. (4) get_bctc_full for a ticker with no real filing serves honest absence ('Chua co du lieu BCTC'), never '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0' manufactured by this path. (5) Arm (b1) behaviour is preserved unchanged — a previously-good stored report is still never overwritten. (6) If the write path is removed entirely, buildAnalysisSummary()'s zero-valued Vietnamese output (line 73) must not reach any served or RAG-retrievable surface either — check that plane explicitly, do not assume removing the INSERT covers it.
backlog.verification_gate: MECHANISM-SCOPED AND FULLY CODE-LEVEL — deliberately carries NO ingest, deploy-window or multi-day dependency, unlike the parent row (this is why it can converge in one pass). (a) A forced/simulated news-chain fallback invocation for a ticker with NO prior financial_reports row creates NO row — asserted against the live serving path via get_bctc_full returning 'Chua co du lieu BCTC', not by reading the DB plane directly (parent-row precedent: the DB plane and the serving plane diverged and only the serving plane matters here). (b) Same invocation for a ticker WITH a good stored row leaves it untouched and still serving non-zero total_assets (arm b1 regression). (c) grep proves no remaining code path can bind a hardcoded zero balance sheet into a financial_reports INSERT. (d) RED-before demonstrated by git-stash A/B with the test changes kept, same technique dev-mcp-server used on the parent row's arm (b2). (e) Full suite run and every failure file-attributed, not name-grepped — 1405b-bctc-vps-fixes.test.ts is a known decoy (has 'bctc' in the filename, its failures are in the unrelated logVpsPush group and are a test-order flake).
backlog.scope_boundaries: DOES NOT own re-extraction or remediation of any already-corrupt or absent report — that stays with OPS-BCTC-REFINE-REPASS-NONBANK-5T, W5-FU-CTG-REFINE-96e36139 and SPIKE-BCTC-Q1-2026-SERVABILITY-CENSUS. DOES NOT own the scale-signature corruption class (FIX-BCTC-VALIDATION-GATE-NONBANK-ZERO-SCALE, e.g. BSR total_assets=166.52 vs equity=145892845365) — different fingerprint, different row.
backlog.why_ba_first: plan_only + next_agent=ba because acceptance (1) is a design decision with a real alternatives space (separate surface vs non-authoritative sentinel row vs delete the write path), and the six-test rewrite in (3) must encode whichever answer wins. backlog.title: 'Write acceptance criteria before editing files' is structurally unverifiable for every agent whose commit zone excludes orch-state.json — move acceptance authorship to the dispatcher
backlog.po_evidence: Surfaced by the FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD-SKILLS supervised sign-off 2026-07-21. agent-father claimed it wrote acceptance onto the row BEFORE editing any file, and the row carries self-reported acceptance_written_at=2026-07-21T19:08:10Z. But the acceptance text's FIRST appearance in git is 304f24edd at 19:14:24Z, AFTER the skills commit 3e4f50d3a at 19:12:13Z — because agent-father's commit zone excludes docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, so a peer cold-evict swept the board and collapsed the acceptance-write and the lane-move into one indistinguishable blob. The claim is UNVERIFIABLE, not disproven. acceptance_written_by/acceptance_written_at are self-reported fields authored by the same agent whose ordering they attest — they are narration, not evidence.
backlog.po_ruling: The dispatcher's framing is correct and generalises: an agent whose commit zone excludes the board can NEVER produce evidence for an ordering claim about the board. Requiring such a claim therefore mandates an unfalsifiable self-report, which is exactly the failure class feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation.md warns about. The requirement is unenforceable across the whole maintenance lane, and the unsatisfiable dispatch instruction was the dispatcher's error, not agent-father's — no fault attaches to the agent. PREFERRED RESOLUTION: acceptance is authored by the DISPATCHER (or PO) at dispatch time, before spawn. The dispatcher's commit zone already includes the board, so ordering becomes provable by construction across two disjoint zones: dispatcher commits acceptance, implementer commits code, and git ordering across the two zones is independently checkable. Rejected alternatives: (a) letting maintenance agents commit the board row themselves — breaks zone separation and re-introduces the peer-sweep class this very sprint just fixed; (b) silently dropping the requirement — loses the real benefit that acceptance predates implementation.

backlog.title: Session-scoped CronCreate loops are invisible and unpersisted across 5 CLI sessions — build the launchd-hosted liveness watchdog that turns 'a session died and its whole loop vanished' from silent into a BUG-channel alert
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 4 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 (cron-registry.json) landing first; this row is that registry's first consumer. See po_design_ruling below: the design call was made, this row implements one third of it.
backlog.problem: CronList in the router session returns 'No scheduled jobs.' Crons live inside 5 separate CLI sessions (dev-team, cowork, system-audit, claude-heler, workflows-fix). No session can see or repair another's crons. When a session dies its whole loop vanishes with zero trace. CronCreate additionally only fires while the REPL is idle, so a session stuck mid-query fires nothing. PO verified there is NO on-disk cron persistence under ~/.claude (no crons dir; ~/.claude/jobs/ holds two stale June background-job state dirs, unrelated).
backlog.po_design_ruling: OPTION (a) BROADER LAUNCHD COVERAGE — SCOPED, plus (c) MONITORING. Option (b), a persistence/registry layer for CronCreate, is REJECTED as a new scheduler. Reasoning: (1) building persistence for CronCreate means re-implementing a scheduler we do not own, inside a surface (the CLI REPL) whose contract can change under us; we already own two durable planes (launchd, and the containerized mcp-server node-cron scheduler with 85 jobs) and a third home-grown one is exactly the 'duplicating cron hosts' that UC-CDC-P5 already names as the thing to avoid. (2) launchd is the ONLY plane that survives session death and it demonstrably works (firer: 815 runs). (3) But WHOLESALE migration to launchd is equally wrong — `claude -p` per tick is expensive and, per FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION, structurally truncates fan-out work. So launchd hosts loop RE-ARM and LIVENESS, not every loop. (4) The REPL-idle constraint is unfixable from our side; that is a second independent argument for making session-plane failures VISIBLE rather than trying to make the session plane reliable. (5) Monitoring alone (option c as a terminal answer) is also rejected: without a registry there is nothing to monitor against.
backlog.three_part_sequence: PART 1 (registry of record) — FOLDED INTO EXISTING UC-SDF-P6, not re-minted: the 5 session-scoped loops must be DECLARED in a repo file so absence becomes detectable. Not a new scheduler; an inventory. PART 2 (this row) — one launchd-hosted watchdog that reads that registry and alerts when a declared loop has produced no evidence-of-life within its cadence. PART 3 (re-arm automation) — EXISTING UC-CDC-P5, sequenced LAST, only after 1+2: re-arming blind is how you get double-hosted crons.
backlog.hard_constraint_evidence_of_life: Evidence-of-life MUST be the loop's own external artifact — its commits, its notebook mtime, its telemetry row — NEVER a self-report or a heartbeat the loop writes about itself. A loop that can assert its own liveness is a loop whose watchdog is self-satisfying (see FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FRESHNESS-CHECK-RELOCATE-TO-SENTINEL in ready[], same defect class, already ruled).
backlog.acceptance: Kill any one of the 5 sessions and, within one cadence period, a BUG-channel message names the dead loop. Today that event is completely silent.

backlog.title: Three time bases coexist in one scheduling system: server jobs mix timezone UTC and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, CronCreate fires at MACHINE-LOCAL France time (CEST/CET, DST-sensitive), and the market it serves is fixed UTC+7 — no single place states what any job's real wall-clock is
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 7 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 cron-registry.json. A registry that records each job's declared time base is most of this answer; doing it before the registry means writing the same table twice.
backlog.problem: (1) mcp-server scheduler jobs individually declare timezone:'UTC' or timezone:'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'. (2) CronCreate jobs fire at machine-local France time (CEST=UTC+2 summer / CET=UTC+1 winter) and therefore SHIFT BY AN HOUR twice a year against the market. (3) Vietnam is fixed UTC+7 with no DST. A job authored as '15:00' has three different meanings depending on which plane it lands on, and nothing declares which.
backlog.dst_is_the_sharp_edge: The France planes silently re-time relative to the VN trading session at each DST transition. docs/standards/cron-jobs.md:292 already documents this reasoning for the guaranteed-slot firer (StartInterval chosen over StartCalendarInterval precisely because the latter is DST-sensitive) — the insight exists but is applied in exactly one place. Next transitions to check against: late Oct 2026 (CEST->CET) shifts every session-plane cron one hour LATER relative to UTC/VN.
backlog.folded_item_5b_minute_collision: FOLDED (item 5b, LOW): restartCadenceAlert (server plane) and cron-db-data-integrity (terminal/session plane) both sit on `15,45 * * * *`. PO assessment: these run in different processes and share no resource except SQLite, so this is a same-minute COINCIDENCE, not a contention bug — it is folded here rather than minted separately because a cron-registry with declared time bases is what makes cross-plane minute maps computable at all, instead of discoverable only by hand-audit.

backlog.title: Add StartLimitIntervalSec=0 to systemd units to prevent crash-loop lockout after transient failures
backlog.description: vn-price-fetch, vn-foreign-flow, vn-sbv-fetch crashed ~2026-07-21 03:05-09 UTC and entered systemd failed state due to missing StartLimitIntervalSec=0 hardening. Systemd default StartLimitIntervalSec=10s/StartLimitBurst=5 causes permanent failed state for any Restart=always unit crashing >=5 times in 10s window. Hardening has been proven safe by commit 42e8448ce (applied to vn-news-fetch/vn-reuters-fetch/vn-tradingeconomics-fetch 2026-05-02) — vn-news-fetch rode through the same incident window unaffected, demonstrating the control. This incident was non-recoverable without manual intervention due to inbound SSH/HTTP being blocked to VPS (user-gated restart already escalated via Telegram).
backlog.scope: Add StartLimitIntervalSec=0 to [Unit] section of vps-scripts/vn-price-fetch.service, vps-scripts/vn-foreign-flow.service, vps-scripts/vn-sbv-fetch.service, vps-scripts/vn-bctc-fetch.service; audit vps-scripts/vn-agm-plan.service and vps-scripts/vn-reuters-fetch.service deployment status (both exist in repo but are never scp'd/enabled by scripts/deploy-vinahost.sh — same dead-code class as OHLCV-backfill gap from c023). Identify and fix byte-identical duplicate deploy scripts (scripts/deploy-vinahost.sh and apps/mcp-server/deploy-vinahost.sh) — update both or dedupe and select one for deployment.
backlog.acceptance: Repo hardening complete: all 4 units have StartLimitIntervalSec=0; redundant deploy script verified or deduped; agm-plan and reuters-fetch units disposition determined (deployed-to-vps OR removed-as-dead-code); redeploy via scripts/deploy-vinahost.sh; live systemctl restart on VPS succeeds (user-gated after reachability restored). Post-deploy: all 3 services recover from failed state and resume pushing data; vn-bctc-fetch state verified separately. BACKFILL (added 2026-07-22T22:45Z from po triage of auditor signal sys-20260722T223302-4f8b): recovery must also REPAIR the outage-window gap, which does not self-heal because prices/foreign-flow pushes are live-only. Live-measured at 43h: daily_ohlcv 2026-07-21=416 tickers and 2026-07-22=51 tickers against an 887-984/day baseline (07-13..07-20), and daily_foreign_flow has NO 2026-07-22 row at all (baseline 102/day). Post-restart acceptance: daily_ohlcv coverage for 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-22 restored to >=880 tickers/day and daily_foreign_flow has a populated 2026-07-22 row; if the existing ohlcv_backfill_queue path cannot cover foreign-flow, state that explicitly and raise the follow-on rather than closing with the gap open.
backlog.notes: Root cause from git: commit 42e8448ce (2026-05-02) added StartLimitIntervalSec=0 to vn-news-fetch/vn-reuters-fetch/vn-tradingeconomics-fetch only. Commit message explicitly lists vn-price-fetch/vn-foreign-flow/vn-sbv-fetch/vn-bctc-fetch as "had no burst limit and are unchanged" — this premise is inverted. No explicit override means systemd applies its compiled-in default (StartLimitIntervalSec=10s/StartLimitBurst=5), not "no limit".
