backlog.title: cowork-team parallel fan-out has no producer/consumer ordering — alert-commander read the signal bus before its co-dispatched producers wrote to it, and went silent on a session with real >5% drops
backlog.mechanism: BGFAN-1 mandates run_in_background=true for every dispatcher spawn and spawn-fanout.md issues all matched slots in ONE parallel block, with no dependency ordering. When a tick matches both a PRODUCER (market-watcher -> price_anomaly; news-scout -> urgent_news/chain_catalyst) and a CONSUMER (alert-commander -> gates on those exact signal types), the consumer can complete its bus read before the producers have posted.
backlog.evidence_16_00Z_tick: Dispatched together: news-scout-offhours, market-watcher-offhours, market-watcher-eod, alert-commander-critical. alert-commander ran ~16:10-16:15Z and reported zero verified_chain/chain_catalyst/price_anomaly on the bus, verified by explicit signal_type-filtered calls — its evidence was CLEAN, the bus genuinely WAS empty at read time. market-watcher-offhours then posted price_anomaly 8680 (GAS -6.98%, 2.89 sigma, 4.02x volume) and 8681 (D2D -3.30%, 52-week low) at ~16:17Z, AFTER alert-commander had exited silent.
backlog.why_this_matters_beyond_tidiness: alert-commander's position-danger gate failed at condition 1/3 for want of price signals its SIBLING produced two minutes later, on a session with real >5% drops (GAS -6.98%, BSR -6.49%, GEX -5.16%). The silent exit was CORRECT given what it could see. The dispatch order is what made it blind. This is a market-facing miss, not an internal hygiene issue.
backlog.options_for_architect: (a) order the fan-out into producer-wave then consumer-wave within a tick; (b) have consumers re-read the bus after a bounded wait when co-dispatched producers are known to be in flight; (c) accept and document that consumers lag producers by one tick. PO has NOT pre-selected one — this is a genuine design decision with a latency/complexity tradeoff and it belongs to architect. Note cowork-team correctly refused to self-modify its own dispatch contract.
backlog.second_order_in_scope: R3 (match-slots.md Step 4b: multi-slot collision WARNs but never blocks) spawned market-watcher TWICE the same tick — the EOD slot fired late (~16:08-16:13Z) pushing the 16:09 dispatch into offhours, so TWO market-watcher cycles processed the SAME 08:32 closing prices four minutes apart. R3 is working as written; the written rule is what needs review. Fold into this design pass — same dispatcher, same tick-ordering root.
backlog.important_scoping_do_not_absorb: This does NOT establish that get_alerts(type=price) is broken. alert-commander separately reported get_alerts(type=price) empty; prior art FIX-ALERT-SCAN-REJECT-STUB-BAR-P0 and FIX-ALERT-OPEN-ZERO-PRICE-RACE sit in that neighbourhood and were deliberately NOT re-filed. At least part of this cycle's blindness is dispatcher ordering, not detector failure. BOTH causes may be live — do not let this row absorb the detector question or close it by proxy.
backlog.acceptance: Architecture brief selecting (a), (b) or (c) with the tradeoff stated, plus the decomposition into implementable rows. If (c) is chosen, the documentation must land somewhere a consumer agent actually reads, not only in the brief.
backlog.architect_design_summary: Chose bounded async schedule_task recheck (variant of PO option b, not synchronous wait) over two-phase wave (a, breaks BGFAN-1 fire-and-forget + risks fire-election TTL lapse) or accept-and-document alone (c, row is market-facing). Mechanism: tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 captures won_slots at dispatch time (last_fired is stamped at spawn not completion, so a consumer re-deriving co-dispatch after the fact would be silently defeated) -> surfaced through the already-shared cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md tick-snapshot read every cowork agent uses (zero spawn-fanout.md prompt-template edit) -> alert-commander schedules ONE schedule_task recheck (~20min, cowork-schedule.json producer_settle_wait_seconds field) only when a co-dispatched gatherer producer is known AND its own read was empty AND this is not already a recheck (bounded, real discriminator, zero cost on quiet ticks). Prerequisite gap found: alert_commander SKILL_MANIFEST does not grant schedule_task today (apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/bootstrap/agentBootstrap.ts:115-139). R3 folded in as root-cause fix: market-watcher/flow/main.md derives sub-flow from wall-clock time and discards the slot= the dispatcher already sends -- a late EOD-slot fire silently loses eod.md own deliverable, not just duplicate compute; match-slots.md Step 4b kept WARN-only (DDD: dispatcher cannot know same-trading-day-close domain fact). digest-daily flowpath/trigger_prompt signal confirmed orthogonal. 8-row PM decomposition T1-T8 in brief section 9.
backlog.po_ruling_deviation_accepted_20260721T18: DEVIATION FROM (a)/(b)/(c) — ACCEPTED. Architect was right to not pick one of my three literals, and the row's own options_for_architect text explicitly said PO had NOT pre-selected one. I verified BOTH brownfield facts the deviation rests on at source rather than accepting them: (F4) docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/last-fired.md:10 states 'AC-P1-7-1: last_fired written after successful spawn' — confirmed, last_fired is stamped at SPAWN, not completion, so any consumer re-deriving co-dispatch from it after the fact would read a slot as fired before its output exists and be silently defeated. That single fact kills the cheap version of (b) and justifies the tick-snapshot won_slots capture instead. (F7) docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/main.md:10-14 routes on wall-clock UTC windows only, and Step 2 ('Read current UTC time. Match the window above') never consumes the slot= the dispatcher already sends — confirmed, the parameter is discarded. Both facts hold. The chosen bounded-async schedule_task recheck is a better option than any of my three: it keeps BGFAN-1's parallel fire-and-forget contract untouched (the real cost of (a), compounded by the fire-election 600s TTL lapse risk during a multi-minute in-session wait), pays zero cost on quiet ticks (the real cost of (b)-as-worded), and does not leave a market-facing miss undefended (the disqualifier for (c)). Brief section 3 states the tradeoffs plainly as the row's acceptance required — including the two I most wanted named: detection latency goes to a bounded ~20min and NOT to zero, and a tick now has two possible verdicts so telemetry readers must check the recheck cycle too. Acceptance MET. Released to pm for the 8-row T1-T8 decomposition.
backlog.po_ruling_r3_folds_here_20260721T1811: ITEM 4 RULED — FOLDS INTO THIS ROW, NO SEPARATE ROW MINTED. The market-watcher slot-routing defect (a late-firing market-watcher-eod falls through to the generic offhours cycle and loses eod.md's ledger + signal-file deliverable that Chef's 08:37Z dish consumes) is already decomposed HERE as T6 (+ optional doc-only T7) against brief section 5, and section 5's fix is the correct root-cause one: route by the slot= already sent, wall-clock table as no-slot fallback only. Minting a second row would split one root cause (a receiving flow discarding its dispatched identity and re-deriving from ambient clock) across two owners — the same defect shape as section 4.3, same dispatcher, same tick. I also endorse architect's refusal to flip match-slots.md Step 4b from WARN to BLOCK: the dispatcher cannot distinguish a legitimate two-dish tick from this incident without leaking market-domain knowledge into a generic scheduler, and blocking would break the documented intentional case. SEQUENCING INSTRUCTION FOR PM — T6 GOES FIRST, ahead of T1-T5. Three reasons: (a) T6 is the only strand that is market-facing DATA LOSS rather than detection latency — a lost eod.md deliverable is a missing artifact a downstream Chef dish depends on, strictly worse than an alert arriving ~20min late; (b) brief section 9 already records T6/T7 as having NO dependency on T1-T5 and being separately shippable, so there is no cost to promoting it; (c) T3 is the one strand that touches apps/mcp-server/ and must be sequenced behind the live qa full-suite run, so T1-T5 cannot complete promptly anyway — T6 is doc-only and unblocked right now. Parallelise T6 against T1/T2/T5 if two developers are available.

backlog.title: Add a real updated_at audit column to prediction_claims, maintained on every write, surfaced per-row on the Du bao AI page so a reader can tell at a glance whether a prediction was actually refreshed
backlog.root_cause: Direct user demand: 'each prediction need add update at time for easy recheck is update or not'. VERIFIED ABSENT end-to-end. The store row type PredictionClaimRow (predictionClaimStore.ts:60, mapRow ~:110) exposes exactly: id, stock, agent_id, claim_text, direction, target_price, resolution_date, confidence, resolution_outcome, actual_price, brier_score, creation_price, is_excluded, created_at, resolved_at — no updated_at. The serve DTO (predictionClaimsHandler.ts) and the page type (dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx:82-83) carry only createdAt and resolvedAt. PO DECISION — ADD A REAL COLUMN, do not repurpose an existing timestamp. Reasoning: (1) resolvedAt is the closest existing candidate but it is NULL for all 5 pending rows in live data, which is exactly the population the user wants to recheck — surfacing it would answer 'was this updated?' with a blank for every row the question is actually about; (2) createdAt answers a different question (when minted) and by construction never moves; (3) FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT deliverable (c) and FIX-PREDCLAIM-BACKFILL-NULL-CREATIONPRICE both introduce a genuine THIRD mutation class — post-creation edits to a claim that are neither creation nor resolution — after which no existing timestamp can represent 'last touched' at all; (4) the backfill will rewrite historical rows, and without an audit column there is no way for a reader to distinguish a backfilled row from an untouched one, which is precisely the recheck affordance being asked for.
backlog.deliverable: (a) mcp-server: add updated_at to prediction_claims using the ESTABLISHED idempotent pattern already in schema-system.ts:209-212 (try { db.exec('ALTER TABLE prediction_claims ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT') } catch {}) — same shape as the creation_price and is_excluded columns added before it. Do not introduce a new migration mechanism for one column. (b) Maintain it on EVERY write path with no exceptions: insertPredictionClaim sets updated_at = created_at; resolveClaim and excludeClaim set it to now; the backfill script sets it; any future partial-update helper sets it. Stamping must live inside the store functions, not at call sites — a call-site convention is exactly the kind of thing the next new call site skips. Use real UTC from the runtime, never a hand-formed string (feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future.md). (c) Backfill existing rows: updated_at = COALESCE(resolved_at, created_at), which is truthful for every row under the current two-event lifecycle. (d) Extend the serve DTO in predictionClaimsHandler.ts with updatedAt, passing through as null where genuinely unset — never coerced, matching the existing 'all nullable columns pass through as null' rule in mapClaimRow. (e) frontend: render it per claim on dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx as 'Cap nhat luc', clearly distinct from the creation date, and legible for pending rows. (f) Fold updated_at into the Zod contract from FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT as a REQUIRED field on write once the column exists.
backlog.acceptance: Every one of the 17 live claims returns a non-null updatedAt through the LIVE served endpoint after backfill. A claim mutated by the backfill script shows an updatedAt strictly later than its createdAt; an untouched historical claim shows updatedAt equal to its resolved_at or created_at. Resolving a pending claim advances its updatedAt within the same tick. The value is visible per row on the rendered page. All timestamps are runtime-generated UTC — no hand-typed ISO strings anywhere in the change.
backlog.note: zone=multi because the change spans apps/mcp-server/ (column + store stamping + DTO) and apps/frontend/ (render) — architect splits per the precedent set by FIX-PRED-CLAIMS-EXCLUDED-SERVE-DISPLAY, which was minted zone=multi (commit c40f90062) and dispatched to dev-mcp-server + dev-frontend in parallel (commit b0a786690). Sequenced P2 behind the three P1 rows: an updated_at on a claim that is still structurally unscoreable would tell the user when a worthless row was last touched. Fix the scoring first, then give the reader the recheck affordance.

  ACB ACV BDI CTG D2D DHG DLC GAS GVR HCM HSG HVN JSH MBB MWG NKG POW PPC REE SIS TCH VDC VNH VPB

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC — THE STALE FILE HAS LIVE CONSUMERS, VERIFIED AT SOURCE:
  1. CLAUDE.md instructs EVERY agent: "All structural data (services, agents, zones, channels, sources, watchlist) lives in docs/data/system-map.json. Query with jq — never hardcode values."   3. docs/agents/fb-market-poster/flow/main.md:200 derives its ticker set from `.project.watchlist[] | select(.active==true)` — a PUBLIC-FACING publisher operating on 33 of 58.
  4. apps/frontend/app/domain/market.ts:293 `WATCHLIST_STOCKS` is a COMPILE-TIME constant that mirrors this file (its own docstring says so: "Canonical watchlist — mirrors docs/data/system-map.json project.watchlist"), embedded at build time, never read from FS at runtime. po confirmed ACB/CTG/MBB/VPB/GAS/MWG appear NOWHERE in that file. backlog.title: system-auditor labelled `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB)` as WARN (rank 2) when its own tier-1 ladder maps `peak >97%` to CRITICAL (rank 3): `--severity` is a hand-authored literal with no binding to the measured value, so the dedup layer's escalation bypass (`new_rank > stored_rank`) is structurally unreachable for magnitude-driven conditions — and three improvised dedup_keys for one condition are currently the ONLY reason the 98.87% alert was not suppressed
backlog.root_cause: PREMISE CORRECTION — THE ESCALATING REPORT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE FINDING. The report to PO asserted: `its BUG Telegram was DEDUP-SKIPPED: dedup_key microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY had already been sent at 2026-07-28T14:30:09Z for the BENIGN 85% state ... the key minted while the condition was 'stable plateau, not a defect' now suppresses notification for '20 MiB from OOM and climbing' for the next 7 days.` PO checked the ledger and the signal rows instead of accepting this. It is wrong on the decisive fact. The 14:30:09Z entry did NOT carry the benign 85% state. Live signal_queue row sys-20260728T143010-6ec2, ts=2026-07-28T14:30:10Z, summary verbatim: `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB) — sustained after OCR workload`. The 14:30:09Z Telegram WAS the near-cap alert, and it WAS sent. What the 14:34:57Z emit hit was a 4-minute-later re-observation of the SAME state (98.84% vs 98.87%) under the SAME key — a textbook intra-cycle duplicate, and the router itself independently classified it as one on the row: `router_dedup_note: INTRA-CYCLE DUPLICATE of sys-20260728T143010-6ec2 (same sweep, same pdf-extractor condition, 98.84 vs 98.87). Triage as ONE.` THE DEDUP GATE BEHAVED CORRECTLY. No escalation was swallowed. Filing the reported bug as reported would have `fixed` the one component in the chain that worked. LEDGER TIMELINE, read from docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json at 2026-07-28T14:44Z, which is what the claim should have been checked against: `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:PDF-MEM-01` ts=2026-07-28T12:49:39Z sev=2 | `mem_pressure:pdf-extractor:A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` ts=2026-07-28T13:12:18Z sev=2 (this is the 85.54% plateau — archived signal row sys-20260728T131219-3fca, `pdf-extractor memory 85.54% of 2.5 GiB (2.138 GiB) — stable plateau`) | `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` ts=2026-07-28T14:30:09Z sev=2 (this is the 98.87%). Three keys, one condition, 101 minutes, all rank 2. DEFECT 1 — SEVERITY IS A HAND-AUTHORED LABEL, NOT A FUNCTION OF THE MEASUREMENT. scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh `_severity_rank()` collapses to `CRITICAL) echo 3 ;; HIGH|WARN) echo 2 ;; MED|INFO) echo 1 ;; *) echo 1`, ranking whatever string the calling agent typed into `--severity`. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md clause 5 states the policy the label was supposed to follow: `verdict=="ESCALATE", reason contains "OOMKilled=true" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "peak >97%" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "no reclamation dip" (>93% baseline case) -> WARN`. 98.87% is a `peak >97%` reading; the policy says CRITICAL (rank 3); the emit said WARN (rank 2). That ladder is prose in a markdown file, enforceable only by an LLM remembering to read it, and the tier-2 sweep that produced this emit does not read it at all — there is no tier2 flow file (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/ contains only main.md, tier1-probe.md, page-freshness.md). Nothing in the emit script can detect that `--severity WARN` contradicts a summary reading `98.87% of 2.5 GiB`. CONTROL CASE, SAME AUDITOR, SAME SWEEP, MINUTES APART — this is why the diagnosis is producer-side and not gate-side: sbv_fx DID escalate its label across the identical window, sys-20260728T142957-693e ts=14:29:57Z severity=HIGH `sbv_fx stale 43min (SLA 30min)` then sys-20260728T143455-6a8a ts=14:34:55Z severity=CRITICAL `sbv_fx stale 47min (check B-02-SBV)`. Rank 2 -> rank 3 on the same sweep, which would fire the bypass exactly as designed. One condition varied its label with the measurement; the other did not. The gate is common to both. DEFECT 2 — DEDUP-KEY NAMESPACE DRIFT, and it is currently MASKING defect 1. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:208 prescribes `"dedup_key":"microservice_degraded:<service_id>:<A-xx>"` with the worked example at :93 `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-20`; the canonical key here is `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30`. The call sites instead improvised `PDF-MEM-01`, `A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` under a `mem_pressure:` category prefix that appears in no documented category set, and `A-30-MEMORY`. THE CONSEQUENCE IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ROW: because `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` was a BRAND-NEW key at 14:30:09Z, `_ledger_prune_and_lookup` found no entry, took the `if [ -z "$LEDGER_ENTRY_TS" ]` branch, and SENT. Had the keys been correctly normalised, the 98.87% emit would have collided with the 13:12:18Z 85.54% entry under one canonical key, compared 2 > 2, evaluated false, and been SKIP-dedup'd — the exact failure the escalating report described, which has not happened yet but WOULD have. Key drift is accidentally load-bearing today. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT THAT FALLS OUT OF THAT: shipping the key-normalisation half of this row WITHOUT the severity-derivation half MANUFACTURES the reported bug. They must land together, or severity-derivation must land first. DEFECT 3 — PO RE-ESCALATION THRESHOLDS HAVE NO MACHINE-READABLE HOME, which is why PO learned of the crossing by hand. PO's 2026-07-28T13:12Z disposition on sys-20260728T131219-3fca reads `RESOLVED, no mint, MONITOR with a named re-escalation threshold (not a silent file-and-forget) ... RE-ESCALATE, and mint then, if ANY of: crosses 95% of cap, OOMKilled=true, or RestartCount climbs.` That text lives in a `po_disposition_20260728` string field on a signal row that has since been cold-evicted to docs/data/orch/archive/2026-07.json. No detector, no emit path, and no bridge reads that field. When 98.87% was measured at 14:30Z, every participant independently re-derived a severity from scratch and every one of them landed on WARN — the auditor's label, the router's corroboration (`SEVERITY: WARN is right — failure mode is OOM -> docker restart -> recovery, not permanent damage`), and the router's trend note (`No push notification sent — the router already spent one push today on a memory claim it had to retract, and a second for a self-recovering WARN would be noise`). Each judgement is individually defensible. None of them had access to the fact that PO had pre-committed 95%-of-cap as the mint trigger four hours earlier. NOT A DEFECT, CHECKED AND CLEARED — the anomaly-task-bridge did not fail: .claude/skills/anomaly-task-bridge/SKILL.md ATB-1 collects `to == "po"`, `status == "NEW"`, `row.ts < now() - 2h`, so at 14:47Z both rows (17 and 12 minutes old) are correctly grace-window-pending, not dropped; they would surface at ~16:30Z. The 2h gate is a deliberate transient-suppression design and this row does not propose changing it — but note that for a service with ~20 MiB of headroom, a 2h grace and a WARN label compose into a 2h blind spot, which is a further argument for defect 1 rather than for touching the gate.
backlog.deliverable: (a) MAKE SEVERITY DERIVABLE FROM THE MEASUREMENT, not merely assertable. Add a measured-value contract to `emit-audit-signal.sh` (exact shape is the implementer's call — e.g. `--metric-value <n> --metric-warn <n> --metric-critical <n>`, or a required `metric` object inside `--detail-json`) and rank from it when present. The derived rank must WIN over the free-text `--severity` string for bypass purposes. The literal `--severity` passthrough into the E-1/E-3 payloads must remain untouched — the file header marks it a deliberate separate design choice (`NEVER rewrites the literal --severity string passed to E-1/E-3 payloads ... EC-5's category_type passthrough rule is untouched by this`). (b) FAIL LOUD ON SELF-CONTRADICTION — cheap, high-value, and it alone would have caught this incident: when a supplied metric implies a rank strictly higher than the literal `--severity`, that is a call-site bug; surface it rather than silently ranking one of them. State in the close-out which order was used and show the interlock. (d) ADD A SAME-RANK MATERIAL-CHANGE BYPASS so a flat label cannot swallow a real deterioration even if (a) is bypassed by some future call site: when a metric is supplied and has moved past a named threshold since the ledger entry was written, send despite `new_rank == stored_rank`, under a distinct grep-able marker (e.g. `OK-threshold-crossing-bypass`) so it is auditable separately from `OK-escalation-bypass`. The ledger entry must persist enough of the metric for the NEXT comparison to be meaningful — a `sev`-only entry cannot express `it got worse at the same label`. (e) GIVE THE MAGNITUDE LADDER A HOME BOTH TIERS PASS THROUGH. The tier-1 clause-5 mapping (`OOMKilled=true` -> CRITICAL, `peak >97%` -> CRITICAL, `no reclamation dip >93%` -> WARN) is real policy currently enforceable only by an LLM reading a markdown file, and the tier-2 path does not read it. Encode it where both tiers pass, or state why not. This is also the natural home for a PO-declared re-escalation threshold (root_cause defect 3) — say explicitly whether that is in scope for this row or a follow-up, and do not leave it implied. (f) RECONCILE THE THREE EXISTING pdf-extractor LEDGER KEYS as part of the data migration, or state explicitly and with a reason why they are left to age out.

backlog.title: A-29 Cron Fire Check is UNEXECUTABLE as specified against its own named data source, so the implementing agent silently substituted a success-rate predicate that is structurally blind to a stopped cron - and the same defect silently drops systemAuditTier1/2/3, which is why the frozen auditor tier heartbeats were invisible
backlog.root_cause: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:174-182 specifies a FIRE-GAP predicate: call get_cron_health, iterate system-map.json microservices[0].crons, compute expected last-fire from the schedule expression, flag if gap > 2x cadence. FOUR independent reasons that predicate cannot execute as written, all PO-verified 2026-07-29T02:14-02:25Z. (1) WRONG PATH: the literal jq path .microservices[0].crons resolves to null; the real path is .project.microservices[0].crons (70 entries). Navigable by a human, but wrong as written. (2) SCHEDULE GRAMMAR IS NOT UNIFORM: of the 70 schedules only 32 are parseable 5-field cron expressions. The other 38 (54%) are prose: */15 min, */6h, 08:00 VN M-F, 23:00 VN Sunday, 1st monthly 06:00 VN, 19:00 UTC daily (02:00 VN), plus the two non-schedules startup and helper. Compute-expected-last-fire-from-schedule-expression is undefined for 54% of the inventory. (3) THE NAME JOIN IS BROKEN: get_cron_health returns 87 runtime jobs; system-map lists 70 crons; after aggressive normalization (lowercase, strip trailing Job, strip non-alphanumerics) only 48 join. 39 runtime jobs have NO system-map entry and therefore no schedule and are uncheckable by this predicate at all, including pollNews, pollNews_all_sources_dark, bondMaturityPoller, publicContracts, vnstockFundamentalsRefresh, deepFetchMain, deepFetchVps, schedulerWatchdog, restartCadenceAlert and diskUsageAlert. 22 system-map crons have NO runtime record. Runtime names carry a Job suffix and :variant suffixes (dataAuditJob:daily, marketScanJob:open) that the SSOT names do not; no mapping contract exists. (4) NO DATA SOURCE FOR CLAUDE-CODE CRONS: systemAuditTier1/2/3 ARE present in .project.microservices[0].crons with clean parseable schedules (*/30 * * * *, 0 */4 * * *, 0 2 * * *) but are ABSENT from get_cron_health because they are Claude Code CronCreate crons, not mcp-server node-cron jobs. They land in the 22-cron no-runtime-record bucket and are silently skipped. WHAT THE CYCLE ACTUALLY RAN INSTEAD: Cron Health (A-29): 127+ jobs tracked; all success_rate >=80%, majority >=99% - PASS. The strings success_rate and 80% appear NOWHERE in docs/agents/system-auditor/ (PO re-ran the grep and confirms zero hits) - the bar is agent-invented and re-chosen per cycle, so A-29 is also non-reproducible. WHY THE SUBSTITUTE IS WORSE THAN NOTHING: success_rate is a ratio over runs that HAPPENED. A cron that stopped firing retains its historical ratio forever - a dead cron reports ~99% and PASSES. The substitute cannot detect a stopped cron under any circumstance, which is precisely and only the failure mode A-29 exists to catch.
backlog.po_ruling: MINTED AS ONE ROW, NOT TWO. The router submitted the A-29 predicate substitution and the three frozen tier heartbeats as separate findings. They are one defect: reason (4) is the mechanism by which the first causes the second to be undetectable. Splitting them would produce two rows that each fix half a join. CORRECTION TO THE DISPATCH BRIEF, recorded because it changes the fix: the brief states Tier-2/Tier-3 are Claude Code CronCreate crons and NOT entries in system-map microservices[0].crons, and concludes even a correct A-29 would not cover them. That is factually wrong - all three ARE in the inventory with clean cron schedules. The gap is on the DATA-SOURCE side, not the inventory side, so the fix is NOT to add them to system-map; it is to give A-29 a second source for Claude-Code-side fire state and to make a join miss loud. THE GENERALIZABLE DEFECT IS SILENT-DROP-ON-JOIN-MISS: today, adding a cron to the SSOT creates the ILLUSION of coverage because an entry with no matching runtime record is skipped without a word. That is a coverage-reporting lie and is the part most likely to recur in other detectors. ROUTED TO ARCHITECT NOT DEVELOPER because none of the four blockers is an implementation bug - each needs a contract decision: a canonical schedule grammar or a normalization pass over 38 prose entries, a name-mapping contract between two divergent namespaces, a fire-state source for Claude-Code crons where NO tool exists today (structural gap, not laziness), and a fail-loud-on-join-miss policy. NOT BATCHED into the auditor detector-correctness epic minted alongside this row: that epic is a triage pass over 18 stalled rows, and A-29 has demonstrated LIVE blindness on a P1 detector - it must not queue behind a housekeeping sweep.

backlog.title: A-21 windowed crash detector drops any crash whose predecessor startup falls outside the fixed 8h fetch window - a crash after >8h uptime is structurally uncountable, so the detector is blindest exactly when a crash is most anomalous. Same defect in the mcp-server Telegram alert job it was ported from.
backlog.root_cause: The crash-vs-deploy discriminator classifies a startup by comparing it to its PREDECESSOR startup, but it only ever sees predecessors inside a FIXED lookback of 2x the alert window (8h), while the gap between startups is unbounded. Both implementations share it. (a) docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:119 fetches mcpServerStartup rows >= datetime('now','-8 hours'), :120 sets the 4h alert cutoff, :122 loops `for (let i=1;i<rows.length;i++)` comparing rows[i] to rows[i-1]. The earliest fetched row has no predecessor in the set and is never evaluated. (b) apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/restartCadenceAlertJob.ts is identical in effect: WINDOW_HOURS=4 (:96), fetch bound `-${WINDOW_HOURS * 2} hours` (:179), loop from i=0 (:200) with an explicit `if (i === 0) continue;` at :207 commented 'No predecessor -> cannot classify -> skip (conservative: not a crash)'. (c) The same query appears verbatim in the design brief at docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-23-auditor-a30-reclamation-gate-a21-windowed-restart.md:178-181, so this originates in the SPEC and was ported forward, not introduced by an implementer. THE INTENT WAS EXPLICIT AND THE GUARANTEE IS FALSE: :171-173 of the TS job states the 2x lookback exists 'to capture the startup that preceded the oldest in-window startup (needed to classify the first row)'. A fixed 2x extension only guarantees that predecessor when the inter-startup gap is short. Formally: for an in-window startup T (T >= now-4h) with predecessor P, P is fetched only if P >= now-8h; if the gap T-P exceeds 8h then P < T-8h <= now-8h and P is ALWAYS dropped. So the discriminator can only classify crashes that follow LESS THAN 8h of uptime - i.e. it works during an already-established fast crash loop and fails on the first crash after any stable period. The conservative skip is not conservative: it is a silent false negative on the highest-signal event.

MEASURED on the host bind-mount, read-only: data/live/lancedb totals 785 MiB for a corpus of ~11243 rows (index_size measured 05:20Z on RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND). rag_entries.lance/data holds 3137 fragment files totalling 596 MiB — roughly one fragment per 3-4 rows, and each POST /index lands a NEW ~6.7-6.9 KiB fragment (the two newest, 11:29Z, correspond exactly to the two index calls logged at 11:29:50.44 and 11:29:51.09). _versions holds 3091 manifests / 32 MiB and _transactions another 3091 files / 12 MiB, so version metadata alone is 44 MiB and grows one pair per write. _indices is 145 MiB across 745 files. backlog.root_cause: PO OBSERVED BEFORE-AND-AFTER STATES, NOT THE WRITE ITSELF — the inference boundary is stated explicitly below. MEASURED: at 2026-07-29T10:41Z the working-tree docs/data/orch/orch-state.json contained 133 .signal_queue.rows[], including sys-20260729T103337-13e5 and sys-20260729T103338-7f95 (both type=data_stale, severity=WARN, to=po, status=NEW, summary 'sbv_fx stale 32min (check B-12)'). At 2026-07-29T10:52Z both were absent, .signal_queue.rows[] was 132, and both were absent from .signal_queue.archive[] as well — so they were not triaged, not archived, not cold-evicted-with-retention. They are absent from commit 3e257beba (authored 12:47:15 +0200 = 10:47:15Z, 'drain 2026-07-29T10:37Z tick'), whose committed file carries 131 rows — byte-identical signal_queue.rows[] id-set to its own parent 3e257beba~1 (comm -13/-23 both empty, i.e. that commit added and removed NOTHING from signal_queue). 131 committed + the 2 uncommitted rows = the 133 PO read. So a peer serialized a 131-row full-document baseline over a 133-row working tree and committed it, silently discarding two rows that had never been committed. THE WRITE GATE CANNOT CATCH THIS AND IS NOT SUPPOSED TO: scripts/orch-apply.sh delegates to scripts/orch-conservation-check.mjs, whose FLOOR_RATIO defaults to 0.5 (line 64) and which only flags when a candidate total drops BELOW HALF of live (line 158). 131/133 = 98.5%, so a 2-row loss passes trivially. Its header comment is explicit that this is a 'whole-board MAGNITUDE-RATIO design, NOT naive per-lane never-decrease', deliberately chosen 'against the naive no-lane-may-ever-decrease wording'. That design decision is defensible for bulk eviction and is NOT the thing to revert — but it means NOTHING in the system currently protects an individual untriaged signal_queue row from being dropped by a stale-baseline write.

backlog.not_the_signal_quality_audit_defect: IMPORTANT — this missed cron run is NOT the cause of the separate signal_quality_audit SLA-breach defect fixed by FIX-SLA-SIGNALQUALITYAUDIT-MONTHLY-CADENCE-MISCLASSIFIED-48H. backlog.title: 34 of 40 sprint ids referenced by task rows / sprint_goal have NO active_sprints[] or closed_sprints[] object — PO sign-off, cold-eviction and decision-journal archival are all structurally unreachable for them
backlog.desc:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-07-30T09:3xZ on docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, not inferred. Every `.task_board.<lane>[].sprint` value and every `.sprint_goal.entries[].sprint_id` was resolved against the union of `.task_board.active_sprints[].id` (8 ids) and `.task_board.closed_sprints[].id` (19 ids) plus the cold-archive closed-id universe (`docs/data/orch/archive/*.json`: .closed_sprints[].id, .closed_sprint_goals sprint ids, [.done_tasks[].sprint]). Result: 40 distinct referenced sprint ids, of which 34 resolve to NOTHING. Top offenders by reference count: TOKEN-ECONOMY-AUDIT (28 refs), ULTRACODE-AUDIT-FIXALL (24), COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP (11), FLOW-PRICE-ALPHA-LOOP (9). Only 6 ids resolve (MARKET-INDICATOR-DEPTH-P0, COWORK-RELIABILITY, BCTC-ANALYTICS-LAYER, FLEET-HOST-SAFETY, OHLCV-UNIT-CONTAM-WHOLEROW-LT1000, VN-MACRO-TOOLING).

THREE CONSEQUENCES, each verified against the executable and not the prose:
(1) PO SIGN-OFF IS IMPOSSIBLE for those 34. `docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:126` makes the Approve path MUST-set `active_sprints[sprint_id].status = "DONE"`. There is no such key to set, so the canonical sign-off write cannot be performed at all — the failure mode is not a wrong token (the documented hazard) but a missing object.
(2) DECISION-JOURNAL ARCHIVAL IS UNREACHABLE. `scripts/agents-flow/decision-journal-archive.sh` selects STATUS-based (header :9 'Selection is STATUS-based (closed sprint id vs still-active), NOT mtime-based'), building a closed-id universe (:120-127) and an active-id set (:116) and longest-prefix-matching each `sprint-<id>[-<agent>].md`. An id in NEITHER set is a THIRD, unhandled state: it is silently skipped forever, on both stdin and --all backfill paths. Live cost: `docs/agent-memory/decisions/` holds 513 sprint-*.md journals / 5.5MB, and the largest over-cap files all belong to dangling ids — sprint-CI-RED-RECONCILE-po.md 331592B (9.2x the 36000B cap), sprint-SYSTEMIC-REMAKE-P1-qa.md 225553B, sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-developer.md 128381B.
(3) THE BREACH DETECTOR THEREFORE NEVER CONVERGES. context-bloat-backstop re-emits on whichever journal a live agent happens to write: 138 context-bloat signals sit in docs/signals/processed/, ~34 of them for the 3 COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP journals alone over 07-25..07-30, every one marked processed with the condition untouched. Same never-converging-detector family as FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNER-LINE-ONLY-SETPOINT-BYTE-CAP-NEVER-CONVERGES.

ORIGIN: triaged from the 2026-07-30T09:07Z drain's context_bloat_breach on sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-architect.md (46429B vs 36000B cap, 191L/600L — byte-axis only). That signal was DEFERRED as a prune (live sprint, file uncommitted-modified at triage time, content is load-bearing design rationale) — but the standard 'defer until the sprint closes' disposition is a FALSE PREMISE here: COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP exists only as `.sprint_goal.entries[15].sprint_id` plus 11 task-row refs (TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2 DONE, -3/-4/-5/-10 READY, -6..-9 BACKLOG), so it can never close and the deferral can never expire.

SUPERVISED + PLAN_ONLY ON PURPOSE — the naive fix bricks the board, and this was measured, not guessed. The obvious fix is a referential-integrity rule in `scripts/orch-validate.mjs` (Stage 1 already does dangling-ref checks and is the validator every `scripts/orch-apply.sh` write must pass). Arming it fail-loud TODAY rejects EVERY subsequent board write, because 34 ids are already dangling. Sequencing is therefore mandatory, and is the design question for architect:
AC-1 RECONCILE FIRST: decide per dangling id whether it is genuinely live (register an `active_sprints[]` object), genuinely finished (register in `closed_sprints[]` so the journal archiver can sweep it), or never was a sprint (rename/strip the `.sprint` field). 'BACKLOG' appearing as a 5-ref sprint id is evidence the field is also being used as a non-sprint sentinel — classify that separately.
AC-2 THEN arm the guard, WARN-first with an env-var escalation to reject, mirroring the notebook-immutability gate disposition (`.claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md` AC-2a: GIT_NOTEBOOK_IMMUTABILITY_MODE defaults to warn). Do not arm reject until a corpus replay reads 0.
AC-3 the guard must cover BOTH reference planes (`task_board.*[].sprint` and `sprint_goal.entries[].sprint_id`) — a check on one plane leaves the other silently broken.
AC-4 give `decision-journal-archive.sh` an explicit third-state branch: an id in neither set must FAIL LOUD (or emit one deduped signal), never be silently skipped. Today's silent skip is what made a 5.5MB/513-file accumulation invisible.
AC-5 verification gate is timestamped and measured, not prose: re-run the resolver and show `dangling == 0`, and show `decision-journal-archive.sh --all` moving a previously-unreachable journal, with a before/after byte count.
AC-6 do NOT fix this by prune/split of any live journal — that is the deferred, separate action and it races live editors (feedback_ctxbloat_breach_on_live_sprint_file_defer).

backlog.status_note:
AC — READ THE AMPLIFICATION CAUTION FIRST, IT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS FIX.

(0) DO NOT 'FIX' THE GUARD RELEASE. drain-esc-dispatch.md TERMINAL-EXIT (:116-117) and Step 5 (:140) both call task_release(guard_key) on EVERY exit path, including the GATE-B known-root path. Observation says that release is currently a NO-OP: bctc-analyst c133 found the guard still held at 21:09Z with expiry 21:10:43Z, i.e. it survived its full 86400s TTL from the 07-29T21:10:43Z claim, across ~8 intervening dev-team drain ticks. Candidate mechanism (UNPROVEN, do not assume): the release passes only {task_id}, no owner_agent, while the claim was made by bctc-analyst — the known released:0-orphan class in feedback_task_release_owner_agent_mismatch_orphans_lock. THE POINT: if you 'repair' that release, the guard frees on the very next drain and the loop goes from 1 re-emit/day to 4 re-emits/day. The broken release is currently the ONLY thing bounding this loop. Any fix must make suppression correct BEFORE, or in the same change as, making the release work.

(1) STATE WHICH PLANE YOU ARE FIXING. Two coherent designs, pick one explicitly and say why: (a) CONSUMER-EXTENDS — on a GATE-B Tier 1 known-root hit, re-claim/extend guard_key with a long TTL instead of releasing it, so the producer stays suppressed for as long as the owning board row is open. Cheap, needs no producer change, and works with bctc-analyst's no-Bash constraint. (b) PRODUCER-ASKS — give the producer an MCP-tool-shaped known-root query it CAN call without Bash. More correct, more surface. A third option — widening the producer's TTL — is NOT acceptable: it re-tunes a constant instead of owning the condition, the same anti-pattern called out in FIX-SIGNALQUALITYAUDIT-WRITE-GATE-UNREACHABLE-BY-EMITTER-CONTRACT.

(2) DO NOT SUPPRESS GENUINE CHANGE. Whatever suppresses must re-open when the underlying finding actually changes. Negative control, mandatory: with a known-root row open, an escalation carrying a DIFFERENT refined_at or a DIFFERENT low-confidence unit set must still emit. Suppressing on ticker+trigger_id alone would silently swallow a real regression on the same ticker.

(3) FIX THE FALSIFIED BOARD CLAIM. REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026's title says minting it stops the 24h re-escalation. Correct it as part of this row, or the next PO re-derives this from scratch for the 6th time.

(4) BIDIRECTIONAL PROOF, on the live signal path, not a fixture. Show (i) zero new docs/signals/bctc-analyst-*.json esc-deep-dive-request for esc-deepdive:FPT:Q1-2026:ESC-5 across at least 2 consecutive bctc-analyst cycles while REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026 stays open, AND (ii) emission still occurs once that row reaches a TERMINAL_SET status or the finding's inputs change. 'The signal stopped' alone is not proof — it is also what a dead emitter looks like.

(5) Regression test pinning the chosen design, so this cannot revert to board-blind re-emission.

backlog.title: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:30 declares zone MUST be one of {apps/<service>/, multi, cross-service/} and that a missing zone gets the batch rejected — but 256/659 open board rows (38.8%) carry a zone outside that enum and 3 carry none, so the stated contract is not the one the board actually runs on
backlog.desc:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-01T04:36Z across the five open lanes (backlog/ready/in_progress/review/qa), not sampled: open_rows=659, conforming=400, null_zone=3, NON-CONFORMING=256 (38.8%). Conformance predicate used is main.md:30's own enum, verbatim: zone == "multi" or zone == "cross-service/" or zone matches ^apps/[a-z0-9-]+/$.

THREE DISTINCT DEFECT CLASSES INSIDE THE 256 — they need different remedies and should not be lumped:
(A) NEAR-MISS PUNCTUATION on an otherwise valid zone — `apps/mcp-server` (14 rows, no trailing slash) alongside a conforming `apps/mcp-server/` (141 rows); also `apps/technical-analysis` (5), `apps/stock-price` (4), `apps/macro-indicators` (4), `apps/pdf-extractor` (3), `apps/vps-scripts` (1), and `cross-service` (6, no slash) beside `cross-service/`. This is the dangerous class: any consumer doing string equality or a prefix test anchored on the trailing slash silently splits one zone into two populations, and the split is invisible because both spellings look right at a glance.
(B) BARE SERVICE NAME, prefix missing entirely — `mcp-server` (9), `dev-mcp-server` (7), `stock-price` (6), `alert-engine` (5), `kinh-dich-service` (4), `api-gateway` (3), `frontend` (3), `news-fetch` (3), `pdf-extractor` (3), `technical-analysis` (3), `rag-service` (2), `macro-indicators` (1).
(C) PATH-SHAPED PSEUDO-ZONES that are not services at all — `docs/agents/` (36), `docs/agents/dev-team/flow/` (14), `docs/agents/system-auditor/` (10), `scripts/` (9), `.claude/skills/` (8), plus a long tail of one-off doc paths, and sub-service pseudo-zones `mcp-server-domain`/`-infra`/`-application`/`-interface`/`-scheduler` (6/5/4/3/2). A handful are not even single values — `apps/mcp-server/ + flow-docs/`, `vps-scripts + apps/mcp-server (fetch-pipeline design)`, `docs/data/system-map.json + docs/architecture-briefs`, `agent-father / docs/data/cowork-schedule.json`.

WHY THIS IS A REAL CONTRACT PROBLEM AND NOT COSMETIC BOOKKEEPING: main.md:30 states 'dev-team Step 3 reads this field; missing zone = batch rejected back to PO'. If that were enforced as written, 259 of 659 open rows could not be dispatched. They evidently are being dispatched, so either the consumer is more permissive than the contract (the contract is wrong and should be widened + normalised) or the consumer is quietly mis-routing class (A)/(B) rows (the rows are wrong and must be normalised). Both are actionable; which one is true is the first thing to determine, and it must be determined by reading dev-team Step 3's actual zone handling, not by assuming.

CLASS (C) IS THE DESIGN QUESTION, not a typo sweep: agent-flow and skill work is a genuine, high-volume category of task on this board that the three-value enum has no slot for. backlog.title: windowPartitioner maxWindowPages truncation creates a headless tail window that continuation-stitch.md's contract never anticipated -- resolveColumnLayout() defaults to code-first, silently swapping code/label on label-first (bank) continuation tables split by the cap
backlog.root_cause: windowPartitioner.ts's maxWindowPages cap (windowPartitioner.ts:92-101) does NOT fold an over-cap continuation table into its current window -- it starts a brand-new window (i=j) at the very next page, which is itself a mid-table continuation page with no header of its own (that's why it matched CONTINUATION_MARKER in the first place). This 'tail window' gets page_type='continuation' (getBctcPendingRefineTool.ts:319-335) and is dispatched to the SAME sub-flow as a genuine first-page window (docs/agents/refine_bctc_md/flow/continuation-stitch.md), whose contract (Steps 2-3) unconditionally treats the window's first page as carrying the table's real header -- a rule that was never updated to anticipate a truncation-created headless tail. Downstream, refinedMarkdownParser.ts::resolveColumnLayout() (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:386-393) decides code-first vs label-first column order by reading the CAPTURED header row's own cell text, but headerCells is a per-call local re-initialized to null on every parseRefinedMarkdown invocation (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:439) -- unlike statement_section, which IS explicitly threaded window-to-window via initialSection/finalSection (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:404-419, finalizeBctcRefine.ts:162,174-175). A tail window with no header of its own (the expected shape) falls back to the DEFAULT code-first layout (refinedMarkdownParser.ts:387,391), silently swapping code<->label for every 4-column row of a label-first (bank Meu B02a/TCTDHN) continuation table whose true header only existed in the truncated head window. This corrupts (not drops) code/label text; value_current/value_prior are read from the same cell indices in both layouts so numeric values are unaffected. bctcScalarAggregator.ts resolves headline scalars (total_assets, equity_total, net_revenue, ...) via LABEL-CANONICAL matching preferred over code (bctcScalarAggregator.ts:20-21,396-399) and also uses row code/label shape for isBankFormFromRows bank-vs-corporate detection -- a swap can silently degrade or null the headline figures this pipeline exists to produce, with no error and no gate that catches it (checkSectionCompleteness/BEQ-7 only checks statement_section PRESENCE, never code/label correctness -- bctcSectionCompleteness.ts:27-60). Same root mechanism as the already-shipped FIX-BCTC-BANK-BS-COLUMN-ORDER (single-window, no-captured-header case) -- that fix added within-window header capture but never cross-window threading, so the maxWindowPages truncation path re-opens the identical hazard through a side door the original fix did not anticipate. Live-confirmed trigger frequency: 5 truncation WARNs within the same second of a single run (docs/agent-memory/health/team-tool-recheck-2026-06-21-1605.md:195-196) -- not a theoretical edge case. NOT independently reproduced within the spike's 120-min timebox: an actual corrupted bctc_table_rows row instance from a live truncation-tail window (would need pulling a real bctc_refined_units row past a report's first truncated unit_id and diffing against a known label-first bank filing).
backlog.deliverable: Architect decision (not a blind copy-paste) among 3 non-exclusive candidate mitigations, then implement the chosen combination: (1) raise maxWindowPages default / make it PDF-adaptive so real long bank continuation tables stop splitting; (2) thread a headerCells/column-layout hint forward across windows in parseDoneUnitsToRows the same way carrySection/statement_section already is, so a headless tail window inherits the correct layout from its head window; (3) have windowPartitioner mark truncation-tail windows explicitly (make the already-claimed but nonexistent truncated_continuation flag real -- windowPartitioner.ts:50 docstring vs 0 grep hits) so continuation-stitch.md's live agent-flow contract can fetch the head window's page-N header context on demand instead of silently assuming it is absent. Whichever combination is chosen, add a regression fixture that exercises the actual >maxWindowPages split-across-two-windows path end to end (partition -> refine markdown -> finalize) with a label-first (bank-form) 4+-column continuation table -- no existing test does this (grep -rn maxWindowPages apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__ only covers inputs that never exceed the cap: AR-refined-units-idempotency.test.ts:346,369; FIX-REFINE-WINDOW-DB-PAGELIST.test.ts:128 tests a different bug -- DB-driven page-list construction, not the continuation cap).
backlog.acceptance: A synthetic label-first (bank Meu B02a/TCTDHN-shaped) continuation table spanning > maxWindowPages pages, run through partitionIntoWindows -> parseRefinedMarkdown (per-window, threading whatever new cross-window state the chosen fix adds) -> finalizeBctcRefine's parseDoneUnitsToRows, produces rows in the tail window with code/label in the CORRECT (non-swapped) order -- not just non-empty. Negative control: an existing code-first (corporate) continuation table fixture is unaffected (0-diff). The health-recheck WARN's severity/wording is corrected in the SAME change (or a follow-up doc-only PR) to stop attributing it to intelligence-cycle/news signal-drop -- see SPIKE-BCTC-REFINE-MAXWINDOW-TRUNCATION Finding 0.

backlog.title: Live /api/cron-status serves a stale 4-file layer_b view — process-lifetime memo with no TTL cached the deleted-cron-docs window
backlog.source: PO triage 2026-08-05 — collateral of the cron-doc deletion window 06:20-07:06Z
backlog.root_cause: docker-compose.yml:26 bind-mounts ./.claude/commands/crons into mcp-server read-only at /app/.claude/commands/crons, and layerBCronRegistry.ts parses it to build the Layer-B half of GET /api/cron-status (the dashboard Cron Recheck Table). getLayerBCronRows() memoizes into a module-level `_cachedRows` (layerBCronRegistry.ts:137-152) that is populated once and has NO TTL and NO invalidation — only the test-only reset hook clears it. Between ~06:20Z and 07:06Z on 2026-08-05, 12 of the 16 cron docs plus .claude/commands/dev-team.md were deleted from the working tree; the memo was filled during that window. PO restored all 13 files from HEAD at 07:06Z and the container now sees 16 files (docker exec ls confirms), but the API still returns layer_b length 7 — the stale memo survives the file restore.
backlog.evidence: Before restore: docker exec ls /app/.claude/commands/crons -> 4 files; curl /api/cron-status -> layer_b length 7 (cron-cowork-team, cron-dev-team, cron-market-watcher#1..#3, cron-orch-sentinel#1..#2). After restore: docker exec ls -> 16 files; curl -> STILL 7. Cache confirmed, not a file problem. Note apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__/layerBCronRegistry.test.ts AC-12 and cronStatusHandler.test.ts AC-12 both assert '13 live files' against the real tree — those would have gone RED during the deletion window, and the hardcoded 13 is itself a NO-HARDCODE violation worth folding in.
ac: AC-1 ops: restart ONLY vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1 to flush the memo, then curl /api/cron-status and assert layer_b length matches the parse of all 16 files. Single-service restart per memory feedback_rebuild_after_dev_change — never `docker compose down && up`, which kills peers. Do it in a quiet window: 4 live CLI agent sessions currently route every gateway call through this container.

AC-2 Decide whether a process-lifetime memo over a bind-mounted doc dir is the right design at all. It means any cron-doc edit is invisible to the dashboard until the next container restart, which silently backdates the operator's view. A cheap mtime check or a short TTL would close it; if the memo is kept deliberately, say so in the handler doc so the next person does not read a stale table as ground truth.

AC-3 Replace the hardcoded '13 live files' expectation in both AC-12 tests with a count derived from the directory (or from system-map.json), so the suite tracks the real fleet instead of pinning a number that was already wrong twice.

backlog.title: 35% of dispatchable rows (147/415) carry a zone token dev-team Step 3 does not accept — a likely systemic cause of the board's chronic dispatch starvation
backlog.source: PO self-detection, triage tick 2026-08-06T07:07Z — generalised from a single concrete instance found while folding a duplicate mint
backlog.root_cause: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md Role in dev-team flow states: 'Every FIX/SPRINT-* entry MUST carry zone: - one of apps/<service>/ (single zone), multi (architect must split), or cross-service/ (genuine root/scripts work). dev-team Step 3 reads this field; missing zone = batch rejected back to PO.' Nothing enforces this at MINT time, so rows have accumulated free-text zones for months. Live count across the two dispatchable lanes (backlog[]+ready[], n=415): 147 rows (35.4%) carry a token that is neither apps/*-prefixed, nor 'multi', nor 'cross-service/'.
backlog.evidence: PO measured live this tick from the hot file. Off-contract tokens by volume: docs/agents/ (29), docs/agents/dev-team/flow/ (11), docs/agents/system-auditor/ (10), apps/mcp-server WITHOUT trailing slash (8), .claude/skills/ (7), mcp-server bare (7), scripts/ (7), scripts/agents-flow/ (5), cross-service WITHOUT trailing slash (5), apps/technical-analysis no-slash (5), apps/macro-indicators no-slash (4), apps/stock-price no-slash (4), UNSET (3), docs/ (3), plus a long tail. Two distinct defect classes are mixed here: (a) genuinely off-contract namespaces (docs/agents/, .claude/skills/, scripts/) and (b) trailing-slash/format drift on otherwise-valid apps/* tokens — (b) may or may not be tolerated depending on the matcher and MUST be resolved by reading the matcher, not assumed.
backlog.concrete_instance: TE-T05 (P1, zone '.claude/skills/') was flagged by the manual-dispatch sweep on 2026-08-01T03:55:50Z and STILL had not been dispatched when the same sweep re-admitted it 2026-08-06T07:23Z under its staleness window — ~4 days, zero dispatches. Independently, the peer po's mint of FIX-DEVTEAM-PIPELINE-RESUME-TERMINAL-LANE-BLIND this same tick carried zone 'docs/agents/' and was corrected to 'cross-service/' during dedup folding specifically because it would otherwise have bounced. Two instances in one tick is what generalised this from a one-row typo to a board-wide hypothesis.
ac: AC-1 READ THE MATCHER FIRST, measure second. Locate the actual code/jq predicate dev-team Step 3 uses to read zone and determine EXACTLY which of the 147 rows it rejects, tolerates, or silently mis-routes. The 35% figure is an upper bound derived from the DOCUMENTED contract, not from the matcher - it must be re-derived from the implementation before any row is rewritten. Report the true rejected/tolerated split for both defect classes (a) off-contract namespace and (b) trailing-slash drift.

AC-2 Do NOT mass-rewrite zones as the first action. Confirm the causal claim first: if off-contract zones truly block dispatch, then rows carrying them should show a materially lower dispatch rate than rows with valid tokens. Measure that on the existing board before changing any data - the hypothesis is plausible and untested, and this row must not become a 147-row blind edit.

AC-3 If AC-2 confirms causation: mint a normalisation pass mapping each off-contract token to a canonical one by ARTIFACT CLASS, reusing the existing PO ARTIFACT-CLASS ROUTING RULING 2026-07-21 verbatim (instruction-prose an agent loads and executes -> agent-father; executable code under apps/**, scripts/** -> zone-matched dev-* or developer). AC-4 Add a MINT-TIME guard so this cannot re-accumulate: validate the zone token in scripts/orch-validate.mjs / orchStateSchema.ts so an off-contract zone fails at scripts/orch-apply.sh, the same way LANE_ALLOWED_STATUSES already fails an un-canonical status token. Opt-IN allowlist for any deliberate exception, never opt-out (feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist).

AC-5 Negative control: a row with a valid zone (apps/mcp-server/, multi, cross-service/) must still dispatch exactly as today, and the new validator must not reject any row currently dispatching successfully. Run the guard against the full live board BEFORE arming it and report the would-reject count.

AC-6 If AC-2 REFUTES the causal claim (off-contract zones dispatch fine), say so explicitly and close this row as a docs-vs-implementation contract drift instead: the main.md prose is then wrong and must be corrected to match the matcher, which is a real but much smaller fix.

backlog.title: backupDatabase() overwrites the ONLY market.db backup with an unconditional copy and zero pre-copy integrity check — one rotation over an already-corrupting file destroys the last known-good state. Add a quick_check gate + 3-generation rotation.
backlog.created_by: po (triage tick 2026-08-06T12:2xZ — routed from ops's P2 flag in the 2026-08-06 incident report)
backlog.root_cause: backupDatabase() performs an unconditional `Bun.write(dst, src)` onto a single rotating market.db.backup file, with no integrity check on the SOURCE before copying and no generational history. A rotation that happens to run while the live DB is already corrupting silently overwrites the last clean snapshot with a corrupt one. Flagged as §5.4 of the 2026-07-30 architecture brief and re-flagged by ops in the 2026-08-06 incident report; never scoped as a task until now.
backlog.evidence: Near-miss already realised once: the 2026-07-30 incident required a `.recover` salvage precisely because the only backup had already been overwritten (see market.db.impoverished-backup-2026-07-30T08:33:51Z, 16.9MB — a salvage remnant of a 400MB DB). The 2026-08-06 recovery got lucky in the other direction: market.db.backup happened to be clean (quick_check=ok) so a straight restore worked. Luck is the current control.
backlog.impact: P2 — secondary. It did not cause any of the 5 corruptions and did not block this recovery, but it is the difference between 'restore from backup' (2026-08-06, ~6.4h of regenerable telemetry lost) and 'salvage a 400MB DB down to 17MB' (2026-07-30). Given the corruption class is demonstrably recurrent, the backup path is the last line of defence and is currently ungated. PO keeps this at P2 rather than promoting it: it reduces blast radius but does not reduce recurrence, and the two P0 rows do. Deliberately NOT bundled into either P0 — different zone, different owner, and folding a defence-in-depth item into an active-incident fix is how P0s slip.
acceptance: AC-1 pre-copy gate: run a cheap integrity check (PRAGMA quick_check) on the SOURCE before any overwrite. Source fails -> ABORT the rotation, keep the existing backup, and alert the BUG channel. Never overwrite a good backup with a bad source.
AC-2 generational rotation: keep at least 3 generations (market.db.backup.0/.1/.2) instead of one, so a single bad cycle cannot erase all known-good state even if AC-1's check is somehow bypassed.

AC-3 the abort path must be loud, not silent — a backup that silently stops rotating is indistinguishable from one that is working, which is the same unarmed-observer failure as FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED. Emit on both success (with generation + source verdict) and abort.
AC-4 prove it: fixture test with a deliberately corrupted source proving the rotation ABORTS and the prior generation survives byte-identical.
backlog.verification_gate: Fixture run with a corrupt source: rotation aborts, prior generation byte-identical, BUG alert emitted.
backlog.note: Housekeeping observed while triaging, NOT part of this row's scope: /app/data now holds ~14 market.db.* forensic artifacts (corrupt snapshots, pre-salvage copies, impoverished-backup) totalling well over 1.5GB on the same bind mount as the live DB. Prior ENOSPC history (project_enospc_blocker) makes that worth a janitor sweep with an explicit retention policy — route separately, do not absorb here.

backlog.title: dev-team-tick-preflight.sh DEFAULT_ROOT resolution is CWD-dependent through the apps/mcp-server/{docs,scripts} symlinks — wrong invocation cwd silently redirects git commit to a nested path and fails
backlog.why_this_row_exists: Live-reproduced this tick, not theoretical. dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:170-171 computes DEFAULT_ROOT via `cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd` — bash's cd/pwd are logical (symlink-preserving) by default. apps/mcp-server/docs and apps/mcp-server/scripts are both symlinks to the repo-root docs/ and scripts/ dirs. If the script is invoked (BASH_SOURCE relative) from a cwd under apps/mcp-server, dirname-walking two levels up lands on apps/mcp-server itself instead of the true repo root. Step 5.5's _step55_git_commit_evict then built its pathspec against apps/mcp-server/docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, and git refused it: "fatal: le chemin ... est au-dela d'un lien symbolique" (path is beyond a symbolic link) — the cold-evict write succeeded on disk (both paths resolve to the same physical file) but the commit step failed, leaving 2 files uncommitted in the working tree until manually caught and committed this tick (commit 4db659e30).
backlog.trigger_this_time: This session's Bash tool keeps one persistent shell across turns; an earlier unrelated turn left cwd at apps/mcp-server (via a bare `cd apps/mcp-server && ...` with no return-to-root), and the next dev-team cron tick's preflight inherited that stale cwd. Not yet confirmed whether any non-interactive/fresh-shell cron path can independently reach the same cwd, but the underlying resolution logic is wrong regardless of trigger: it silently produces a different ROOT depending on caller cwd, which a repo-root-anchored script never should.
backlog.scope: Make SCRIPT_DIR/DEFAULT_ROOT resolution symlink- and cwd-invariant, e.g. `cd -P "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P` (physical) instead of logical cd/pwd, so it always resolves through the symlink to the canonical repo root regardless of invocation cwd. Audit other scripts sharing the same `$SCRIPT_DIR/../..`-style idiom under scripts/agents-flow/ for the same fragility while in the zone.
backlog.acceptance: Script invoked from repo root, from apps/mcp-server, and from apps/mcp-server/scripts/agents-flow all resolve ROOT to the same canonical repo-root path (verify via `pwd -P` comparison in a test). Existing dev-team-tick-preflight.test.sh suite still green.
backlog.evidence: git commit failure text this tick: "fatal : le chemin '/Users/admin/Documents/Hung/__works__/__PROJET/__labo/VN-Market-Intelligence-MCP/apps/mcp-server/docs/data/orch/orch-state.json' est au-dela d'un lien symbolique"; ls -la apps/mcp-server/docs -> symlink to ../../docs; realpath of both the symlinked and canonical orch-state.json paths match (no content divergence, no data loss — recovered via manual commit 4db659e30).

backlog.title: deriveOrchApplyHelpers() in drain-signals.test.js only throws when it matches ZERO helpers, so PARTIAL regex drift (3 of 4 matched) silently reproduces the exact sandbox crash it was built to prevent
backlog.source: Residual bound recorded by router on FIX-DRAIN-TEST-HARNESS-ORCH-HELPER-COPY-LIST (router_residual_partial_drift_not_caught_20260721T2022, 'ROUTER DID NOT MINT'); minted by PO at that row's DONE_VERIFIED sign-off 2026-08-06T15:46Z so the bound survives the terminal lane move.
backlog.desc: MECHANISM (re-read at source 2026-08-06T15:45Z, still present): scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js:255-265 derives the sandbox helper-copy list by regex-scanning scripts/orch-apply.sh for /\$\{REPO_ROOT\}\/scripts\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(?:sh|mjs|js))/g. Its stale-regex guard at 261-263 throws ONLY when found.size === 0. So it catches TOTAL regex rot and is blind to PARTIAL drift: if orch-apply.sh later invokes a helper via $SCRIPT_DIR/, a bare relative path, an interpolated variable, or any other idiom, the derivation returns N-1 of N, the sandbox omits that one file, and orch-apply.sh inside the sandbox crashes at makeOrchRefHarness() exactly as it did before the parent fix — killing every assertion after the first harness block. NOT CURRENTLY BROKEN, and PO verified this twice: git log shows ZERO commits to scripts/orch-apply.sh since a5d079663 (predates the parent fix), and today's ground-truth scan finds exactly 3 live invocations (orch-validate.mjs L136, orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs L159, orch-conservation-check.mjs L179), every other scripts/ mention being a comment (L3,15,17,22,34,38,62,124,146,168). This row exists because the parent's AC-4 asked for the CLASS to be closed and the derivation closes only the dominant idiom.
acceptance: AC-1 Make the guard fail on PARTIAL drift, not only on zero matches: after deriving, independently scan orch-apply.sh's NON-COMMENT lines for any scripts/<name>.<sh|mjs|js> reference and throw if any such reference is absent from the derived set. The second scan must be deliberately broader/dumber than the first (it is the cross-check, not a second copy of the same regex) — a comment-stripping pass plus a loose scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(sh|mjs|js) match is sufficient. Comment lines MUST be excluded or the guard fires permanently on the 10 documentation mentions listed in desc.

AC-2 Prove BOTH polarities against fixtures, not by inspection: (a) a fixture orch-apply.sh that invokes a 4th helper via a non-matching idiom (e.g. $SCRIPT_DIR/orch-fake.mjs) MUST make the harness throw a named, actionable error; (b) the real repo orch-apply.sh MUST still pass. Without (a) this ships as another guard nobody has seen fire — the exact defect class as FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED.

AC-3 Full suite must remain green and must not shrink: scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js is 36/36 PASS / exit 0 as of 2026-08-06T15:45Z. Report the post-change count explicitly; a count below 36 means an assertion was lost, not that the change was clean.

AC-4 Do NOT solve this by hardcoding a fallback list or by widening the primary regex to swallow every idiom — both re-create the hand-maintained manifest the parent fix deleted. The invariant to enforce is 'the derived set covers every helper orch-apply.sh actually invokes', and the enforcement is a LOUD THROW, never a silent top-up.

backlog.title: No detector exercises an actual data-SERVING read path — every liveness check probes container health or a DB file, so a service can serve empty/error to 100% of callers indefinitely and every board stays green (kinh-dich dark 6 days undetected; news push silent 11h, alarm fired 1 min before self-recovery)
backlog.desc:
Two independent live outages in 8 days were invisible to the entire detector fleet because NOTHING in the fleet asks a service for real data and checks that the answer is real.

OCC-1 (kinh-dich, 6 days, telegram 4459/4461): stock-price served `/price/history?code=<any>` -> [] and kinh-dich returned 503 'insufficient price data for market reading' for EVERY ticker from 2026-07-31T00:41Z until PO rebuilt the container 2026-08-06T15:59Z. During that entire window: container healthchecks PASS, `docker ps` healthy, and the market-db-journal-guard reported PASS — because it probes the DB FILE's journal_mode, not whether any read path returns rows. 4461's own closing line: 'no detector fired for 6 days. All-tickers insufficient price data is trivially detectable — needs an active read-path probe, not a DB-file probe.'

OCC-2 (news push, 663 min, FIX-NEWSVPS-OVERNIGHT-PUSH-OUTAGE-663M-SILENT): the transport hung 2026-08-05T19:38:29Z -> 2026-08-06T06:42:25Z. Tier-1 B-01 fired at 06:41:27Z — ~1 minute before self-recovery, i.e. 11h into an 11h04m outage. ops's AC-2 recon is correct that no existing detector MIS-behaved: threshold-on-staleness detectors are inherently trailing, so they alarm at threshold-expiry, not at failure onset. That is exactly the structural gap.

ROOT CAUSE (shared): the fleet has container-health probes, DB-file probes, and staleness-threshold probes. It has ZERO probes that call a public read path and assert the RESPONSE IS NON-DEGENERATE. Empty array, 503, and 'database is locked' are all indistinguishable from healthy to every current check. This is the `feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data` class, now measured at 6-day blast radius.
backlog.acceptance:
AC-1 Enumerate the load-bearing SERVING read paths from docs/data/system-map.json (do not hardcode): at minimum stock-price /price/history, kinh-dich /reading/<ticker> + /market, news, foreign-flow, and the frontend-facing mcp-server equivalents. Output the enumerated set as data, not prose.
AC-2 Ship ONE reusable probe actuator (scripts/, so it is callable by cron and by Bash-less agents' owning flows alike) that, per path, issues a real request for a real watchlist ticker and applies a NON-DEGENERACY predicate, not a status-code predicate: HTTP 200 with an empty array, a 503, or an error body all count as FAIL. The predicate must be stated per path (e.g. price/history: >=1 OHLCV row with a plausible non-zero close; kinh-dich reading: a hexagram number in 1..64).
AC-3 NEGATIVE CONTROL IS MANDATORY AND IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW: replay the probe against the pre-fix state of BOTH occurrences and show it FAILS. backlog.desc: OBSERVED LIVE THIS TICK, not derived. docs/agents/po/flow/main.md AC-3 (added by FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR, currently review[]) instructs: SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git show --stat "$SHA" | grep -q docs/data/orch/orch-state.json || send_telegram(channel=bug, FAIL-LOUD: orch-state.json NOT in own commit ...). Running AC-3 as written would have emitted a bug-telegram asserting the writes had NOT landed, while all four mutations were provably present in HEAD tree: git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | jq confirmed po_manual_dispatch_flagged_at=2026-08-06T18:57:46Z, occurrence_count=3 + next_agent=developer on the CLEAN row, the decision-journal evidence key, and desc_len=3145 on the filled stub.
backlog.root_cause: The predicate tests the WRONG object. AC-3 exists to prove the writes reached the persistence layer, and its own generic rule states that correctly (any step that writes an artifact AND asserts its own persistence must re-read the persistence layer (git HEAD) before claiming it). But the implementation re-reads the COMMIT AUTHORSHIP (is this path in the stat of the commit I just made) rather than the persistence layer (are my mutations in HEAD tree). Those coincide only when no peer committed the shared hot file between the orch-apply write and this agent commit. On shared main with multiple concurrent sessions that window is routinely lost - see feedback_shared_main_peer_push_sweeps_held_data_commits and feedback_coldevict_bare_commit_sweeps_worker_staged_index for the same sweep behaviour observed from the other side.
backlog.user_impact: False FAIL-LOUD on the bug channel from a routine, correct PO cycle. Two compounding costs: (1) it trains readers to discount AC-3 bug-telegrams, which defeats the gate the parent fix was built to install; (2) the inverse error is worse and also live - a PO tick whose orch-apply genuinely failed but whose commit happened to include an orch-state.json change made by a PEER would PASS the grep and be reported as confirmed. So the predicate is both false-positive and false-negative prone. Every PO tick that mutates the board is exposed.
backlog.fix_spec: Replace the authorship grep with a content assertion against HEAD tree. After the commit, re-read the persistence layer and assert the specific mutation this cycle made is present, e.g. git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json piped to a jq predicate over the id(s) and field(s) this cycle wrote (the same ids already named in the cycle RETURN/journal), not a filename grep. Pass when the mutation is found in HEAD tree regardless of WHICH commit carried it; FAIL-LOUD only when it is genuinely absent. Keep AC-3 mandatory and keep the generic rule prose - only the predicate changes. Note the parent row FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR is still in review[]: this is its read-side fast-follow, so land it before that row is signed off or the sign-off ratifies a predicate that does not hold.
backlog.ac: AC (replay both branches, no live writes): POSITIVE - fixture where the agent own commit does NOT contain orch-state.json but HEAD tree DOES contain the named mutation, new predicate must PASS and emit no telegram (current predicate FAILS here - this is the live 18:59Z case). NEGATIVE - fixture where the agent own commit DOES contain orch-state.json but the named mutation is absent from HEAD tree (simulating an orch-apply that silently did not land the field), new predicate must FAIL-LOUD (current predicate PASSES here - the dangerous inverse). backlog.title: notebook-auto-prune charges the ENTIRE byte-cap overage to dated journal sections: rolling headings (## Archive, ## Known patterns) carry the MAX sentinel key so they can never be the drop candidate, yet they contribute their full bytes to the overage — every breach is paid for by deleting real cycle history while the actual bloat is retained
backlog.verification_gate: replay_on_fixture_both_axes
backlog.desc: REPORTED BY ba (signal ba-2026-08-06T18:53:30Z-gateway-blind), 2x reproduced live on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/ba.md during the TE-T05 cycle (section FIX-VNINDEX-CROSS-PLANE-PLAUSIBILITY-GATE dropped twice, once after an Edit, once after a full Write; recovered from git HEAD 8732d0854/2b55a01b1). PO READ THE SCRIPT AND THE REPORTER'S STATED ROOT CAUSE IS WRONG — do not implement against it. ba claimed the hook 'counts ALL ## headings toward its 3-section cap instead of scoping to DATED headings only per notebook-write AC-2a'. There is NO 3-section cap anywhere in scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh: the drop loop is `while true` and breaks the instant BOTH line_count<=LINE_CAP AND byte_count<=BYTE_CAP hold (L389-395). Section count is only consulted for the SECTION_COUNT<=1 safe-fail. The true mechanism is the INVERSE of what was reported: rolling headings are not over-counted as droppable, they are structurally EXEMPT from being dropped while still being fully counted in the byte total.
backlog.root_cause: Two independently-correct mechanisms compose into a data-loss ratchet. (1) SELECTION plane: nso_sections_with_ts assigns the 17-char MAX sentinel key ($NSO_SENTINEL_KEY) to any '## ' heading with no parseable timestamp. The drop candidate is always MIN_KEY. So a rolling heading — '## Archive', '## Known patterns / preferences', '## Identity', the exact stable-ROLLING-heading convention .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md itself prescribes — sorts to MAX and can NEVER be the drop candidate as long as one dated section survives. That exemption is deliberate and correct in isolation. (2) MEASUREMENT plane: BYTE_CAP = LINE_CAP * 60 is computed over the WHOLE FILE (L347-352, L387-388), rolling sections included. Compose them and the invariant becomes: 100% of any byte overage is repaid by deleting dated cycle history, 0% by the rolling sections, REGARDLESS of which sections actually hold the bytes. On ba.md the binding axis is bytes, not lines: 45L/10252B against cap 200L/12000B — i.e. it prunes at 22% of the line cap because 2 of its 4 headings are permanently-retained rolling sections. Worse, it is a RATCHET: ba's documented recovery action (re-document the lost content into the Known-patterns section) grows the undroppable share, which makes the NEXT dated section get dropped sooner. Any notebook following the prescribed convention converges to rolling-sections-only.
backlog.corroboration: Signal notebook-direction-defaulted-docs-agent-memory-notebooks-ba-md-2026-08-06T185213Z fired on the SAME file the SAME day and is the second half of the proof: ba.md's dated headings are date-only ('## TE-T05 · 2026-08-06', '## UC-CRITIC-HOOKS-ENFORCEMENT · 2026-08-06') so they normalize to an IDENTICAL key and tie; the only non-tied sections are the two sentinels, which nso_vote_direction excludes from the direction vote by construction — so direction is UNRESOLVABLE, DIRECTION_SOURCE=default, and the drop falls to the newest_first default (drop physically-LAST of the tie group). The tiebreak signal was filed action_required=informational_no_action_needed; it is not informational, it is the corroborating half of this row.
backlog.fix_spec: Make the two planes agree. Preferred: make the MEASUREMENT plane match the SELECTION plane — compute the cap predicate over the DROPPABLE (non-sentinel) section bytes only, so the pruner stops deleting history to pay for bytes it is structurally forbidden to reclaim, and instead emits an honest signal when the undroppable remainder alone exceeds cap (the same honest-signal contract L400-425 already uses for the single-section case). Alternative: keep whole-file measurement but make rolling sections droppable-of-last-resort once every dated section is exhausted. Either way the rule must be stated in .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md so the prescribed Archive/Known-patterns convention and the pruner stop contradicting each other.
backlog.ac: AC-1 REGRESSION (must FAIL before, PASS after): fixture notebook, 3 dated sections + '## Archive' + '## Known patterns', total bytes over cap, where the two rolling sections alone hold MORE than the overage. Current code deletes a dated section and still leaves the file over cap on the next write; fixed code must retain all 3 dated sections and emit the honest over-cap signal instead. AC-2 NEGATIVE (must not regress): fixture whose bloat genuinely IS in the dated sections and whose rolling sections are small — the true-oldest dated section must still be dropped exactly as today. AC-3 RATCHET: replay the same fixture through 3 consecutive over-cap writes; assert the retained dated-section count is non-decreasing (today it strictly decreases to zero). AC-4: no live notebook is written by the test.

Nearest neighbours checked and NOT covers: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-DIRECTION-UNRESOLVABLE-ZERO-TS-NOTEBOOKS (review[]) shipped the default-and-proceed behaviour and owns the DIRECTION vote when ALL sections are sentinel — it does not touch which sections are eligible to be dropped, nor the byte accounting. FIX-NOTEBOOK-LINECAP-SWEEP-BYTE-BLIND-BACKSTOP (review[]) is the cron pre-filter, a different actor.
