backlog.title: VnDirect Tier1+Tier2 served path structurally cannot emit a nil Change/ChangePercent -- an unavailable change is served as 0 ("genuine flat day"), violating DSI-INV-1
backlog.desc:
PROVEN 2026-08-06 during PO sign-off of FACTORY-STOCK-vndirect-mapper-tests (ruling: docs/agent-memory/decisions/ruling-20260806T2059Z-vndirect-mapper-tests-po.md).

MECHANISM. apps/stock-price/pkg/infrastructure/fetchers.go declares its inline VnDirect payload struct with Change/PctChange as NON-pointer `float64` -- Tier1 :78-79, Tier2 :182-183. Unmarshalling JSON `null` into a non-pointer float is a documented no-op in encoding/json ("unmarshaling a JSON null into any other Go type has no effect on the value"), so the field silently keeps its zero value. The code then does `change := item.Change` (:89, :193) and returns `Change: &change` (:113-114, :214-215) -- the address of a local, which is structurally NEVER nil. An omitted field behaves identically.

The comment sitting directly above that code at :88 and :192 reads `// DSI-INV-1: use pointers so 0 is distinguishable from nil (unavailable)`. It is false with respect to its own code -- the pointer exists but can never be nil. Classic comment-not-code; do not let the comment convince a reviewer the invariant holds.

CONTRACT BREACHED. pkg/domain/models.go:22-23 -- `Change *float64` with tag json:"change" and the comment `// nil = unavailable, 0 = genuine flat day` (named invariant DSI-INV-1, org-wide, see docs/architecture-briefs/2026-06-05-carry-yield-single-signal-fixture.md). The pointer propagates untouched through pkg/application/usecases.go:76-77 into the served FetchPriceResponse, so the wire response emits `change: 0` where the contract says `change: null`. A consumer cannot distinguish "VnDirect had no change data" from "the stock genuinely closed flat".

MEASURED, not inferred (stdlib-only harness, both struct shapes copied verbatim from the two files, identical input):
  `"change":null`  -> SERVED &0  |  PRIMITIVE nil  -> DIVERGE
  field omitted    -> SERVED &0  |  PRIMITIVE nil  -> DIVERGE
  `"change":0`     -> SERVED &0  |  PRIMITIVE &0   -> agree
Reproduce by unmarshalling those three payloads into (a) the fetchers.go inline struct and (b) the mapper.go struct, then comparing nil-ness of the resulting pointers. The correct shape already exists and is already tested: apps/stock-price/pkg/primitive/vndirect-quote-mapper/mapper.go:30-31 + :116-124, guarded by mapper_test.go cases `null_change_and_pctChange_maps_to_nil_pointers`, `omitted_change_fields_treated_as_nil`, `partial_null_-_only_change_is_null` (all green).

AC-1 ESTABLISH REACHABILITY BEFORE ASSUMING SEVERITY. This row proves the code path cannot emit nil; it does NOT prove VnDirect ever actually sends null or omits the field. Capture real api-finfo.vndirect.com.vn/v4/stock_prices payloads (illiquid/halted/newly-listed tickers and pre-open are the likely shapes) and state with evidence whether null/omitted change occurs live. If it never occurs, say so plainly and downgrade to P3 -- do not quietly close, the struct shape is still wrong and the comment is still false.
AC-2 Fix the served shape so an unavailable change reaches the wire as null, not 0. Preferred: rewire Tier1/Tier2 to call the existing primitive (see FACTORY-STOCK-extract-vndirect-mapper -- ONE rewire closes BOTH rows; do not bill this twice and do not re-create mapper.go). Fallback if that refactor is not taken: change the two inline structs to *float64 and copy-when-non-nil.
AC-3 This is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on a served endpoint, not a pure refactor -- an unavailable change flips from `0` to `null` on the wire. Do NOT ship it as invisible. Check every consumer of FetchPriceResponse.Change / .ChangePercent for a bare dereference or a formatter that assumes non-nil, across the Go plane AND any TS/frontend consumer of the JSON, and state what you checked. rebuild_required: a served-path change to a shipped binary -- rebuild stock-price and RAW-verify sample tickers after.
AC-4 Delete or correct the false `// DSI-INV-1: use pointers so 0 is distinguishable from nil` comment at fetchers.go:88 and :192 in the same change.
AC-5 Regression guard on the SERVED path, not on a copy -- the whole point of the row that produced this finding. A test that would have failed before this fix and passes after, exercising the fetcher's own mapping.

DO NOT close by making the primitive match the served path. The primitive is the correct one; models.go documents the contract; reverting it would enshrine the violation and break 3 currently-green tests.

backlog.title: system-auditor committed cycle c71 TWICE 36s apart and the second commit retroactively rewrote the first commit's already-published OUTPUT-CONTRACT counters (signals_posted 0->1) on a dedup-SKIP cycle — the immutability guard caught it but is mode=warn so nothing blocked

The signal's createdAt is 21:12:17Z — it fired on 95c1ffb01, the LATER commit, 36s after the one that was verified. So the answer to the relayer's own question ('did a LATER commit alter that section?') is yes. WHAT THE SECOND COMMIT DID (`git diff 18a3e2399 95c1ffb01 -- docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md`): it edited two factual counters INSIDE the already-committed '## c71' section — `Anomalies: 0 new (C 0, W 1-dedup-skip, I 0)` -> `Anomalies: 1 (C 0, W 1-dedup-skip, I 0)`, and `[OUTPUT-CONTRACT] signals_posted=0 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=1 (via E-3 SKIP-dedup) | dashboard_rows=1 | dedup_skipped=1` -> `signals_posted=1 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=1 | dashboard_rows=1 | dedup_skipped=1`. Do not fix a symptom layer before this is answered; the two have different fixes and only one of them is a script.

AC-2 One notebook cycle = exactly ONE commit. The cycle boundary IS the commit (memory: feedback_notebook_cycle_boundary_is_commit_not_session). Make a second commit that touches an already-published '## c<N>' section for a cycle id already present at HEAD fail loud rather than silently amend.

backlog.title: audit-output-contract V4/V5 compare a NEW-only anomaly tally against an ALL-emissions signals_posted counter that includes dedup-skips - every dedup-only auditor cycle self-reports a false contract VIOLATION
backlog.source: telegram report 4474 (analysis-agent, 2026-08-06T21:11:17Z) - triaged and REFUTED as a genuine contract violation by po at 2026-08-06T22:05Z; the report is real but the thing it reports is the checker misfiring, not the auditor lying
backlog.root_cause: Two counters with different denominators are compared as if they had the same one. scripts/audit-output-contract.sh line ~180 counts '[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup' as signals_posted++ (and signal_queue_rows_written++ and dedup_skipped++). docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:835 defines the RETURN-headline N as NEW findings only and says verbatim 'dedup-skipped known anomalies do NOT count - they are not new'. V4 (anomalies-count == 0 AND signals_posted > 0) and V5 (next-token == clean AND signals_posted > 0) therefore fire on ANY cycle whose only emissions were dedup-skips: the agent correctly writes headline 0, the script correctly counts signals_posted 1, and the comparison is structurally guaranteed to report a violation. This is not probabilistic - it fires every time. V2 and V3 are unaffected because signal_queue_rows_written and dashboard_rows also increment on SKIP-dedup, so those two comparisons are denominator-symmetric; only V4/V5 straddle the new-vs-all boundary.
backlog.evidence: Mechanism read at source (script lines 158-186 + main.md:835,1067), not inferred from the symptom. Live instantiation, cross-checked on two planes: the auditor cycle at 2026-08-06T21:10Z emitted exactly one signal, sys-20260806T211009-070b (rag-service A-30 memory floor breach, WARN), against dedup key mem_pressure:rag-service:A-30-floor-breach whose ledger entry docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json shows last_sent 2026-08-06T17:15:06Z - i.e. a SKIP-dedup, so headline 0 NEW anomalies was CORRECT and V4's VIOLATION was false. Independent confirmation that this is a checker bug and not an agent bug, from the auditor's own notebook one cycle earlier (id=sys-20260806T204129-7435, 20:41Z): its OUTPUT-CONTRACT line reads 'signals_posted=0 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=1 (via E-3 SKIP-dedup) | dashboard_rows=0 | dedup_skipped=1' - the same event class scored as signals_posted=0 there and signals_posted=1 at 21:10Z. That line is also hand-composed (the parenthetical '(via E-3 SKIP-dedup)' is not in the script's output format), which is its own main.md:1065 violation and is the SECOND finding here: the two cycles only disagree because one ran the script and one did not. Underlying condition independently probed and found benign - docker stats shows rag-service at 93.89% (961.4MiB/1GiB) with RestartCount=0 and OOMKilled=false, receding from the 98.20% reading, so the dedup suppression itself was correct behaviour and there is no infra escalation hiding behind this ticket (checked explicitly to avoid the inverse error recorded in feedback_a30_discriminator_crash_cliff_misscored_as_reclamation_dip).

Do not fix this by redefining the headline to include dedup-skips: main.md:835 is the SSOT for what N means and the RETURN block reports 'M dedup-skipped' separately for exactly this reason.

AC-2 Regression fixture must include the negative control that is the whole point of this row: a markers file containing ONLY '[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup' lines plus --anomalies-count 0 must produce NO violation. Add the positive control alongside it (a real '[emit-signal] OK' line plus --anomalies-count 0 must still violate) so the fix cannot be shown to work by simply disabling V4/V5 (feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist).

AC-3 Audit the other emit-signal marker forms against the same new-vs-all boundary before closing: 'OK-escalation-bypass', 'OK e3-only' and 'OK no-telegram' all increment signals_posted too - confirm from main.md whether each is a NEW finding for headline purposes, and state the answer in the script header rather than leaving it implicit.

AC-4 Second finding, same row because same 20-minute window and same file: the 20:41Z OUTPUT-CONTRACT line was hand-composed in violation of main.md:1065 ('MUST be the verbatim output of scripts/audit-output-contract.sh - never hand-composed'). backlog.title: freshnessSlaMonitorJob market-hours gate covers only the CLOSE side: the */30 cron's 02:00Z tick lands 0-3s INSIDE the market-hours window, when a market-hours-only source is necessarily as stale as the whole overnight gap — a CRITICAL 'price stale Nmin (threshold 10min)' is emitted deterministically on the first tick of every trading day
backlog.note: Telegram report 4479 (2026-08-07T02:00:03Z) '[sla-monitor] CRITICAL breach: price stale 74min (threshold 10min)' — FALSE POSITIVE, structural and daily. MECHANISM (read at source): apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/freshnessSlaMonitorJob.ts:449 MARKET_HOURS_ONLY_SIGNALS = ['price','foreign_flow'] and :531 skips escalation only when `!isVnMarketHours(now)`; the documented window is 02:00-08:59 UTC Mon-Fri (:445-446). apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/cronConfig.ts:123 sets freshnessSlaMonitor to '*/30 * * * *', so the first tick of every trading day fires 0-3s AFTER the window opens. At that instant a market-hours-only source has been legitimately idle for the entire overnight gap, so the 10-minute market-hours threshold is unsatisfiable by construction — the gate handles the CLOSE side of the window and has no warm-up on the OPEN side. backlog.title: rebuild-raw-verify-check.sh ATTEST_ERE does not match 'RAW-verified' — the hyphenated PAST-TENSE form that is this repo's dominant attestation idiom (18 of 24 occurrences in the last 400 commit messages) — so the gate false-blocks pushes whose verification genuinely happened and was genuinely attested.
backlog.root_cause: scripts/audits/rebuild-raw-verify-check.sh:115 `ATTEST_ERE='raw-verify|raw verified|realdata'`. The three alternatives cover the hyphenated INFINITIVE ('raw-verify') and the SPACED past tense ('raw verified'), but NOT the hyphenated past tense ('raw-verified'): 'raw-verified' does not contain the substring 'raw-verify' (position 10 is 'i', not 'y') and does not contain 'raw verified' (hyphen != space). `shopt -s nocasematch` is correctly set at :180 and :202, so this is NOT a case-sensitivity bug — casing is already handled; the gap is purely the missing tense/separator combination. Both escape hatches (i) commit-message attestation at :181 and (ii) docs/agent-memory/decisions/**|reports/TASK_REPORT_*.md added-line attestation at :203 share the SAME regex variable, so a single missing alternative closes BOTH escapes simultaneously.
backlog.evidence: MEASURED, not inferred. (a) Predicate replayed verbatim in bash with `shopt -s nocasematch` and the live ERE string: 'RAW-verified' NO-MATCH, 'RAW-VERIFIED' NO-MATCH, 'raw-verified GREEN' NO-MATCH; 'RAW verified' MATCH, 'RAW-verify' MATCH, 'REALDATA' MATCH. (b) CORPUS FREQUENCY over the last 400 commit messages (`git log -400 --format=%B | grep -oiE 'raw[- ]verif(y|ied)' | sort | uniq -c`): RAW-verified=16, raw-verified=2 (18 total, ALL non-matching) vs raw-verify=3, RAW-verify=1, raw verified=1, RAW verified=1 (6 total, matching). So 18/24 = 75% of the attestation phrasings this repo actually writes are invisible to the gate. (c) LIVE INCIDENT: this is the root cause of pendingSignal#3 (fleet-worktree-push auto-push-abort, 2026-08-07T02:47:17Z, ahead=21 threshold=20). The router's remediation was commit 1c26af802, which added a decision-journal line WORDED to contain 'RAW verified' (spaced) — its own commit message states the verification 'genuinely happened (documented in detail in the S76/S77/S78 entries above: docker logs, per-tool log file, DB query, wc -l line counts, test runs) but neither commit message in this range used the exact case-insensitive token the gate's ATTEST_ERE requires'. That is a per-incident WORKAROUND (rephrase until the regex matches), not a fix: the gate is unchanged and will false-block the next agent who writes the idiomatic 'RAW-verified'.
backlog.ac: (AC-1) ATTEST_ERE must match the hyphenated past tense. Prefer collapsing the tense/separator axes rather than appending a 4th literal — e.g. `raw[- ]verif(y|ied)|realdata` — and state in a code comment WHY the axes are collapsed (a literal-list ERE is what shipped the gap; adding one more literal leaves 'rawverify', 'raw-verifying' etc. equally invisible and re-opens the same class). Do NOT weaken it into matching bare 'verified' — the token must stay a deliberate attestation, not an accidental word. (AC-2) REGRESSION TEST, corpus-based not synthetic: assert the new ERE matches every distinct phrasing actually present in the repo's commit-message corpus (derive the list with the uniq -c command in `evidence` (b), do not hand-write it), and assert it still REJECTS a control body containing 'verified' / 'verify' with no raw|realdata qualifier. A fresh-fixture-only test is what let this ship (same class as project memory feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist). (AC-3) Prove the live incident is closed: replay the gate over the exact range that aborted (BASE..HEAD spanning the flagged confidence-threshold lines) with commit 1c26af802's journal line REMOVED from consideration, and show it now PASSES on the pre-existing 'RAW-verified' text alone. (AC-4) Grep the fleet for any OTHER gate carrying its own copy of this token list and fix or converge them in the same pass — a second divergent copy is the same defect one file over.

The originating report's claim that no-Bash is "deliberate fleet-wide policy shared by every cowork gatherer/publisher agent" is factually wrong — there are three standing exceptions in the same cadence tier.

WHY NOT AN MCP TOOL (the option that needs no grant at all): verified — docker-compose.yml does NOT mount ./scripts into the mcp-server container (mounts are ./data/live, ./data/pdfs, ./mcp.config.json, ./reports, ./docs/agent-memory, ./docs/data, ./docs/data/orch, ./docs/signals, ./docs/analysis-briefs, ./.claude/commands/crons). Both agents already hold repo-wide `Write` and `Edit`, so an injected agent can already reach code execution transitively by rewriting a script a Bash-capable peer runs. Bash makes that direct rather than transitive. What is genuinely NEW is process execution and network egress (git push, docker, curl) from an agent whose input includes untrusted scraped news text. That is accepted here as proportionate to a live P1 coverage loss on a proven artifact, and it is the reason for the tight scope above and the non-precedent clause below.

done_verified.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T16:49:30Z by po from a coordinator finding during refine-worker verification. The reporter explicitly asked PO to settle the period-provenance question before sizing, and correctly declined to size it themselves. SETTLED BELOW AT SOURCE.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION WAS POSED AS A BINARY. THE ANSWER IS NEITHER, AND THAT IS WORSE THAN EITHER BRANCH.
The reporter asked: do financial_reports.period_year / period_quarter derive FROM the filename (severe) or from parsed content (cosmetic)? Traced end to end, they derive from NEITHER — and neither does the filename. Both come from the SAME caller-supplied ingest key, so they are structurally incapable of disagreeing with each other, and neither is ever compared to the document.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:183-184 — periodYear/periodQuarter are read out of multipart form fields: fields.get("period_year"), fields.get("period_quarter"). Purely caller-supplied by the VPS pusher.
  - :194-201 — the ONLY validation is on SHAPE: year rejected unless 2000..2099, quarter rejected unless in {Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4}. The pair (2025, Q4) is perfectly well-formed and passes. Nothing checks correspondence to the PDF.
  - :224 — normaliseFilename(sourceUrl || actionCode+".pdf", actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter). THE FILENAME IS DERIVED FROM THE PERIOD KEY, not the reverse.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 — canonical = ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf; the source URL's own basename is used ONLY if it ends in .pdf AND already contains the action code. "DPM_2025_Q4.pdf" is exactly the canonical form, so it is a RENDERING of the stored key.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/parseBctcReport.ts:77-82 — ParseBctcReportParams.period is a PARAMETER of type FiscalPeriod. The parser is TOLD the period; it never reads it out of rawText.
  - :465-470 — $periodYear: report.period.year, $periodQuarter: report.period.quarter, $sortKey: report.period.sortKey written straight through to the INSERT at :354.
CONCLUSION: the filename is NOT cosmetic and is NOT independent evidence. It is the same value as the DB period columns, from the same unvalidated source. The reporter's "if from the filename" severity branch is the one that applies — for a different reason than they expected.

SEVERITY IS HIGHER THAN EITHER BRANCH THE REPORTER OFFERED, BECAUSE OF SLOT OCCUPANCY.
sort_key is year-quarter, built from the same key, and the row identity/conflict key is (action_code, sort_key) — see parseBctcReport.ts:316 (.get(report.actionCode, report.period.sortKey)) and the ON CONFLICT clause at :393. A document mislabelled 2025-Q4 does not merely carry a wrong label: IT OCCUPIES THE SLOT THE REAL DPM Q4-2025 REPORT WOULD LAND IN. The correct Q4-2025 filing can never be ingested into that slot while this row holds it. That is a durable data-loss condition, not a display bug.
Second consequence, as the reporter predicted: apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/financial-reports/bctcFullTools.ts:461 sets deltaType = latest.period_year !== priorRow.period_year ? "YoY" : "QoQ". Q1-2026 financials stored as 2025-Q4 will be diffed against DPM 2025-Q3 and labelled QoQ. Every DPM QoQ/YoY series is then wrong, and wrong in a way that looks well-formed.

TIME PRESSURE IS REAL BUT THE REPORTER'S URGENCY MODEL IS WRONG, AND ACTING ON IT WOULD WASTE WORK.
The report reasons that "the remaining 31 windows keep accreting under whatever period identity is stored", so each daily fire deepens the mislabel. IT DOES NOT. The period identity is a SINGLE key already fixed on the row at ingest; the 31 remaining windows all inherit that one key and cannot make it more wrong. Nothing degrades per fire.
WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES STATE IS FINALIZE. Live probe this tick through the mcp-server runtime: get_bctc_report_id(code="DPM") returns {report_id: null, report_ids: [], count: 0, existing_refine_status: "PENDING"}. That tool filters on refine_status='DONE' (getBctcReportIdTool.ts:131), so RIGHT NOW nothing is served and no consumer can reach the mislabelled document. Finalize flips refine_status to DONE and ARMS it.
THEREFORE: do NOT halt the refine slot — that discards the 15 completed windows for no safety gain, since the mislabel neither grows nor becomes reachable while status is PENDING. The correct intervention is to correct or remove the period identity on this one row BEFORE finalize. That is an ops/data action, is AC 1 below, and is deliberately separated from the code fix so it can run on a different clock.

CONCRETE INSTANCE (reporter's evidence, accepted — five independent pages, internally consistent, correctly reasoned): report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d, stored as DPM_2025_Q4.pdf, content unambiguously Q1-2026 — unit-0005 "Cho ky hoat dong tu ngay 01 thang 01 nam 2026 den ngay 31 thang 03 nam 2026"; unit-0007 "Tu 01/01/2026 den 31/03/2026" with a "Tu 01/01/2025 den 31/03/2025" comparative; unit-0009 "Quy I Nam 2026" + "Tai ngay 31 thang 03 nam 2026"; unit-0010 "Tai ngay 31 thang 03 nam 2026"; unit-0011 "Quy I Nam 2026". The reporter pre-emptively excluded the OCR-year-misread hypothesis (2025 appears correctly throughout as the comparative column, "Nam 2025 (Trinh bay lai)") — po concurs, and Q4-2025 covers Oct-Dec 2025 while this document covers Jan-Mar 2026, which are disjoint periods, not an off-by-one.

BLAST-RADIUS QUESTION ANSWERED — DPM IS NOT IMPLICATED IN THE 07-19 REPARSE CORRUPTION. The reporter asked whether DPM fell inside FIX-BCTC-REPARSE-BATCH-CORRUPTION-NGAYNOP-FLIP. It did not: that incident's decision record names CTG, DBC, DGC, DXG, FRT, GEX, KDC, KDH, MSN, PDR, SAB, SHB, VCB, VJC, VND — no DPM. Different defect (that one flipped ngay_nop and zeroed total_assets), different mechanism, no shared cause. Do not bundle them.

CLASS PARALLEL — THIS IS THE UC-CDC-P1 MECHANISM IN A SECOND SUBSYSTEM, AND THE REPAIR SHAPE IS ALREADY RATIFIED THERE. UC-CDC-P1: calendar_status is caller-supplied, the tool's Zod schema is a bare z.string().optional() with no enum gate, the server never computes it, and a correct producer (vnTradingCalendar) already existed unwired. Here: period identity is caller-supplied, validation is shape-only, the server never derives it, and a correct producer already exists — THE DOCUMENT ITSELF, which states its period unambiguously on five separate pages. Both are instances of memory lesson feedback_pressure_state_caller_supplied_fields_dead_server_computed_live. The ratified remedy shape there was: compute server-side at the boundary AND gate the caller override. Apply that shape; do not invent a new one.

REMEDY — DIRECTION SETTLED, ONE GENUINELY OPEN CHOICE.
Add a period-vs-content check at the ingest/parse boundary so a document whose stated period contradicts its supplied key cannot be silently stored under that key. Honest options, NOT chosen by po:
  [a] VALIDATE ONLY — extract the period from the PDF text, compare to the supplied key, and on mismatch reject-or-quarantine rather than writing. Conservative; keeps the caller as source of truth and only refuses contradictions.
  [b] DERIVE FROM CONTENT — treat the caller key as a hint and take the period from the document.
  [c] BOTH — derive, and gate the caller override the way UC-CDC-P1 gates calendar_status.
STRONG CAUTION AGAINST NAIVE [b], from this very document: the reporter also found units 0002/0003 carrying OCR_quality_critical at confidence 0.45-0.50. Text quality is NOT guaranteed, so a content-derived period would itself be unreliable on exactly the poor-OCR filings that most need checking. Whatever is chosen must FAIL LOUD (quarantine) rather than fall back to the unvalidated key, or it re-creates this defect with extra steps. A mismatch must never resolve silently in either direction.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. DATA, AND IT IS TIME-ORDERED FIRST: report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d is corrected or removed BEFORE its refine finalizes, so it never occupies (DPM, 2025-Q4) in a DONE state. Verify via get_bctc_report_id(code="DPM", year=2025, quarter="Q4") returning either nothing or a document whose content is genuinely Oct-Dec 2025.
  2. CODE: a document whose text states a period contradicting the supplied (year, quarter) key is NOT written under that key — it is rejected or quarantined, with a loud signal naming both periods.
  3. NEGATIVE CONTROL (mandatory — without it the fix degrades into blanket rejection): a correctly-labelled filing, AND a filing whose text is too poor to extract a period at all, must BOTH still ingest normally. Do not let "cannot determine period" become "reject".
  4. The real DPM Q4-2025 report can subsequently be ingested into the freed slot — proving the fix restored capacity, not merely removed a bad row.
  5. Regression test asserting the (action_code, sort_key) slot cannot be occupied by a document of a different period.

SECONDARY, EVIDENCE ONLY — DO NOT MINT, DO NOT EXPAND SCOPE INTO IT. The reporter also flagged unit-0003's "I. No dai han" total 215.286.231.782 against listed sub-items 132.540.000.000 + 78.521.573.782 = 211.061.573.782, a ~4.2bn gap consistent with a dropped line, at confidence 0.45-0.50. That is ESC-5 deep-dive territory per the existing low-confidence handling path, and is recorded here only because it is the same document and is the direct evidence for the [b] caution above. It is NOT part of this row's acceptance.

DO NOT ROUTE THIS THROUGH FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES — see the warning annotation added to that row this tick. Fixing filename derivation alone would make the filename stop reflecting the stored period, removing the only visible symptom while the corruption persists. That is active harm, not a partial fix.

ready.note:
PO TRIAGE 2026-07-21 (TNB c115 finding F-CHEF-MORNING-FALSE-FULL-VERDICT). VERDICT: CONFIRMED AT SOURCE by PO — with ONE correction to TNB's evidence chain (below). This is a FALSE CERTIFICATION, which is a strictly worse failure mode than every previously-tracked chef finding: all prior ones were HONEST degraded self-reports.

RAW EVIDENCE (PO read docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-morning.json directly; note the fields are NESTED — metadata.* and tnb_synthesis.* — a top-level jq query returns null and will look like a missing field):
- metadata.cycle_id = "morning-2026-07-21T05:20:19Z"
- metadata.quality_verdict = "full"
- metadata.layers_walked_summary = "1-6 (full)"
- tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer = "Fed funds rate 3.63% with risk-off sentiment signaled by gold spike +$24.1 to $4053/oz. Safe-haven demand reflects caution amid margin debt expansion."  -> Fed funds ONLY. NO PMI. NO EFFR-IORB spread. Both are mandatory Layer-2 content per tnb-methodology.md / the main.md Layer table.
- known_gaps = ["[gap:business_context_sparse] ...", "[gap:gold_4300_active] ..."] -> ZERO L2 gap token.
So the dish certifies 6/6 layers walked while its own persisted payload shows Layer 2 is not walked, and emits no gap token to compensate. The quality signal is not merely wrong, it is confidently wrong — downstream consumers that trust quality_verdict to gate use have no way to detect this.

*** CORRECTION TO TNB'S EVIDENCE (PO re-verified; do not carry TNB's version forward) ***
TNB's finding argues the self-scoring gate CAN work by contrasting the SAME-DAY eod dish, which it says "explicitly tokens [gap:L2_US_macro_absent]". That contrast is NOT RAW-verifiable: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-eod.json DOES NOT EXIST (PO ls-confirmed; TNB's OWN other finding, GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST, states the same file is Glob-confirmed absent). TNB therefore cited the eod NOTEBOOK claim as if it were persisted-JSON evidence, in the same handoff where it correctly reports that JSON never landed — an internal contradiction.
The proof leg SURVIVES, but must be re-anchored to the EVENING dish, which PO verified RAW: unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-evening.json has metadata.quality_verdict="degraded" AND tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer="EFFR-IORB spread 1.64pp NEUTRAL. Brent +2.31% ... Gold +1.97% ..." — i.e. genuine L2 content and an honest verdict, same agent, same day. That is a sound same-day control and it establishes the same point: the defect is isolated to the morning cycle, not universal.
CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: do not build the fix around a comparison with the eod JSON. It is not there.

OCCURRENCE COUNT = 1 (first live-verified). Below the 3-cycle auto-cure threshold, and PO agrees auto-cure is the WRONG instrument here regardless of count — see the sibling row below.

FIX SHAPE (PO directive): the verdict gate must be a DETERMINISTIC ASSERTION, not a narrative self-judgement. Before writing metadata.quality_verdict="full", the agent must assert per-layer that the layer's own payload field is non-empty AND contains its mandatory tokens (L2: PMI and/or EFFR-IORB). If an assertion fails, "full" is not writable — the verdict must downgrade to "degraded" and a [gap:L<N>_...] token must be appended to known_gaps. Verdict and gap-token must be derived from ONE evaluation so they cannot disagree.

AC: (1) quality_verdict="full" is unwritable when any mandatory layer field lacks its required tokens; (2) verdict and known_gaps are computed from a single pass (no independent second judgement); (3) negative control — a synthetic dish with L2 stripped must produce degraded + an L2 gap token, proving the assertion fires (without this the fix is indistinguishable from always writing degraded); (4) RAW-verify on the next morning fire by reading metadata.quality_verdict + tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer from the persisted JSON — an agent self-report or notebook line is NOT acceptable evidence (the 07-21 morning notebook line matched the false "full" verbatim, so the notebook faithfully reproduces the bad verdict and cannot detect it).

SIBLING / DO NOT MERGE: FIX-CHEF-L6-TOKEN-PERSISTENCE-RECURRING (P3, BLOCKED) is the nearest prior art and is RELATED BUT DISTINCT. That row = a token WAS generated and then dropped on JSON write (persist-step vs narrative-gen, isolation-first, 3 manifestations despite 2 auto-cures). THIS row = no token was ever generated AND the verdict was affirmatively certified "full". Different mechanism, opposite end of the pipeline. They share the family "chef self-scoring integrity" and should be looked at together, but merging them would bury a false-certification bug inside a persistence bug. The L6 row's own lesson applies here though: more same-shape auto-cure is the wrong move; this needs a deterministic assertion.

ready.title: Every subagent shares ONE git working directory + ONE HEAD: any agent that honours a `branch:` field (e.g. a PM handoff) checks out that branch in the shared checkout, and every concurrent peer's commits silently land on it. 4 independent hits on 2026-07-31 alone; zero board rows existed.
ready.root_cause: STRUCTURAL, not behavioural. There is no worktree/checkout isolation between agents — all agents (router, dev-team, pm, po, developer, architect, agents-architect, qa) operate on the same `$PROJECT_ROOT` and therefore the same `.git/HEAD`. `git checkout <branch>` is a process-global mutation of shared state with no lock, no claim and no TTL, so it is not serialisable against peers the way the index is (the index at least has `index.lock` + the Layer-0 sweep guard). CLAUDE.md's `NO branches — all work stays on main` invariant is the only thing holding the system together, and it is enforced by prose alone: nothing structurally prevents a `branch:` field from appearing in a PM handoff / task row and being obeyed. Note this is the SIBLING hazard to the shared-INDEX sweep (FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD family, 6 rows, Layer-0 hook shipped): same shared-working-dir root, different shared resource (HEAD vs index), and the sweep-guard hook is structurally blind to it because it only inspects $GIT_INDEX_FILE shape, never HEAD.
ready.evidence: dev-team signal `dev-20260731T020908` (signal_queue, status READ, minted by commit 3b20fc8c9): '4x today: subagents share dev-team's git checkout (no worktree isolation); a branch checkout (e.g. PM handoff's branch: field) hijacks peer commits.' The 4 named incidents that tick: dev-team's own stray commit, agents-architect's stray commit, the FIX-COWORK-FIRE-ELECTION-TICK-TOMBSTONE developer originating the branch, and the head-stamp developer's stash-pop failure. Independently corroborated by project memory `feedback_subagent_branch_checkout_hijacks_shared_working_dir` ('dev-team's own commits land on a subagent's branch; recover via isolated worktree, never checkout main mid-subagent-edit') — the hazard has been KNOWN and carried as tribal memory + ad-hoc recovery, never as a board row. 4 occurrences in one day clears the recurring-bug bar (>=2) by a factor of 2.
ready.ac: (AC-1) Name the enforcement layer and make it STRUCTURAL, not prose. The prose invariant already exists in CLAUDE.md and did not prevent 4 hits — a 5th doc sentence is a rejection. Candidate layers to evaluate explicitly, choosing and justifying one: (a) a `pre-checkout`-equivalent guard (git has no pre-checkout hook — say so if rejecting, do not silently assume one exists) e.g. a wrapper/alias or a `post-checkout` hook that hard-reverts + fail-louds any move off `main`; (b) real per-agent `git worktree` isolation; (c) a schema-level ban on the `branch:` field in task rows / PM handoffs so the trigger can never be authored. ROOT CAUSE (RAW-verified 2026-07-22T20:00-20:10Z, router + po). chef-evening cron is `45 19 * * *` = 19:45 UTC = 02:45 VN of D+1 — cowork-schedule.json chef-evening.vn_description literally reads '02:45 VN next day (GMT+7)'. chef.md Step 0.5 L48 computes WORK_DATE = TZ="Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh" date +%Y-%m-%d and L70 builds MARKER_KEY = published:<slot>:<WORK_DATE>. EVIDENCE — task_list_held(task_kind=cowork-slot) shows BOTH published:chef-evening:2026-07-22 (owner_client_session 9f4a6bfc-b001-4349-8a44-545f24c1b0ac, claimed_at 1784750141 = 19:55:41Z) AND published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 (owner_client_session ab870ed6-0502-4e49-811a-8e7c90aff1ef, claimed_at 1784750490 = 20:01:30Z) HELD SIMULTANEOUSLY, ttl_seconds 100800 each. Both runs therefore claimed successfully, both passed the gate, both published. Artifacts on disk, both dish_type=evening + quality_verdict=degraded, overlapping conviction VHM+VIC: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-22-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-22, timestamp_utc 19:56:15Z, EIB/VIC/VHM/VJC, regime risk-off) and docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-23-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-23, timestamp_utc 20:00:37Z, VHM/VIC/VCB, regime carry-unwind-risk-off). NOTE the historical convention was the UTC/trading-day label — published:chef-evening:2026-07-21 was claimed 2026-07-21T19:51:10Z i.e. VN 07-22 — so the 19:55Z run followed PRECEDENT while the 20:01Z run followed the SPEC AS WRITTEN. Neither agent misbehaved. The spec is ambiguous exactly at the boundary it is supposed to defend.

WHY THIS IS **NOT** UC-CCA-P3 — DO NOT FOLD AND CLOSE. UC-CCA-P3 fixes marker LIFECYCLE (claim timing + release immunity). Its design recommendation (early read-only probe + late task_claim immediately before send_telegram + never release) would NOT have prevented this incident: both peers would still compute DIFFERENT keys, both probes would read free, both late claims would succeed, both would publish. Key AGREEMENT is orthogonal to key LIFECYCLE. A mutex whose key depends on which timezone the reader happens to consult is not a mutex. If UC-CCA-P3 ships alone, this defect survives and the umbrella closes green — the recurring-detection-vs-recurring-FAILED-FIX class (feedback_recurring_detection_vs_recurring_failed_fix).

PO RULING (product decision, po-owned, decided 2026-07-22 — DO NOT re-litigate; architect/ba own the HOW, not the WHAT). The dedup key and the human-readable date label are TWO DIFFERENT VALUES and MUST NOT be derived from one expression. chef.md L654 (CYCLE_DATE = WORK_DATE verbatim) deliberately couples them; that coupling IS the defect, not the fix — it was introduced by GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST to make the FILENAME deterministic and it silently made the MUTEX KEY timezone-dependent. (1) MUTEX KEY = window-anchored and timezone-free: derived from the scheduled cron fire-window expressed in UTC (shape e.g. published:<slot_id>:2026-07-22T19:45Z), NOT from any `date` call made by the executing agent. Two peers executing the same scheduled window MUST derive byte-identical keys with zero shared state beyond the cron expression. This is invariant to timezone, to VN/UTC midnight straddle, to DST, to host clock skew, and to run-start jitter within the window (19:55 vs 20:01). It needs NO trading-calendar lookup. NEVER put a trading-calendar / holiday lookup on the mutex path. (2) DISPLAY LABEL (metadata.date_vn, synthesis filename, prose) = the VN trading session the dish INFORMS. chef-evening fires after the prior VN close (08:00Z) and before the next VN open (02:00Z of D+1) and gates on macroIndicatorRefreshJob US macro data — it is a FORWARD preview; the slot's own dish_type is literally `evening_preview`. Therefore the correct label for a 19:45Z fire is the NEXT VN session = the VN wall date at fire time. Tonight's correct label is 2026-07-23; the 19:55Z run's date_vn=2026-07-22 is WRONG. Weekend/holiday note for ba: the cron is daily including weekends, so 'next VN session' is not the next calendar day on Fri/Sat/Sun fires — the LABEL MAY remain the plain VN wall date (simple, calendar-free); if a true session label is ever wanted it belongs in a SEPARATE display-only field and never in the key.

CAUTION for architect/ba: metadata.cycle_id is NOT a ready-made substitute — today's two runs emitted cycle_id evening-2026-07-22T19:56:00Z and evening-2026-07-22T20:00:37Z, i.e. cycle_id is keyed to RUN-START and diverges exactly like WORK_DATE does. RECOMMENDED PLUMBING (non-binding): the cowork dispatcher ALREADY holds the canonical window value — the fire-election lock cron:cowork:2026-07-22T20:00Z carries payload.tick — so pass the tick DOWN to the spawned agent instead of having the agent re-derive it; DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-T1-TICK-SNAPSHOT-WON-SLOTS (tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7, already in ready[]) is the natural carrier. Deriving-at-the-leaf is what created this bug class.

LIVE FORWARD HAZARD (self-healing — do NOT 'fix' it with lock surgery): published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 expires 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z, which is AFTER tomorrow's 2026-07-23T19:45Z fire. If tomorrow's run uses the UTC-date convention it derives :2026-07-23, finds it HELD, and SILENTLY SKIPS — a MISSED evening dish. If it uses the VN convention it derives :2026-07-24 and publishes. Tomorrow's outcome is a coin flip on which convention the spawned agent picks. So this ONE defect produces BOTH double-publish AND missed-publish. Both markers are deliberately LEFT IN PLACE: they are the evidence, and releasing published: markers is the known-wrong direction (feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish). Hazard self-clears 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z.

AC: (1) two peers spawned for the SAME scheduled window derive byte-identical MARKER_KEY regardless of host timezone, of VN-vs-UTC midnight straddle, and of run-start offset within the window; (2) the key contains NO value obtained from a `date` call made by the executing agent; (3) mutex key and display label are SEPARATE named values with separate derivations, and no later step re-derives either; (4) chef-evening's synthesis date_vn + filename carry the NEXT-VN-session label per the PO ruling above; (5) the fix applies to ALL cowork published: gates (chef-morning/intraday/eod/evening, digest-daily, digest-sunday, fb, market-watcher, news-scout, tnb-audit) — not chef-evening alone; the same straddle hits ANY slot whose UTC fire hour maps across VN midnight, and single-fire slots carry a 100800s TTL that outlives the next window; (6) RAW-verify by executing two same-window runs: exactly ONE claim succeeds, exactly ONE synthesis artifact exists for the window, exactly ONE MARKET post is emitted.

SEQUENCING: ships WITH UC-CCA-P3, not before and not after — lifecycle-without-key-agreement is defeated by divergent keys, key-agreement-without-lifecycle is defeated by leaked or released markers. architect should treat UC-CCA-P3 + this row as ONE design.

RECURRENCE 2026-08-06 (PO triage, 3rd+ confirmed instance of this key-derivation class). This row's own 2026-07-22 title predicted today verbatim: "the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the [next day's] 19:45Z dish". It did, 15 days later, while the row sat in BACKLOG.

SEQUENCE (every step RAW-verified, not agent self-report):
(1) 2026-08-05T19:51:57Z the scheduled chef-evening fired (cowork-schedule.json .slots[chef-evening].last_fired) and the session died mid-composition AFTER claiming published:chef-evening:2026-08-05 and BEFORE send_telegram. Router released that marker and re-dispatched a retry at ~19:52Z.
(2) The retry did not begin executing until 2026-08-06T06:34Z. THE 10h42m GAP IS NOT AN AUTH OUTAGE AND NOT A SCHEDULER STALL -- that was the initial triage hypothesis and it is wrong. It is macOS host sleep: `pmset -g log` shows a MAGICWAKE at 2026-08-06 08:34 CEST = 06:34Z, matching the retry's start instant exactly, and the agent's own runtime was only 175909ms (~2m56s). Do not design against a phantom auth/scheduler bug.
(3) On wake, chef.md Step 0.5 recomputed CYCLE_DATE_UTC = `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` = 2026-08-06, so the retry keyed published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 and published a degraded dish to MARKET at 06:37:25Z (msg id 1129, headline "Thi truong 5-6 thang 8"). docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-06-evening.json records quality_verdict="degraded", 0 clusters, gaps [gap:L2_US_macro_absent_no_gap_token] [gap:L3_VN_macro_incomplete] [gap:business_context_unavailable]. It landed 13h before its real 19:45Z window and while the VN session was still OPEN (06:37Z = 13:37 ICT, close is 15:00 ICT) -- an "evening" dish published mid-session.
(4) That marker then tombstoned tonight's legitimate 19:45Z fire (28h TTL, expiry 2026-08-07T10:37:25Z). PO manually released published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 at 2026-08-06T06:53Z to unblock it, RAW-verified absent from task_list_held afterwards. THAT MANUAL RELEASE IS THE THING THIS ROW MUST MAKE UNNECESSARY.

DECISIVE DESIGN INPUT -- THE CORRECT KEY IS ALREADY COMPUTED AND SITTING UNUSED. scripts/agents-flow/cowork-catchup-predicate.js (shipped under TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-1/-2) already emits per slot exactly the fields this row needs: scheduled_utc_time, scheduled_key_part, expected_publish_task_id. Executed live 2026-08-06T06:52Z it returned for chef-evening: scheduled_utc_time=2026-08-05T19:45:00.000Z, expected_publish_task_id=published:chef-evening:2026-08-05 -- i.e. the predicate ALREADY identifies the missed window as 08-05, which is precisely the key the retry should have used and did not. So the fix is not new date logic. It is:
  (a) propagate the nominal scheduled tick into the slot trigger_prompt (e.g. `slot=<id> scheduled_utc=<ISO8601>`), sourced from the values the predicate already produces;
  (b) make chef.md Step 0.5 derive CYCLE_DATE_UTC from that scheduled_utc when present, falling back to wall-clock ONLY for genuine ad-hoc runs. Because CYCLE_DATE_UTC is already the single canonical date-derivation point (chef.md:73 -- pinned once, reused verbatim at Step 7.6 synthesis filepath + metadata.date_vn and Step 8b notebook header), this lands in ONE place and simultaneously fixes the marker key, the synthesis filename and the dish's own date label;
  (c) add a lateness guard: when now - scheduled_utc exceeds the slot's freshness window, the run must publish under an explicit backfill label or abort -- never silently retarget to the current day. The predicate ALREADY implements this notion (catchup_eligible:false with reason "rolled_past_vn_date" / "freshness_window_exceeded"); reuse it, do not reinvent it.

GENERALITY -- DO NOT SCOPE THIS TO CHEF. Every guaranteed slot derives its published-marker key the same wall-clock way, so any delayed, retried or post-sleep execution of digest-daily, tnb-audit, fb-daily, digest-sunday has the identical failure. On this host (laptop, France) sleep is a routine nightly condition, so "execution delayed hours past the nominal tick" is the NORMAL case, not an edge case. Any fix that assumes prompt execution is already wrong.

review.title: cold-evict runs on EVERY dev-team tick and can never move a done[] row: the Step 5.5 trigger is a COUNT gate (done_n>10) while the done[] eviction is a COUNT-AND-AGE gate (rank>=keep_n AND older than 7d). Different axes, so the trigger is structurally unclearable by the action it fires. Compounded by 10 of 16 done rows carrying the literal string "unknown" as created_at, which string-sorts ABOVE every ISO date and pins them as permanently un-evictable.
review.status_note:
THREE COUPLED DEFECTS, all PO-verified at source 2026-07-25T14:50Z. Fix all three or the loop returns.

(A) POISON VALUE DEFEATS THE SORT — scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh:236. `sort_by(.created_at // "0000-00-00T00:00:00Z")` is a plain STRING sort, and the `//` alternative only substitutes when created_at is null/absent. It does NOT catch the literal string "unknown". 10 of the 16 live done[] rows carry created_at:"unknown" (ARCH-ORCH-F1, ARCH-ORCH-F2, ARCH-ORCH-QA, BCTC-CURRENT-404-INVESTIGATE, FDA-4, FDA-8, FU-LOCKSTORE-EXPIRED-GC, FU-PRESSURE-EMIT-DARK, FU-TICK-SNAPSHOT-EMIT-DARK, PM-ORCH-DASH-DECISION-DRILLDOWN). 'u' (0x75) > '2' (0x32), so after sort_by|reverse those 10 rank as the NEWEST rows, keys 0-9. They therefore consume the ENTIRE KEEP_RECENT_DONE=10 window and fail `.key >= keep_n` forever — even though they would PASS the age gate, because line 245's `try (created_at|fromdateiso8601) catch 0` maps them to epoch 0. The malformed value makes the oldest rows look newest. Schema permits it: orchStateSchema.ts:102 `created_at: z.string().optional()` — any string, no ISO-8601 refinement. No live writer of "unknown" found in scripts/ (grep clean), so this is legacy data, not an active producer.

(B) TRIGGER AND ACTION ARE ON DIFFERENT AXES — scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:368 fires Step 5.5 when ANY of {terminal_sprint_n>0, sprint_goal_terminal_n>0, done_n>10, dv_n>0}. Live right now: 0 / 0 / 16 / 0 — so `done_n > 10` is the SOLE live disjunct. The action it fires (orch-cold-evict.sh:242-247) evicts a done row only when `.key >= keep_n` AND created_at older than `now - DONE_MAX_AGE_DAYS*86400` (default 7d, line 66). A COUNT gate firing a COUNT-AND-AGE action cannot be self-clearing. Even with (A) fixed the loop RETURNS: the 6 well-formed done rows accumulated over 4 days (~1.5/day), so a 7-day age window holds ~10 rows on its own and done_n re-crosses 10 within roughly a week. (A) alone buys about seven days, not a fix.

(C) THE ACCEPTANCE INSTRUMENT ITSELF LIES — orch-cold-evict.sh:256 `[.task_board.done_verified // [] | .[].id // ""]`. jq's `//` fires when the LHS produces NO outputs, so on an EMPTY array this yields `[""]`, length 1. Live proof: done_verified is `[]` and signal_queue.archive is `[]`, yet --dry-run prints 'done_verified[] would evict: 1 items' and 'signal_queue.archive[] evict: 1 items'. Harmless for actual eviction (the `select(. != "")` at 258-260 drops the phantom) but it corrupts the exact report an operator or a test would read to decide whether a run did anything. Confirm with: jq -n '[[] | .[].id // ""]' -> [""]. Same shape guards n_evict_done at line 344. FIX (C) FIRST — the acceptance test for (A)/(B) reads this report.

review.trap_do_not_fix_it_this_way:
THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A SILENT REGRESSION. The tempting repair for (B) is 'make the trigger ask the action's own question' — fire only when a row would actually be evicted from done[]. DO NOT DO THAT WITHOUT WIDENING IT. Step 5.5's trigger has NO signal_queue term at all (preflight.sh:349-368 reads only active_sprints, sprint_goal.entries, done, done_verified), yet orch-cold-evict.sh DOES evict signal_queue.rows[] and signal_queue.archive[] — that is precisely what the 14:18Z commit did. Since preflight.sh:419 is the ONLY automated caller, the permanently-true done_n condition is, by accident, the sole thing that ever causes signal_queue to be swept. Narrow the trigger to the done[] predicate and signal-queue eviction stops being reached at all: a wasteful-but-harmless loop would become a silent bloat regression. The trigger must gain a signal_queue disjunct in the SAME change that tightens the done disjunct.
CURRENTLY DORMANT BUT DO NOT USE THAT AS A REASON TO SKIP IT: signal_queue.rows[] is live 124 'triaged' + 1 'RETRACTED', and NONE of those are in TERMINAL_SIGNAL_STATUSES {READ,RESOLVED,SUPERSEDED,ACUTE-RESOLVED-ROOT-TRACKED} — so signal eviction is presently near-dead for a SEPARATE reason, owned by FIX-SIGNALQUEUE-TRIAGED-NO-EXIT-TRANSITION (minted 2026-07-25T14:07Z). review.acceptance:
(1) BICONDITIONAL, the core AC: after the fix, on the LIVE board, `Step 5.5 trigger fires` <-> `the run changes the hot file`. Demonstrate BOTH directions, not just one: (i) a tick where the trigger does NOT fire and --dry-run reports 'Byte reduction: 0 bytes'; (ii) a tick where the trigger DOES fire and the run reports a byte reduction > 0 with the evicted ids named. A gate is only meaningful if its input can cross the threshold in both directions (this is the standing generalisation on SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP).
(2) The 10 "unknown" created_at rows must reach a defined terminal state — either backfilled to a real ISO timestamp or evicted. 'Still pinned but now sorted differently' is NOT acceptance. Name the ids and show done[] length before/after.

review.title: Tier-1 A-30 memory check inspects 1 of 13 containers — hardcoded 'mcp-server' scope makes 11 capped containers permanently invisible to the only memory detector in Tier-1 (rag-service sat at 98.46% of cap while the same tick reported HEALTHY / 0 anomalies)
review.root_cause: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:209 _check_mem_creep() hardcodes its subject: ctr=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i 'mcp-server' | head -1). Line 211's failure string ('mcp-server container not found via docker ps') confirms the scope is deliberate-but-narrow, not an accident of parsing. The tuned WARN_PCT=85 predicate at :224 is then applied to that ONE container and nothing else. Tier-1 has no other memory check, at any threshold, for any other container — so 12 of the 13 running containers have ZERO memory coverage in the tier whose job is first-line health. DEMONSTRATED FALSE-PASS (router-verified, same tick): 2026-07-25 08:30Z Tier-1 reported 'A-30 Memory: 58.63% — PASS' + HEALTHY / 0 anomalies (commit 4280e27f5) while docker stats showed rag-service 727.8MiB/768MiB = 94.76%, rising to 756.1MiB = 98.46% by 08:45Z. Router 10-probe / 4-min window (08:48:04Z-08:52:01Z, 25s spacing): pinned 756.1-756.2MiB / 98.46%, ZERO reclamation dips; per-process VmHWM 775224kB > VmRSS 762236kB (reclamation HAD occurred earlier, so the flat line is a real plateau not a measurement artifact). Service was serving correctly throughout (docker health=healthy, FailingStreak=0, /health 200, /search 200, /index 200). PO re-verified at 08:56Z: rag-service 756.2MiB/768MiB 98.46%, mcp-server 1.708GiB/3GiB 56.94%, every other container <= 16.88%. NOT a threshold-tuning problem and NOT agent error — the check cannot look at the container, so no threshold value could ever have caught it. Script is clean in git (no uncommitted edits) and git log on it shows the last 3 commits touched launchd checks only (b9484fa7a, e0d9187cd, 84096f617) — the scope line is live and untouched.
review.deliverable: (a) SCOPE — replace the single grep'd container with a loop over EVERY running container that declares a memory cap. Resolve the set from the LIVE daemon, never a hardcoded name list and never docker-compose.yml (which is config-truth, not runtime-truth — the two already drift, see FU-RUNTIME-SET-TRUTH-RECONCILE). Discriminator VERIFIED live 2026-07-25T08:56Z: `docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} {{.HostConfig.Memory}}' $(docker ps -q)` returns a byte cap per container and exactly 0 for uncapped — today 12 capped + mcp-gateway at 0. SKIP the uncapped ones: docker stats reports their MemPerc against total host memory (mcp-gateway prints 0.27% of 7.753GiB), which is not a headroom signal and would be a meaningless comparand against WARN_PCT. (b) PREDICATE — apply the SAME already-tuned WARN_PCT=85 boundary per container. Do NOT introduce per-container threshold constants (see PO DECISION). (c) MESSAGE — the failure string must name the ACTUAL container(s) over the line; today :225 hardcodes the words 'mcp-server mem' so a widened loop would mislabel every other container's breach as mcp-server. Report all breaching containers in one detail line, not just the first. (d) Drop the `head -1` silent-multi-match on the resolution path — with a loop it is dead, and it was always a silent-truncation hazard. (e) LEDGER — extend the acknowledged-degraded suppression to memory (see PO DECISION), seeded with the rag-service entry.
review.note: PO DECISION — the router correctly flagged the design tension: rag-service's normal set-point IS legitimately high (98.46% flat, healthy, serving), so a flat 85% across all containers would manufacture a fresh every-tick false positive and re-open exactly the churn the DONE row FIX-AUDITOR-A12A20A30-FP-REEMIT-CONVERGE just closed. RESOLVE IT WITH THE ACK LEDGER, NOT WITH THRESHOLDS. The mechanism already EXISTS and is LIVE in this same script — FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION shipped it at commit b9484fa7a: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:255-330 reads docs/data/auditor-launchd-ack.json, and a listed condition that already has an OPEN backlog fix-row is reported as 'acknowledged-degraded (suppressed)' instead of flipping the verdict, WITH two guarantees that are exactly what is needed here: (1) mixed case never suppresses — an unacknowledged breach alongside acked ones still FAILS, so no permanent blindness; (2) a documented STALENESS RULE — the entry is removed once its tracked_by row reaches DONE_VERIFIED, so suppression cannot outlive the fix. Extend that ledger with a parallel acked_memory[] array (or a sibling docs/data/auditor-mem-ack.json) keyed by container/service name + tracked_by + acked_at, honouring the identical two guarantees, and SEED IT with rag-service tracked_by RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND. That single seed row is what makes a flat-85 loop safe on day one. EXPLICITLY REJECTED: per-container hardcoded threshold overrides. They are a static list that lags reality — the identical failure mode is already an open bug on this same probe family (FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX: a whitelist authored 2026-07-08 never learned a lock kind introduced 2026-07-19). review.title: RECURRING DATA LOSS: the notebook-write compose step silently REWRITES the content of RETAINED prior sections to pay for an over-cap current section, instead of trimming its own section first - and the skill has no immutability invariant, so a diff reviewer cannot tell authorized pruning from unauthorized rewriting
review.premise_correction_read_first: The incoming report framed this as 'zero deletions were required, it dropped 82 lines anyway', arithmetic from the commit's NET +43/-82 diffstat. THAT PREMISE IS WRONG and an implementer who chases it will fix nothing. The new section is 71L, not 43L; 152 + 71 = 223 > 200, so cap pressure was REAL and deletions WERE required. The defect is not that it deleted - it is WHICH bytes it deleted and that no rule forbids them.
review.measured_evidence: PO measured per-section line counts on both sides of 9b27e9723 (7 sections/152L -> 6 sections/113L). BEFORE -> AFTER: 05:08:58Z 81L -> 10L REWRITTEN; d4-auto 03:00 3L -> 3L intact; x1b5c2a9 02:33 25L -> 10L REWRITTEN; d986065c 00:42 10L -> DROPPED; 88ec89d6 00:36 14L -> 10L REWRITTEN; a1f7k9x5 23:39 10L -> 9L REWRITTEN; 60d26f9b 23:10 9L -> DROPPED; new section 06:09:36Z = 71L. So FOUR retained sections had their content silently rewritten, on top of two whole-section drops. The immediately-prior cycle's own audit record was compressed 81L -> 10L.
review.defect: THREE findings. (1) LADDER ORDER INVERTED: the new section is 71L against the AC-6 cap of <=60L per section. AC-3 Step 1f prescribes an ordered remedy whose FIRST step is 'If current-cycle section > 60L: trim to 60L first'. The agent skipped its own trim and paid the cap out of other sections' content. The spec-compliant outcome was reachable: trim 71->60 (212L), drop oldest 60d26f9b (203L), drop next-oldest a1f7k9x5 (193L) -> 5 sections, ~193L, every retained section BYTE-IDENTICAL. Actual outcome: 6 sections, 113L, four retained sections mutated. (2) NO IMMUTABILITY INVARIANT: nothing in AC-1..AC-6 of .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md states that retained sections are immutable. Steps 1c and 1f authorise DROPPING whole oldest blocks; no clause authorises editing a retained block's content, and no clause forbids it. Because AC-3 lands the result as ONE whole-file Write/Edit, both authorized pruning and unauthorized rewriting appear in the commit diff as plain deletions - they are indistinguishable to any reviewer. That is why this ran for multiple cycles unnoticed. (3) SPEC SELF-CONTRADICTION: AC-2 says 'Keep: current cycle + 2 prior sections = last 3 total', but AC-3 Step 1c says drop ONE oldest per cycle. Under Step 1c the section count is INVARIANT (add one, drop one), so AC-2's steady state of 3 is unreachable from above - this notebook sat at 7 sections, which AC-2 forbids and Step 1c permits indefinitely. Whichever is normative, the other is wrong.
review.acceptance: (1) The skill states an explicit IMMUTABILITY INVARIANT: sections retained across a cycle are byte-identical before and after. The ONLY authorized mutations are dropping a whole oldest block, the AC-2b intra-prune of a named permanent accumulator, and trimming the CURRENT cycle's own section. (2) AC-2 and AC-3 Step 1c are reconciled into one rule and the doc states which is normative. (3) The cap-pressure ladder ordering is made explicit and mandatory: trim own section to <=60L FIRST, then drop oldest whole blocks, NEVER mutate a retained section to make room. (4) A MECHANICAL check - runnable by the agent or a hook - that compares retained-section bytes before and after the settled write and fails if any surviving section changed. This is the AC that makes the class detectable at all; do not drop it for being harder than the prose ACs. (5) SCOPE FENCE: do NOT fix this in scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh. That is a DIFFERENT actuator (a PostToolUse hook running AFTER the write) and already carries its own 4-row REVIEW cluster: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH, FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNER-LINE-ONLY-SETPOINT-BYTE-CAP-NEVER-CONVERGES, FIX-NOTEBOOK-LINECAP-SWEEP-BYTE-BLIND-BACKSTOP, FIX-ALERT-COMMANDER-NOTEBOOK-SINGLE-BLOB-UNPRUNABLE. This row is the agent's IN-MEMORY compose step, AC-3 Step 1, which runs BEFORE the hook ever sees the file. (6) The fix applies to the shared skill and therefore to all 37 APPEND-class agents in AC-6, not to system-auditor alone.
review.blast_radius: .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md is the shared end-of-cycle write path for the 37 agents listed in its AC-6 APPEND class. If the compose step can rewrite retained history for system-auditor it can do so for all of them, and durable audit history is the one artifact the fleet cannot reconstruct.

review.title: SPIKE->FIX: get_cycle_bootstrap under-returns shared/broadcast chain_catalyst vs get_agent_signals (recurring 2+: 07-21 08:20Z, 07-22 04:29Z). Live probe: catalyst 8779 on bus + in alert-commander inbox but status='read'. get_cycle_bootstrap and get_agent_signals inbox-mode share getSignals(db,agent,{status:'unread'}) (agentSignalStore.ts:837) which mark-reads unread->read on read. Leading hypothesis: first consumer to bootstrap a shared/broadcast catalyst (to_agent='all' or multi-recipient) marks it read so later agents' bootstrap (unread-only) miss it; recovery only via non-consuming all-producers path (from_agent=null). SPIKE must (1) fetch created_at + to_agent of the missed rows across BOTH recurrences to rule out a pure timing artifact (signal created after the bootstrap call), then (2) decide fix direction: (a) bootstrap unions shared catalyst types via a non-consuming window, or (b) broadcast signals get per-recipient read-state / are not single-reader-consumed. review.title: sla-monitor's bctc threshold is NOT a policy constant — it rises 60min/hour in lockstep with the measured staleness, holding a fixed 5439-minute margin. The gate can therefore never clear and never escalates, and the 'threshold' value printed in every CRITICAL alert is meaningless.
review.status_note:
MECHANICALLY PROVEN, not inferred. PO extracted every bctc sla-monitor alert from list_unresolved_reports() over a 21-hour window (2026-07-24T17:00Z -> 2026-07-25T14:00Z, 12 samples) and differenced the two numbers in each message:
  stale=5950 thr=511 | 6010/571 | 6070/631 | 6160/721 | 6250/811 | 6340/901 | 6400/961 | 6550/1111 | 6700/1261 | 6910/1471 | 7090/1651 | 7210/1771
The set of (stale - threshold) values across all 12 samples is EXACTLY {5439}. One element. The threshold is not a duration policy — it is a second clock running 5439 minutes behind the first.

ISOLATED TO bctc, WHICH IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A GLOBAL MISREADING: in the same alert stream over the same window, every other metric's threshold is CONSTANT — bond_maturity 10080 (7d) in all samples, signal_quality_audit 2880 (48h) in all, news 30, sbv_fx 30. Only the bctc threshold moves. So this is a bctc-specific threshold computation, not a shared formatter bug and not an artifact of how the message is rendered.

HYPOTHESIS FOR THE ROOT CAUSE, stated as a hypothesis and NOT verified at source (PO did not read the sla-monitor implementation — the next agent must): a constant difference between two quantities that both grow with wall-clock time means BOTH are ages measured from `now` against FIXED timestamps, 5439 minutes apart. That is, the code is almost certainly comparing `now - T_data` against `now - T_other` — an AGE-vs-AGE comparison — where a correct SLA compares an AGE against a DURATION. Whoever picks this up should first confirm or refute that shape before changing anything; if it is refuted, the 5439 constant still has to be explained.

OPERATIONAL COST: the bctc breach re-fires roughly hourly and has done so continuously for at least 21 hours (almost certainly far longer — 3 samples/hour of bond_maturity + signal_quality_audit + bctc dominate the 100-row unresolved-report backlog). Because the margin is fixed, the alert carries zero information about whether the situation is improving or worsening: it will print CRITICAL with a larger pair of numbers forever.
review.relationship_to_adjacent_rows:
NOT a duplicate — PO checked the four adjacent bctc-freshness rows and all of them concern WHICH ROWS ARE MEASURED or WHICH LAYER IS MEASURED, none concerns the threshold being non-constant:
- FIX-BCTC-SLA-FRESHNESS-EXCLUDE-TERMINAL (backlog) — closest neighbour; excludes url_not_found terminal rows from the metric so genuinely-absent tickers cannot breach forever. That fixes the NUMERATOR (population). This row fixes the COMPARATOR. Both can be true at once and fixing either alone leaves the alert wrong.
- FIX-BCTC-QUEUE-MAXAGE-GATE (backlog) — drops >30d zero-result tickers from the active SLA queue. Population again.
- FIX-AUDITOR-B05-BCTC-FRESHNESS-LAYER-SPLIT (backlog) — B-05 applies a 24h SLA to the raw PDF-push layer instead of the analysis layer. That is the system-auditor plane, a DIFFERENT emitter from sla-monitor.
- SPIKE-FRESHNESS-REMEDIATE-TRIAGE (backlog) — designs the breach-triage layer; consumes SLA verdicts, does not compute them.
Sequencing note: if FIX-BCTC-SLA-FRESHNESS-EXCLUDE-TERMINAL lands first the staleness number will drop, but the threshold will still track it at 5439 and the gate will still never clear — so that row does NOT subsume this one.
review.acceptance:
(1) Read the sla-monitor bctc threshold computation at source and state in the closing report what the 5439 constant actually is. Do not change code before that sentence can be written.
(2) The bctc threshold must be a FIXED duration from config, asserted equal across at least 3 alert emissions separated by >1h — same property the other four metrics already satisfy today. Use bond_maturity/signal_quality_audit/news/sbv_fx as the positive control: whatever mechanism keeps THEIR thresholds constant is the one bctc should be using.
(3) BIDIRECTIONAL PROOF, not just 'it no longer fires': show the gate CLEARING on fresh data and FIRING on stale data. A threshold that can only ever be breached is the defect being fixed; a threshold that can never be breached is the mirror defect and is not acceptance either.
(4) Regression test pinning the bctc threshold to its configured constant, so this cannot silently drift back to a computed value.
(5) State the configured bctc SLA duration explicitly in the row closure. Nobody currently knows what the intended value is — the alerts have been printing a moving number, so the real policy has never been visible.
review.files_hint: sla-monitor threshold config + the bctc freshness check in apps/mcp-server (locate via the alert string 'CRITICAL breach: bctc stale {N}min (threshold {M}min)'); compare against the bond_maturity / signal_quality_audit / news / sbv_fx threshold definitions in the same module, which are already correct and serve as the in-repo reference implementation.
review.review_note:
AC-1 (read source before changing anything): confirmed PO's hypothesis exactly, not refuted. getSlaThreshold("bctc")'s active branch (non-trading-day / out-of-earnings-window off-hours) returned minutesSinceLast{WindowEnd,EarningsWindowEnd}(now) + OFF_HOURS_GRACE_MINUTES(30) -- literally `now - T_anchor` for a FIXED past anchor timestamp (last VN market-session close, or last earnings-window close). ageMinutes itself is `now - T_data` for the FIXED timestamp of the last real financial_reports row. Both are AGES growing 1:1 with wall-clock `now`, so ageMinutes - thresholdMinutes = (T_anchor - T_data) - grace is a time-invariant constant for as long as no new bctc data arrives and the day/hours regime doesn't flip -- a breach recorded in that regime can NEVER self-clear by the passage of time alone. Algebraically verified against PO's exact 5439 sample: over the 2026-07-24T17:00Z->2026-07-25T14:00Z window every "now" fell inside the same VN-Saturday non-trading-day regime, T_anchor = 2026-07-24T08:59Z (last Friday market close), backing out T_data ~= 2026-07-20T13:50Z (last real bctc parse) -- internally consistent with the reported stale=5950min at the first sample.

The false-CRITICAL-during-quiet-period concern the removed dynamic formula was chasing is now the sole job of the already-shipped queue-depth+service-state idle/crash gate (checkSignalSla, FIX-HEALTH-RECHECK-BCTC-IDLE-VS-CRASH) -- strictly more accurate (real pipeline state vs calendar guesswork) and already short-circuits before the threshold is ever consulted.

review.title: orch-state `blocks` AND `co_edit` are write-only — read by NO script, so any sequencing or atomic-ship guard expressed in them is decorative. PO authored one of each on 2026-07-25 believing both bound; neither did. 7 rows carry `blocks` (1 holds a prose paragraph instead of task ids), 2 rows carry `co_edit`
review.source: dev-team 16:37Z tick caught PO's own decorative guard on FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES; mechanism + full-repo reader grep + 7-row population + positive control independently re-verified at source by po
review.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T17:00:10Z by po. Surfaced by the dev-team 16:37Z tick, which caught PO's own decorative guard; independently re-verified at source by po before minting. The reporter explicitly declined to mint and left the call to PO.

THE DEFECT. `blocks` reads as a sequencing constraint and binds NOTHING. It is write-only across the entire repo. An author who writes `blocks: ["X"]` on row A, intending "X must not start before A", has created zero enforcement — and, critically, has no way to tell the difference from a working gate by inspecting the board.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT RELAYED:
  - scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-141 — `effective_depends_on` unions ONLY the candidate row's own `.depends_on`, `.depends` and `.blocked_by`; inline first, then backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows. It never traverses a reverse edge from any other row.
  - :161-164 — `deps_satisfied` short-circuits `true` when the effective list is empty.
  - Full grep across scripts/lib/*.jq, scripts/devteam-*.jq, scripts/orch-*.mjs, scripts/orch-*.sh, scripts/agents-flow/*.sh: NO consumer of `blocks`. The only textual matches are unrelated test-assertion prose ("... blocks idle").

LIVE POPULATION — 7 rows carry the field, and the three states are instructive:
  - INERT-BUT-INTENDED (1): FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT -> FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES. This was PO's own guard, written 16:49Z today, believed binding, and it was not. Now repaired by writing the reciprocal `depends_on` inline on the target. THIS IS THE PROOF THE FIELD IS A TRAP: a caller whose entire job is board correctness used it wrongly on the same day, because nothing about it signals that it does not work.
  - ACCIDENTALLY-BINDING (1): RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND -> ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-REBUILD-CRON. This one DOES hold — but not because of the `blocks` edge. The target independently carries `blocked_by: ["ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-CRON-SAFETY-GATE", "RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND"]` and status BLOCKED. Positive control for the correct shape, and evidence that the correct shape is already known and used elsewhere in the same board. Verified at source rather than assumed.
  - MALFORMED (1): FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE's `blocks` value is not a task id or a list of them — it is a prose paragraph beginning "PUSH-AUTONOMY-1. This standing red makes any literal '0 fail on the FULL suite' reading of the push gate permanently unsatisfiable...". A separate data-quality defect that only survives because nothing ever parses the field. It is IN SCOPE for this row: whichever remedy is chosen must not silently swallow a non-list value.
  - EMPTY / harmless (4): TASK_2006, TASK_2005, ALPHA-S2-SUB5-WATCHDOG-STRETCH, ALPHA-S2-FF-SUB6-BUCKETING-HELPER all carry `blocks: []`.

REMEDY — THREE HONEST OPTIONS, po did NOT choose:
  [a] MAKE THE GATE READ THE REVERSE EDGE — extend `effective_depends_on` to also scan every lane for rows whose `blocks` contains the candidate's id. Most faithful to author intent, and fixes all existing writers retroactively. Costs a full-board scan per candidate inside a hot eligibility predicate; measure before adopting.
  [b] MAKE `blocks` AN ALIAS — have scripts/orch-apply.sh mirror `A.blocks: [X]` into `X.blocked_by += [A]` at write time, so the reverse edge is normalised into the forward field the gates already read. Keeps the eligibility predicate untouched and cheap. Needs care: mirroring must be idempotent, must not fight a hand-written `blocked_by`, and must fail loud on a non-list value (see the malformed row above) rather than mirroring garbage.
  [c] DELETE THE FIELD — strip `blocks` from all 7 rows and forbid it, forcing every sequencing intent through `depends_on`/`blocked_by`. Smallest surface, but discards genuinely useful documentation-of-intent and does nothing to stop the next author reaching for an intuitive name.
WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE is leaving a field that reads as a constraint in every board dump while binding nothing. If [c] is chosen, the deletion must be paired with something that makes the mistake loud — see acceptance 3.

SCOPE ITEM DISCOVERED WHILE REPAIRING THE INSTANCE — A SECOND WAY DEP GATES CAN SILENTLY OPEN. scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh defaults `STUB_FIELDS="id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref"`. `depends_on`, `depends` and `blocked_by` are NOT in the keep-set, so a re-run strips inline deps out of hot rows. That is normally survivable because `effective_depends_on` falls back to backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows — BUT the strip is documented idempotent with "existing cold wins" (docs/policies/dev-standards.md), so a row whose cold entry already carries `depends_on: null` (as FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES does today) would lose the inline value while the stale cold null survives. Net effect: a dependency that was set correctly, later silently unset by an unrelated maintenance migration. Either add the three dep field names to STUB_FIELDS, or make the cold-merge non-clobbering for dep fields specifically. This belongs here because it is the same failure mode by a different route: a gate that is present in the author's mental model and absent from the machine's.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A sequencing intent expressed the way PO expressed it at 16:49Z (reverse `blocks` edge only, target row otherwise unconstrained) either BINDS or is REJECTED AT WRITE TIME. It must not be silently accepted and ignored.
  2. The existing 7 `blocks`-carrying rows are each dispositioned — migrated, normalised, or deleted — with the malformed FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE prose value handled explicitly rather than crashing or being swallowed.
  3. NEGATIVE CONTROL, and this is the criterion that distinguishes a real fix from a cleanup: after the change, deliberately author a new reverse-only `blocks` guard and demonstrate that it is caught — by binding, by a validation error, or by a loud warning. A remedy that only fixes today's 7 rows leaves the trap armed for the next author.
  4. STUB_FIELDS (or the cold-merge rule) preserves `depends_on`/`depends`/`blocked_by`, verified by running the stub migration over a fixture row carrying an inline dep and asserting the dep still binds afterwards.
  5. Do NOT hand-edit docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json as part of this — 761KB, outside the orch-apply validation gate.

CROSS-REF, NOT A NEW INSTANCE: this is adjacent to SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP (ready/P1) but deliberately NOT filed as an instance there. That row's class is gates whose INPUT cannot cross a threshold; here there is no gate at all — the field simply has no consumer. Filing it there would dilute a class that row has carefully bounded. The transferable lesson does belong in that SPIKE's findings doc as one line, however: A FIELD'S EXISTENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A CONSUMER — when auditing any guard expressed as data, grep for its READER before trusting it.
review.po_stubfields_scoping_20260725T1715: po 2026-07-25T17:15:22Z — SCOPING RULED, per the reporter handing this sub-item to PO. The STUB_FIELDS residual is IN SCOPE for this row and the cheap remedy is ENDORSED: add depends_on, depends and blocked_by to the STUB_FIELDS default at scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh:57 (currently id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref). Independently re-verified: the script contains ZERO occurrences of any dep field name, and combined with its documented existing-cold-wins merge, a re-run would strip an inline dep from a hot row while a stale cold null survives — silently re-opening a gate that was set correctly. One line, no cold-file surgery.
