review.title: bctcReparseJob: double-wrap recordJobRun + ungated restart catch-up defeat the T4 cadence guard's evidentiary trail
review.detail: Found during SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY AC-2 (findings docs/spikes/SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY.md). runBctcReparseWithDb (apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/startupHelpers.ts:361-366) wraps recordJobRun(db,'bctcReparseJob',fn) where fn discards runBctcReparseJob()'s real ReparseRunResult (Promise<void> arrow fn) -- so cron_job_runs.rows_written is ALWAYS NULL for this job (RAW-confirmed live: 100% of ~90 sampled rows across 11 days, 2026-07-29). Worse: recordJobRun marks the row 'success' whenever fn() resolves without throwing, REGARDLESS of whether runBctcReparseJob()'s OWN shouldSkipRecoveryReplay guard (bctcReparseJob.ts:718) early-returned a no-op -- so a guard-SKIPPED invocation still writes a fresh 'success' row, silently re-arming its own 21.6h dedup window. This is the SAME double-wrap class already found+fixed for runBaseRateComputationWithDb (FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD, 2026-07-23) and runEvidenceAccumulatorWithDb (EVIDENCE-ACCUM-SILENT-CRON) -- bctcReparseJob was never patched. It uniquely compounds with a SECOND defect: the startup catch-up in startScheduler.ts:169-182 fires runBctcReparseWithDb(db) UNCONDITIONALLY 30s after every container boot/restart with NO staleness gate -- its own introducing commit (75b729183, 2026-04-12) claimed to mirror runDailyAuditIfStale's pattern (dataAuditJob.ts:292-311, which correctly checks last_daily_audit_at age before running) but never implemented an equivalent check. Net effect, RAW-confirmed live (docker exec, market.db, last 30 days): 2-7 cron_job_runs rows per calendar day for bctcReparseJob (vs. the intended 1x/day), overwhelmingly 0-3ms duration (guard-skip echoes) with occasional real multi-hour runs, plus status='crashed' zombie rows on restart-cluster days (2026-07-19, 2026-07-28) -- the table's 'last success' signal is contaminated by boot-time noise unrelated to real reparse activity, and is the best-supported explanation for the 2026-07-10 incident this SPIKE investigated (ops' pre-edit probe showed clean, then a subsequent restart re-armed the guard within 30s, before ops resorted to falsifying 25 rows instead of using the job's own nowMsFn override).
review.ac: (1) runBctcReparseWithDb gains its own shouldSkipRecoveryReplay(db,'bctcReparseJob',DAILY_CADENCE_MS) check BEFORE calling recordJobRun (mirrors the FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD fix pattern exactly) so a guard-skip never reaches recordJobRun and never writes a fresh row. (2) fn's default implementation captures runBctcReparseJob()'s real ReparseRunResult and maps resolved+failed to rowsWritten (or an equivalent field) so cron_job_runs.rows_written is no longer always NULL for this job. (3) startScheduler.ts's bctcReparseJob startup catch-up (currently unconditional, :169-182) gains a staleness gate consistent with its own stated intent to mirror runDailyAuditIfStale -- either reuse shouldRunCatchup() (matching the other 5 hardened catchups in the same file) or an equivalent last-run-age check, so a restart does not unconditionally fire the job every single boot. (4) new unit tests proving both fixes through the real default code paths (mirror FIX-BASE-RATE-COMPUTATION-CRON-DEAD.test.ts's approach) -- specifically a test that 2 back-to-back invocations within the cadence window produce exactly 1 cron_job_runs row, not 2. (5) RAW-verify post-fix: cron_job_runs rows-per-day for bctcReparseJob drops to <=1 on days without a genuine multi-file reparse, and rows_written is populated (non-NULL) on real runs.

review.title: signal_quality_audit has had ZERO writes for 55 days (last row 2026-06-05T20:13Z, 6 rows lifetime) because its write gate keys on finding_data.confidence being a number — a field the highest-volume emitter's own contract does not require. FIX-SLA-...-MISCLASSIFIED-48H widened the alarm threshold to 30d and correctly left the CRITICAL firing; nothing owns the condition that makes it fire, so it re-emits ~1/hour forever.
review.detail:
PO triage 2026-07-30T19:07Z (report-queue pass). NOT a false-positive — the alarm was sanity-checked first and PASSED three independent ways: (a) 40 alert samples spanning 2026-07-28T16:00Z..07-30T19:30Z back out to ONE fixed epoch, 2026-06-05T20:13Z, agreeing to within 6 seconds between the oldest and newest sample — a broken baseline drifts, this one is a fixed anchor with a monotonic clock; (b) the threshold is CONSTANT across every sample (2880, then 43200 after the fix landed 07-30T09:00Z), unlike the known-broken sibling metric FIX-SLA-BCTC-THRESHOLD-TRACKS-STALENESS-NOT-CONSTANT where (stale - threshold) was a fixed 5439 constant proving an age-vs-age comparison — here the margin grows, so the comparison is well-formed; (c) dev-mcp-server independently queried the live named-volume market.db for the sibling row and reported 'zero rows since 2026-06-05T20:12:12Z', matching the arithmetic to the minute by a different method.

WHY IT IS DEAD, read at source (not inferred). The table's only writer is insertSignalQualityAudit() (infrastructure/db/signalQualityAuditStore.ts), reached from exactly one call site: post_agent_signal's handler at interface/mcp/tools/news-analysis/agentSignalTools.ts:455-500. Three preconditions must ALL hold: (1) the signal was not dedup-suppressed — note the `if (id <= 0) { ... return }` early-return sits ABOVE the audit block, so every dedup-suppressed post skips the audit silently; (2) signal_type is price_confirmation or urgent_news; (3) typeof finding_data.confidence === 'number'.

The suspected structural break is (3) against the emitter contract. domain/signals/signalTypes.ts makes confidence REQUIRED for price_confirmation (:159 z.number().min(0).max(1)) but OPTIONAL for urgent_news (:217 .optional()), and docs/agents/tools/package/news-scout.md:66 documents urgent_news's required finding_data as headline/source/severity — confidence is NOT in the documented required set. So a fully-compliant news-scout urgent_news post never trips the audit write. docs/agents/tools/list/get_signal_effectiveness.md shows urgent_news at 58 recorded signals; the audit table has 6 rows LIFETIME. price_confirmation, the one type that does mandate confidence, does not appear in that effectiveness sample at all.

BOTH failure modes are silent by construction: agentSignalTools.ts:499 catches and console.warn's ('non-fatal'), and signalQualityAuditStore.ts:78 catches and console.warn's again. Two swallow layers, no counter, no alarm. The SLA monitor is the only thing that ever noticed.

WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY OWNED — checked both adjacent rows, neither covers it: FIX-SLA-SIGNALQUALITYAUDIT-MONTHLY-CADENCE-MISCLASSIFIED-48H (REVIEW/qa) is a threshold change and its own freshnessSlaChecker.ts:209-211 comment states the current gap 'still fires under the new value' BY DESIGN; FIX-MONTHLYSIGNALQUALITYAUDITJOB-MISSED-JULY-RECOVER-GUARD (BACKLOG/P3) is about monthlySignalQualityAuditJob, which orch-state's own note at :10859 says verbatim 'never writes to the signal_quality_audit table'. So the sign-off path currently closes both neighbours while the condition persists.

OPERATIONAL COST: 39 of the 179 unresolved Telegram reports PO cleared this tick (22%) were this one alarm, arriving ~1/hour. It is the single largest cluster in the queue and it regenerates unboundedly.

CAUTION for whoever picks this up — the 30d threshold in freshnessSlaChecker.ts was sized off '6 rows total ... real gaps of >2 weeks between them even in a healthy period'. If the capability never worked, there was no healthy period and those 6 samples are noise, not a cadence. Do NOT re-tune the threshold again off the same 6 rows; establish first whether the write path is reachable at all.
review.ac:
(1) STATE THE MECHANISM BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. Determine which of the three preconditions actually blocks the write in production and say so in the closing report. Cheap decisive probe: count agent_signals rows with signal_type IN ('price_confirmation','urgent_news') since 2026-06-05 and, for those, how many carry a numeric finding_data.confidence. Three distinguishable outcomes: (a) zero such signals posted -> the emitters are dead and THIS row is the wrong fix, re-file against the emitter; (b) signals posted but confidence absent/non-numeric -> the emitter-contract gap named above is confirmed; (c) signals posted WITH numeric confidence but no audit row -> the insert itself is failing and the two console.warn swallows are hiding it. Do not guess between these.

(2) DECIDE WIRE-OR-RETIRE, EXPLICITLY. Either the capability is wanted (then make the write path reachable for the signal types that actually flow, and align docs/agents/tools/package/news-scout.md + signalTypes.ts so the emitter contract and the audit trigger agree) or it is not (then REMOVE signal_quality_audit from DEFAULT_SLA_CONFIG entirely — an SLA on a table nothing writes is pure noise). A third threshold widening is not an acceptable outcome.

(3) MAKE THE SWALLOWS OBSERVABLE. At minimum the two non-fatal catches (agentSignalTools.ts:499, signalQualityAuditStore.ts:78) must increment something a probe can read, so a future 55-day dead spot is detectable without waiting on an SLA alarm. Same class as feedback_composite_score_masks_dead_detector_pruned_table.

(4) BIDIRECTIONAL PROOF, not 'the alarm stopped'. If wiring: show an audit row actually landing from a realistic post_agent_signal payload AND still absent when the precondition legitimately fails. If retiring: show the SLA entry gone and assert no other consumer reads the table (233-cowork-resilience-e2e.test.ts:393 asserts on signal_quality_audit — reconcile it or explain why it passes against an empty table, which is itself a finding).

(5) Regression test pinning whichever decision is made, so this cannot silently revert to a dead-table-plus-tuned-threshold state.

review.title: The escalation actuator shipped in eac71308e is ALREADY past threshold for 2 live sessions the moment it landed: prior_warns counts the ENTIRE historical .git/sweep-guard.log with no time window and no deploy baseline, so it is a de-facto instant fleet-wide reject flip — the exact flip the brief deliberately staged as a Phase-2 with 24h observation + rollback. Compounding it, `actor` is $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, which every subagent of one router session SHARES, so it can never scope to an agent.
review.root_cause: TWO defects in one block, `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit:487-506`. (D1) RETROACTIVE, UNWINDOWED COUNTER: line 500 `prior_warns=$(grep -Fc " actor=${actor} " "$LOG_FILE")` counts every BARE line ever written for that actor. The log is append-only and nothing prunes or windows it (`post-commit` only appends `correlated sha=` lines, which carry no `actor=` and so do not double-count). The actuator therefore inherited a pre-existing backlog at deploy time instead of starting from zero. (D2) ACTOR != AGENT: line 487 `actor="${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-...}"`. In Claude Code every subagent spawned from one router session inherits that same session id, so router/dev-team/pm/po/developer/architect/qa all report as ONE actor. T8's shipped property ('a different actor's first BARE commit in the same repo still only warns') is true in a scratch repo where the test fabricates distinct ids, and vacuous in production. Consequence: a first-time-offending agent inherits every peer's strikes, so the actuator converges SESSIONS, not offenders — which is precisely the fleet-wide behaviour the brief's own rationale ('WITHOUT waiting on a fleet-wide reject-mode flip') claimed to avoid.

review.title: 80-page OCR cap vs 50%-completeness threshold: 3 large PDFs never finish extraction, full re-OCR every boot

review.desc:
pdfOcrWorker.ts:extractAndStorePdfPages hard-caps OCR at 80 pages (line ~261, maxPages = Math.min(totalPages, 80)) but the completeness re-extraction gate (line ~217-219, threshold = Math.max(expectedPages * 0.5, 3)) checks the CAPPED extracted-page count against the UNCAPPED expected page count. For any PDF with totalPages > 160, 80 < threshold forever — the extraction is judged perpetually incomplete, DELETED (db.run "DELETE FROM pdf_extracted_text WHERE filename = ?") and re-OCR'd from scratch, capped at 80 again, on EVERY call — i.e. every single composition-root bootstrap OCR loop run (composition-root.ts §4b), forever, with zero possibility of ever satisfying the threshold.
LIVE CONFIRMED on vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1, 2 consecutive boots (2026-07-30T22:07:03Z, 2026-07-31T00:56:46Z), identical shape both times: GVR_2026_Q1.pdf (totalPages=204, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=102), GVR_2025_Q4.pdf (totalPages=285, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=142.5), 000000013535084_20240328__MSN__Bao_cao_thuong_nien_2023compressedsigned.pdf (totalPages=255, extracted pinned at 80, threshold=127.5) — DB query (bun:sqlite against /app/data/market.db) confirms all 3 sit at exactly c=80 rows, never advancing across boots. Each re-OCR burns ~10-12 real minutes of sequential tesseract CPU (bracketed via consecutive "[pdfOcr] starting" log timestamps) on every boot; combined they are the dominant driver of the ~33min (22:07:03Z -> 22:40:10Z) bootstrap-OCR wall-time observed despite 271/279 other PDFs being fast-skip cache hits.
WORSE than pure waste: the DELETE happens BEFORE re-extraction, so any concurrent read_bctc_pdf / getCachedPdfText call against these 3 filenames during the ~10-12min re-OCR window sees ZERO cached pages (previously-available 80 pages deleted, new 80 not yet reinserted) instead of the stale-but-present partial text — a real availability regression window on every single boot, not merely CPU waste.

review.title: Batch telegram analysis reports or suppress duplicates
review.promotion_note: BOUNDED-1 idle-capacity backlog pickup — WIP (in_progress) was 0; promoted top-priority unsupervised depends_on-eligible BACKLOG/TODO row (priority_rank=3)
review.review_note:
ROOT CAUSE RE-VERIFIED before coding (mandatory per dispatch brief), and the brief's own hypothesis was CORRECT: Task 1792's bctc_signal_debounce table only debounces the SAME (action_code, period_key) within a 1h rolling window (retry-storm case — 10 calls in 3 minutes) -- it is a PARTIAL fix, not the full fix. It does nothing for bctcReparseJob.ts, which runs DAILY at 09:30 GMT+7 and retries the same still-broken low-confidence backlog every single day, 24h apart, well outside 1792's 1h window. Each daily cycle therefore re-fires the exact same [BCTC-1345b] Telegram bug alert for a ticker+period that was ALREADY known/tracked the day before -- that daily re-fire (not same-minute retry storms, which 1792 already fully solved) is the actual source of the backlog note's "6 reports today / 11 more the next day, all same low-confidence-guard class" noise. No separate "quality chain" cross-ticker suppression mechanism exists elsewhere (checked telegramReportStore.ts's Task-1215 category dedup in telegram.ts's sendTelegramBug: it exists, is generic and DB-backed, but requires a "checkbox-emoji category" marker in the message text that the [BCTC-1345b] message does not carry, so it never engages for this alert; also its 4h window is shorter than the 24h reparse cadence and it would over-suppress genuinely-new-ticker findings sharing a category within the window -- rejected for that reason too).

FIX (parseBctcReport.ts storeReport()): before sending the [BCTC-1345b] alert, query financial_reports.validation_status for the exact same (action_code, sort_key). If it is ALREADY 'low_confidence' from a PRIOR parse, suppress the Telegram send (the row still upserts as normal -- audit trail / validation_status tracking untouched). Reuses the existing validation_status column already on financial_reports -- zero new table/migration. Self-closing by construction: the moment a later re-parse produces real confidence, validation_status flips off 'low_confidence' and a future genuine regression will alert again (proven by test 3 below). 1792's 1h debounce is left fully in place underneath (belt-and-suspenders for the same-minute race case); this task's gate is a superset, not a replacement.

Options considered and rejected: (a) PO note's "batch per-cycle" digest -- no existing cycle-boundary primitive to hook into in this codebase; XS/P3 size does not justify inventing new batching infra for a P3/XS row. (b) tagging the [BCTC-1345b] message with a category marker to piggyback Task-1215's generic telegram.ts dedup -- rejected for the reasons above (window too short + over-suppression risk across genuinely-different tickers).

TESTS (new file FIX-BCTC-1345B-REPORT-BATCH.test.ts, 3 cases): (1) REGRESSION -- ages the 1792 debounce row back 2h (simulating bctcReparseJob's next daily cycle, debounce window already expired) then re-parses the SAME already-low-confidence ticker+period; RED genuinely confirmed via git stash of the fix alone (2 Telegram sends observed, expected 1) then GREEN after restoring the fix (exactly 1 send). review.title: [BCTC-1345b] alert hard-codes 'Check for OCR corruption (VNM/VEA pattern: assets<equity or margin>100%)' but financial=0.10 is emitted ONLY by the unit-mismatch short-circuit that bypasses those rules entirely — 65 live rows (23 tickers) each send the triager to a rule family that provably cannot return 0.10
review.desc:
MEASURED, not inferred.

ROOT CAUSE. parseBctcReport.ts:737-741 computes confidence_financial as a ternary: when detectUnitMismatch(totalAssets, netRevenue) (cross-statement, >1000x) OR detectBsIntraStmtUnitMismatch(totalAssets, totalLiabilities) (intra-BS, >100x) fires, it SHORT-CIRCUITS to the literal 0.1 and validateFinancialFigures() is never called. The alert built at parseBctcReport.ts:275-279 then tells the reader to check the VNM/VEA patterns -- but those are BCTC-VAL-01 (assets<equity) and BCTC-VAL-03 (margin>100%), both implemented INSIDE the validateFinancialFigures() call that was just skipped.

PROOF THE HINT IS UNREACHABLE FOR THIS VALUE. Brute-forced validateFinancialFigures over 160,000 input combinations (totalAssets/totalEquity/totalLiabilities/netRevenue x 10 values each, operatingMargin x 16): the ONLY outputs it can ever return are {0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}. It returns 0.1 ZERO times. Documented VNM pattern (assets 957 << equity 18829, revenue 63645) -> 0.8; same without the >30x-revenue escape -> 0.0; documented VEA pattern (margin 3.3 = 330%) -> 0.8. None is 0.10. Therefore financial=0.10 is a UNIQUE, unambiguous fingerprint of the unit-mismatch branch and NEVER of the two patterns the alert names.

SECOND DEFECT -- DEAD FLOOR. financialFiguresValidator.ts:306 'return Math.max(confidence, 0.1)' and its docstrings at :28 and :177 ('soft violations stack, floor at 0.1') describe a floor that cannot be reached: max stacked soft penalty is 0.6, because BCTC-VAL-01's guard requires totalEquity>0 while BCTC-VAL-06 requires totalEquity<0, so those two can never both fire. Minimum non-hard-fail output is 0.4. The 0.1 in the docstring is what makes the collision with the unit-mismatch sentinel invisible on reading.

LIVE BLAST RADIUS (market.db via runtime container, 2026-08-01T06:2xZ). confidence_financial distribution over 221 non-null rows: 1.0 -> 121, 0.1 -> 65, 0.8 -> 18, 0.0 -> 17. Note 0.4 and 0.6 have ZERO rows, and 0.1 is the 2nd most common value at 29.4%. All 65 came through the unit-mismatch branch (independently corroborates the brute-force). 23 distinct tickers. Sub-detector split over those 65: cross-statement only 44, intra-BS only 11, both 7, neither-now 3.

TRIGGERING INSTANCE. NVL 2026-Q2, parsed_at 2026-08-01T05:52:14.418Z: total_assets=420322071420, total_liabilities=0, equity_total=0, net_revenue=31, extraction_confidence=0.375, confidence_financial=0.1, validation_status=low_confidence. assets/revenue ratio = 1.4e10 -> detectUnitMismatch fires (raw VND vs trieu VND). assets>equity, so the VNM signature the alert names is ABSENT; the VEA margin rule was never evaluated. Contained at serve time only INCIDENTALLY: get_bctc_full returns 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' via PUB-1 (refine_status=PENDING, not DONE/PARTIAL) -- NOT via any corruption guard. checkBctcIdentityGuard's predicate (total_assets<=0 OR total_assets<equity_total) passes this row, since equity_total=0 makes assets>=equity trivially true.

AC-1: the [BCTC-1345b] message must name the detector that ACTUALLY fired -- cross-statement unit mismatch (assets/revenue ratio R), intra-BS unit mismatch (assets/liabilities ratio R), or the specific BCTC-VAL-NN rule -- with the offending figures. No hard-coded ticker-pattern hint.
AC-2: the VNM/VEA hint may only appear on values that rule family can actually return (0.0/0.8).
AC-3: resolve financialFiguresValidator.ts:306. Either delete the unreachable floor and correct the :28/:177 docstrings, or keep it and move the unit-mismatch sentinel off 0.1 so the two stop colliding. Do NOT silently leave both.
AC-4: regression test asserting the unit-mismatch alert text does NOT contain the VNM/VEA string, and that a genuine BCTC-VAL-01/03 alert does.
AC-5: NON-GOAL -- this row does NOT fix the underlying unit normalisation (no open row owns that; the 2026-06-07 commit 06c65978c added the DETECTOR only) and does NOT repair the 65 existing rows. Scope is alert truthfulness + the dead floor.

PRIOR ART CHECKED. FIX-BCTC-1345B-REPORT-BATCH (review[], next_agent=qa) touches the same emission block but is about VOLUME/dedup, not text correctness -- its verdict must not be read as making this alert accurate. FIX-BCTC-VALIDATION-GATE-NONBANK-ZERO-SCALE (backlog, architect) is the serve-time validation_status label, not the alert. Recurrence is established (4 fires, 2 audit cycles), so this is past the single-fire observation threshold.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN AN OBSERVATION: the mismatch runs in BOTH directions. 4412 and 4415 have the marker above the re-read; 4420 has the re-read above the marker. The emitted resolution — "Trusting the higher (real-artifact) value" — is therefore not a conservative fallback, it is arbitrary: it picks a different source on different cycles, so the number the auditor finally reports is not attributable to any one plane. An agent self-report whose reconciliation rule is direction-dependent is exactly the class flagged in feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation, and it is being used to attest that signal rows were written.

LIKELY BENIGN EXPLANATION TO RULE OUT FIRST (cheap, do this before any code change): .signal_queue.rows[] is a live hot structure that peer agents write to concurrently, so a marker parsed at time T and a re-read at time T+delta can legitimately differ if another agent appended or if a drain removed rows in between. If that is the whole story the fix is to snapshot once and compare within the snapshot, not to pick the larger number. Confirm or refute by timestamping both reads.

BUG A (explains 4412/4415, marker HIGHER): every tier's FIRE_TICK (main.md Step 0d, lines 140/147/152/165) is minute-precision ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"); every signal_queue row .ts (emit-audit-signal.sh:529) is second-precision ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"). review.title: FIX — rag-service compaction failure-path never resets _insert_count (repositories.py:251 reset is inside the try, after optimize()) => any compaction failure makes EVERY subsequent insert re-fire a full-table optimize(); bursts of ~20MiB rewrites inside 18.1 MiB of headroom kill the container as ExitCode=0/OOMKilled=false
review.root_cause: MECHANISM (PO-verified by execution 2026-07-29T10:20-10:28Z; supersedes DIAGNOSE-RAG-SERVICE-RESTART-LOOP). TWO STACKED CAUSES. (1) FIXED BASELINE EATS THE CAP: embedder.py _model is a lazy singleton (:37 init None, :51 _ensure_model_loaded) with NO release path — grep of apps/rag-service/**/*.py for unload|.release(|del self._model|gc.collect|empty_cache returns ONLY the :37 initializer, so once loaded the model is resident for the container's life. MEASURED on the live container: cold RSS 50.7 MiB (6.6% of 768 MiB); model load logged 10:24:28.5Z->10:24:48.9Z on the FIRST embed; docker stats immediately after, having served exactly ONE POST /index: 749.9 MiB / 768 MiB = 97.65%. HEADROOM 18.1 MiB. (The embedder docstring's '~600-700 MiB warm' understates live by ~50-150 MiB.) Cap was halved in 2dc1d8c4e (Wed Jun 10 2026, 'reduce memory limits to 512m/768m', diff -memory:1.5g/+memory:768m; rag block docker-compose.yml L165-171) for host-budget reasons and never re-validated against the model's fixed cost. (2) COMPACTION FAILURE-PATH DOES NOT RESET ITS COUNTER — this is a real code defect, NOT tuning. repositories.py compact() :237-259 puts 'self._insert_count = 0' at :251 INSIDE the try, AFTER 'await table.optimize(cleanup_older_than=...)' at :250; the except at :257-259 logs a WARNING and returns NORMALLY without resetting. insert() :230-235 wraps 'await self.compact()' in its own try/except whose handler DOES reset (:235 'self._insert_count = 0  # reset to avoid tight retry loop') — but that handler is UNREACHABLE because compact() already swallowed the exception. NET: on ANY compaction failure the counter stays >= _COMPACT_EVERY, so EVERY SUBSEQUENT INSERT re-fires a full-table optimize() until one attempt happens to win. The code's own comment names the exact failure it fails to prevent. LIVE PROOF of the burst: 2026-07-29T09:02:36.139Z / 09:02:36.140Z / 09:02:40.06Z / 09:02:43.13Z all 'compaction failed (non-fatal)' -> 09:02:44.17Z 'compaction complete' -> 09:02:44.75Z failed again = SIX full-table optimize() calls in 8.6 s. Failure modes seen: 'Retryable commit conflict for version 12326/12331: This Rewrite transaction was preempted by concurrent transaction Rewrite' and 'Object at location .../_versions/18446744073709542049.manifest not found'. The retry the engine explicitly asks for is never performed. review.title: dev-team pipeline-resume task_status/should_hold lookups are blind to terminal lanes — head stays in_progress on a done[] task and re-spawns the agent on finished work
review.status_note: ROOT CAUSE (from signal): docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md pipeline-resume task_status lookup (~line 263) queries only in_progress[] + active_sprints[].tasks[] — never done[]/done_verified[]/review[]/qa[]/ready[]/backlog[]. A gateway-less specialist closing its own head task can only write the lane, not .head (INV-GATEWAY-1), so .head stays {status:in_progress, active_task_id:<now-done task>}. Next tick's resume then reads task_status=empty (NOT 'BLOCKED', so the existing carve-out misses it), falls through the WF-2 supervised check (also terminal-lane-blind), and re-spawns the agent on already-finished work via the S2 dispatcher-wrap. LIVE INSTANCE 2026-08-06: architect closed GUARD-COWORK-NOTEBOOK-AGENTS-SELF-EDIT-FLOW-DOC to done[] (commit 336228ebe); .head stayed pinned at updated_at 2026-08-05T19:41:30Z until the router hand-patched it to idle at 07:14:28Z. That hand-patch is a DATA fix, not a code fix — recurrence is certain without this row. AC: (1) task_status resolution scans terminal lanes and short-circuits to an idle-reset, mirroring the existing BLOCKED carve-out's self-heal shape; (2) the WF-2 should_hold predicate gets the same terminal-lane guard (po hit this independently the same tick — should_hold returned true for a task already in done[]); (3) regression fixture replays the live shape: head pinned in_progress at a done[]-lane task id => resume must idle-reset, NOT re-spawn. NEGATIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: a genuinely in-flight in_progress task must still resume normally — a fix that idle-resets everything trivially passes (1)-(3) and breaks the pipeline.
ac: AC-1 Add a terminal-lane check (done[] + done_verified[]) to BOTH the task_status lookup and the should_hold lookup, mirroring the shape of the existing BLOCKED carve-out's self-heal (~lines 267-285) rather than inventing a new control-flow branch.
AC-2 On a terminal-lane hit, short-circuit to an idle .head reset — never fall through to S2 dispatcher-wrap. Write via scripts/orch-apply.sh per the hot-file write contract.
AC-3 Negative control: a head naming a row that is genuinely in_progress must still resume exactly as today. A head naming a BLOCKED row must still take the existing BLOCKED carve-out, unchanged.
AC-4 Positive control: replay this tick's exact shape (head.active_task_id = a done[] row, head.status=in_progress) and assert the resume path idles the head instead of spawning next_agent.

AC-5 Root-cause framing to preserve in the fix: the trigger is a gateway-less specialist closing its own head task (INV-GATEWAY-1), which is a NORMAL, supported condition — not an error path. The fix must not require the specialist to gain gateway access.

review.po_falsification_20260725T1507: po_falsification_20260725T1507: A "VN-Index frozen feed" report was raised this tick and PO REJECTED it as a weekend degenerate case. Recording the falsification here (closest in-scope row — this row governs whether a vnIndexDelta is trustworthy enough to reach MARKET) so the next observer does not re-raise it. CLAIM: bctc-analyst c119-c123 saw an identical vnIndexDelta of -13.27 across 5 consecutive cycles; router independently reproduced vnIndexDelta -13.27000000000021 via get_macro_snapshot. WHY IT IS NOT A DEFECT: 2026-07-25 is a Saturday and the last VN session closed Friday 2026-07-24. Every one of c120 (07-24T18:11Z), c121 (07-24T21:10Z), c122 (07-25T00:24Z), c123 (07-25T15:20Z) and the PO probe (07-25T15:24Z) falls AFTER Friday close. An unchanging index value across a closed market is the correct output, and an unchanging session-delta derived from it is likewise correct. COUNTER-EVIDENCE that the field is alive, not stuck: stored artifacts under docs/data + docs/signals carry vnIndexDelta values of 7.35, 2.07, -0.86, -7.08 and -20.68 — the field demonstrably varies day to day. THE ONE THING THAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, and is a useful input to this row rather than a separate task: prevFetchedAt reads 2026-07-24T21:15:04.625Z while vnIndexDelta stays -13.27. If the delta were computed against the value AT that prevFetchedAt (post-close, 1686.11) it would be 0, not -13.27. So the delta and its own stated anchor disagree about what the anchor is. On a closed market "delta = last session move, carried by design" and "delta is stale" produce byte-identical output and CANNOT be distinguished — per feedback_auditor_freshness_threshold_market_hours_blind and feedback_single_observation_degenerate_case_read_as_broken_mechanism, do not adjudicate it off-hours. RE-TEST INSTRUCTION for whoever implements this gate: probe get_macro_snapshot twice DURING a live session (VN market 02:15-07:45 UTC) and assert that vnIndexDelta recomputes against the advancing prevFetchedAt. If it does not, THAT is the real defect and it belongs in this row scope. NOT routed to market-watcher or ops.

Zero rows is therefore the ONLY shape a real outage (or a genuine all-zero session) can produce — and the surrounding try/catch also leaves foreignFlowMovers=[] on any DB error. foreignFlowSection.ts:21 answers that shape with `if (movers.length === 0) return []`, and eveningSummaryJob.ts:191 splats the result unguarded (`lines.push(...formatForeignFlowSection(...))`), so the entire "Khoi ngoai" section vanishes silently with no notice. The canonical unavailable copy lives one branch lower, at foreignFlowSection.ts:26-29, gated on movers.length > 0 AND every entry netVol === 0 — a set the `<> 0` SQL predicate cannot emit. franceSummaryJob.ts:434 is worse: it wraps the call in `if (foreignFlowMovers.length > 0)`, so even a future empty-path message would be suppressed there. INVERTS THE CLOSED ROW'S RESIDUAL FLAG: FIX-FOREIGN-FLOW-BULLETIN-UNAVAIL-STRING's router_note worried the unavailable copy could MISLABEL a genuine zero-net-flow day as an outage. Reading the query shows the opposite is what actually ships — a genuine outage is labelled as nothing at all, and the misleading branch is unreachable. review.title: agentBootstrap buildToolNameMap() singleton blocks on execSync git rev-parse -> cascading TDZ flake on 1299b + real cold-start risk (SPIKE item #1)
review.detail: SPIKE item #1 — the HIGH-severity follow-up that was dropped when items #2/#3/#4 were minted 2026-07-10 (FIX-CYCLEJOB-1294-FOLLOWUP-SWEEP, FIX-RAG-TEMPORAL-DECAY-TEST-JITTER, CI-PERFILE-STRUCTURAL-MITIGATION all exist; this one never got a row). Mechanism: agentBootstrap.ts:358 `const toolNameMap = buildToolNameMap()` eagerly + synchronously probes ~107 tool-registration fns at module top-level; registerAgentMemoryTools -> getProjectRoot() runs blocking execSync('git rev-parse --show-toplevel') (projectRoot.ts:16). Under CPU starvation the git fork stalls past bun's 5s per-test timeout; the mid-flight-errored ES module instance is then permanently TDZ-poisoned ('Cannot access toolNameMap before initialization'), cascading to every remaining test in the file (6/9 failed in worst reproduced run, 11/24 runs under contention per SPIKE). Also a genuine production cold-start latency risk: server.ts:40 imports agentBootstrap on the live MCP boot path and ~30 test files import it transitively (this is the 'rotating failing file' blast radius). FIX options: remove the subprocess from the eval path -> memoize project-root via import.meta.dir walk-up (no git spawn), OR make registerAgentMemoryTools' project-root resolution lazy (resolve at tool-invocation, not at the registration probe). AC: no execSync on the module-eval path + cold-start non-regression guard + all ~107 tool names resolve + 1299b 9/9 green + ~30 agentBootstrap-importer tests green. PLAN-ONLY backlog for BOUNDED-1 — do NOT dispatch this tick.

review.po_dataset_exceeds_cap_20260729T1140: DECISION INPUT for the resident-set trade, measured 2026-07-29T11:40Z, no action requested — but this one materially changes the shape of the trade, so read it before sizing anything. THE ON-DISK DATASET IS ALREADY LARGER THAN THE MEMORY CAP: data/live/lancedb = 785 MiB versus a 768 MiB cgroup limit (rag_entries.lance/data 596 MiB / 3137 fragments, _indices 145 MiB / 745 files, _versions 32 MiB, _transactions 12 MiB). Combined with the fixed ~700 MiB embedder singleton already recorded on this row at po_measured_input_20260729, the cap is being asked to hold a fixed model baseline AND the working set of a corpus that already exceeds the whole limit on its own, while the corpus grows ~103 rows/h and RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND is time-gated until it reaches ~56254 rows (~5x today). SO THE QUESTION THIS ROW OWNS IS NOT ONLY how many MiB to grant. A cap chosen to fit today loses the same argument again in weeks, because two of the three consumers grow without bound. The options worth costing are at least: (a) raise the cap against the 16GB host budget this row already owns, (b) shrink the fixed baseline (a model release path — embedder.py has none, which is the finding on FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP, or a smaller/quantised model), (c) shrink the dataset footprint so the working set is bounded (compaction and version retention — FIX-RAG-COMPACTION-DISK-AMPLIFICATION, raised to P2 this tick on this evidence). NOT ESTABLISHED, and it gates option (a): whether the charged memory is reclaimable file-backed cache or anonymous allocation. Nobody has read the container cgroup memory.stat anon/file split — see the same caveat on the CLEAN-EXIT row. If it is mostly file cache then raising the cap buys throughput, not safety, and the real fix is (b) or (c); if it is anonymous then (a) is genuinely load-bearing. Do not size a cap change before that split is measured. PO is NOT authorising a cap change or a rebuild — user-gated infra.

review.title: system-auditor C-08 is a broken detector, not a real defect: its expected=0 threshold is mathematically unsatisfiable (24h alerts window vs 2h-TTL agent_signals stubs) AND its window over-captures via the ISO8601 strcmp bypass already fixed in the code-plane twin
review.source: PO triage of system-auditor Tier-DATA sweep c20 2026-08-05T08:18:46Z - signal sys-20260805T081846-1853. Root-caused live against the named-volume market.db (readonly) 2026-08-05T08:23-08:27Z.
review.root_cause: C-08 (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:649) is `SELECT count(*) FROM alerts a LEFT JOIN agent_signals s ON a.id = s.alert_id WHERE s.id IS NULL AND a.triggered_at > datetime('now','-24 hours')` with expected=0. TWO independent faults compound, and the reported anomaly is a FALSE POSITIVE - the alert-engine write path is HEALTHY. (A) UNSATISFIABLE THRESHOLD: agent_signals alert-correlation stubs are TTL-bound at 2h (`expiresAt(ttlMinutes ?? 120)`, agentSignalStore.ts:570/604/634/661/688/715) and hard-purged by cleanExpired() on the daily off-hours dataAuditJob cron, while `alerts` rows are retained ~30d (checkStaleAlerts.ts D-4 is UPDATE-only, never deletes). So every alert older than the last GC sweep NECESSARILY has no surviving correlation row. expected=0 can only be met if zero alerts fired in the whole stale band. The check's own code-plane inverse (checkOrphanAgentSignalsAlertId.ts:15-16) already states this in prose: 'agent_signals correlation stubs are TTL-bound, ~2h, and purged by cleanExpired(), so any historical debt self-expires' - C-08 was never re-derived against that fact. (B) ISO8601 STRCMP BYPASS: `alerts.triggered_at` is a raw JS toISOString() string ('2026-08-04T01:21:58.806Z') while `datetime('now','-24 hours')` renders space-separated ('2026-08-04 08:26:52'). At index 10 'T'(0x54) > ' '(0x20), so every row sharing the bound's date-part compares greater and the window over-captures. LIVE PROOF 2026-08-05T08:26Z: as-written window = 40 alerts / 22 orphans; TRUE 24h window (julianday) = 28 alerts / 10 orphans; the oldest row the as-written window admitted was 31 HOURS old. This is the known recurring class feedback_sqlite_iso8601_datetime_strcompare_bypass, and it was ALREADY FIXED in the code-plane twin on 2026-08-01 (checkStaleAlerts.ts:23-30 wraps both sides as `datetime(triggered_at) < datetime('now',...)` and cites the same lesson by name) - the remedy simply never propagated to the flow-doc SQL the agent actually executes. That is memory feedback_fix_landed_in_the_pregate_not_the_probe_the_agent_actually_runs.
review.evidence_write_path_is_healthy: Age-bucketed LEFT JOIN on the live DB gives a perfectly clean split with NO overlap: alerts <=17h old = 18 linked / 0 orphaned; alerts >=18h old = 22 orphaned / 0 linked. The 18h boundary equals the last cleanExpired() sweep (oldest surviving correlation stub = 2026-08-04T14:29:22Z, 17h old; 131 of 144 agent_signals rows are already past expires_at and awaiting the next sweep). Orphan status is therefore a pure function of GC timing x alert volume and carries ZERO information about write-path health. Producer-family breakdown confirms no producer-specific gap - EVERY family appears on BOTH sides (news 7 orphan/9 linked, price 9/1, ta 3/3, other 2/3, macro 1/2); a genuine co-write gap would concentrate in one family. fingerprint-null does not correlate either (21/16 vs 1/2). The brief's hypothesis that 'alert-engine writes alerts/price_alerts but not agent_signals' is DISCONFIRMED: `price_alerts` and `alert_engine_records` both hold 0 rows, and the prior co-write gap FU-ALERT-COWRITE-SCHEDULER-JOBS (2026-06 archive) is DONE and holding.
review.growth_claim_is_false: The escalating brief framed this as monotonic 1->22 growth over 15 days implying a worsening defect. RAW-verified FALSE. True firing history: 1 orphan (sys-20260721T003810-2b02, 07-21) -> 121 orphans (sys-20260730T003538-10ba, 07-30, recorded in docs/data/DASHBOARD.md:242-249 and MISSING from both the live .signal_queue and the archives) -> 22 orphans (08-05). PO 2026-08-06T12:2xZ — NOT signed off; returned to developer for one added AC. The named-volume migration itself is CORRECT and is a strict improvement (21 days of fail-open observer output ended), so PO is deliberately NOT reverting it. But AC-1 canonised `sqlite3 "file:...?immutable=1"` as the read pattern for three observer scripts on the claim that immutable=1 'bypasses WAL/-shm entirely and is always safe here'. That claim is FALSE, and PO measured it false on the live DB this tick — this is not a style nit and not an inference from memory.

RAW MEASUREMENT, live market.db, 2026-08-06T12:2xZ, with data/live/market.db-wal at 1,545,032 bytes of pending un-checkpointed writes:
  sqlite3 'file:data/live/market.db?immutable=1' -> daily_ohlcv=775891 , pragma_journal_mode='delete'
  sqlite3 'file:data/live/market.db?mode=ro'     -> daily_ohlcv=775912 , pragma_journal_mode='wal'
Two distinct defects in one measurement: (a) 21 rows silently missing, no error, no warning, no signal — the probe cannot tell a stale read from a fresh one; (b) far worse, immutable=1 reported journal_mode='delete' (the persisted header value) while the DB is actually in WAL. So the integrity probe reports the DB is in the SAFE journal mode at the exact moment it is in the DANGEROUS one. The observer whose entire purpose is catching DB drift would have certified as clean the precise condition that has now corrupted this database five times. A silently-blind integrity probe is worse than no probe, because it reads as clean telemetry.

Corroboration that this is a general rule and not a one-off: scripts/audits/verify-market-db-journal-mode.sh, which opens through the container's normal readonly path (NOT immutable=1), correctly returns journal_mode=wal at the same instant. Two observer tools on the same DB disagree right now, and the disagreement is exactly this defect.

The unifying rule to encode: immutable=1 is safe IFF -wal is 0 bytes / absent at read time, and silently wrong otherwise. Prior evidence gave contradictory unconditional verdicts (2026-06-25 'immutable=1 correct' — measured when -wal was 0 bytes, so bypassing WAL cost nothing; 2026-07-31 'immutable=1 silently stale' — measured with pending WAL). Both observations are consistent under the conditional rule; neither supports an unconditional one. The developer's AC-2 evidence ('byte-identical counts, 6/6 columns') is a single-snapshot check that almost certainly landed in a checkpointed moment and does not establish general safety.

COUPLING (why this is urgent now, not later): FIX-STOCKPRICE-PRICEHISTORY-RO-WAL-DSN-... proves market.db's journal_mode actively oscillates DELETE->WAL from four live Go re-armers. Every oscillation opens a window with pending WAL — exactly when immutable=1 goes blind. Fixing the stock-price row removes most windows but does NOT fix this: WAL can be legitimately entered again for other reasons, and an observer that is only correct when the thing it observes is already healthy is not an observer.

Either checkpoint-then-retry, or fall back to a normal read-only open, or emit an explicit UNKNOWN/DEGRADED verdict. The one forbidden outcome is emitting a number that looks clean. Fail-loud beats fail-open here — the 21-day fail-open silence this very row was minted to fix is the same failure mode in a different costume.

review.class_ref: SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP — instance 11, sub-class 6 (LLM-prose writer over a bulk structure saturates the field its own gate reads)
review.note:
MINTED 2026-07-25T16:25:39Z by po (router triage input, RAW-verified at source by po before minting — every number below was measured this tick, none relayed).

THE DEFECT IS NOT INACCURATE BOOKKEEPING — IT IS A TRIGGER THE WRITER MAKES UNSATISFIABLE.
Read contract, docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-sentiment.md:16-21 — STALE_TICKERS = watchlist tickers where last_covered_news_scout == null OR (now - last_covered) > 48h, sorted oldest-first, take <=3 per cycle. Write contract, docs/agents/news-scout/flow/stage-log-notify.md:62-63 — "for each ticker analyzed this cycle (both event-driven AND sweep-forced): set .tickers[t].last_covered_news_scout = now". The write contract is CORRECT AS WRITTEN. The execution is not: every cycle stamps ALL tickers, so no ticker can ever age past 48h, STALE_TICKERS is permanently empty, and the <=3-per-cycle rotation can never fire. The sweep is the only mechanism guaranteeing periodic coverage of low-news watchlist tickers; it has been the equivalent of disabled.

MEASURED (docs/data/coverage-state.json, .tickers has 57 entries):
  - after the 16:14Z tick: all 57 carry the byte-identical stamp 2026-07-25T16:14:39Z (jq group_by -> ONE group, n=57).
  - previous committed version: all 57 carry the byte-identical stamp 2026-07-25T12:10:42Z (ONE group, n=57).
  - the 16:14Z cycle (c200) analyzed 2 tickers by its own evidence trail: fragments #584 VNM and #585 MARKET. Not 57.
  - COVERAGE COST, the reason this is P1: ~2 of 57 tickers get event-driven coverage per cycle. The other ~55 are reachable ONLY via the sweep. With the sweep alive (<=3/cycle, ~6 cycles/day) full rotation completes in ~3.2 days; with it dead the long tail gets zero scheduled coverage indefinitely.

SCOPE IS DOUBLE WHAT THE INPUT REPORTED — MARKET-WATCHER HAS THE IDENTICAL DEFECT, LIVE.
The triage input named only news-scout. po checked the sibling field in the same file and it is equally saturated: all 57 tickers carry byte-identical last_covered_market_watcher = 2026-07-25T08:10:06Z. market-watcher's flow carries the same pair of contracts in the same shape — read at docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/cycle.md:60-73, write at :240-250 ("for each ticker priced this cycle (both anomaly-driven AND sweep-forced)"). Any fix that touches only news-scout leaves half the defect live. BOTH agents are in scope; this is stated here because a narrow reading of the originating report would miss it.

THE BEHAVIOUR IS INTERMITTENT, NOT A CLEAN REGRESSION — DO NOT CHASE A BREAKING COMMIT.
po walked 25 historical revisions of the file. Distinct-stamp counts for last_covered_news_scout: 3/4/7 on 06-30, then 1 across 07-02..07-21, then 5 at 819fff993 (07-23, correct shape: a 38-ticker fossil group at 07-21T16:14 plus small 2/2/4/11 groups from later cycles), then 1/1 on 07-25. last_covered_market_watcher: 8,9,10,10,10,6,7,11 through 07-23, then 1,1 on 07-25. So BOTH agents have produced correct per-ticker stamping at some points and blanket stamping at others, with no code change in between. THAT IS THE ROOT CAUSE AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: the write is a prose instruction executed by an LLM against a 57-entry JSON blob, so faithfulness is non-deterministic per cycle. Editing the prose to say it more emphatically is NOT a fix — the prose is already correct. The fix must move the write to a deterministic scripted surgical patch.

INDEPENDENT PROOF THE WRITE IS A FULL-DOC OVERWRITE, NOT A MERGE — A TOP-LEVEL CONFIG KEY WAS SILENTLY DELETED.
coverage-state.json had a top-level sweep_config block ({max_staleness_hours: 48, sweep_batch_size: 3}) — present at 0866c35b6 (2026-07-21), ABSENT from 819fff993 (2026-07-23) onward, and absent live today. Nothing deleted it deliberately; a hand-rewrite of the blob dropped it. Corroborated by docs/handoffs/2026-07-16-coverage-state-cross-agent-lost-update-and-three-premise-corrections.md:16, which enumerates the then-current top-level keys including sweep_config, and by docs/data/.trash/2026-07-20/docs/archive/coverage-state.json.tmp:67 which still carries it. CONSEQUENCE, fold into this fix: BOTH flow docs still cite "sweep_config.sweep_batch_size" (stage-sentiment.md:21, cycle.md:73) against a key that no longer exists — a dangling config reference. It is currently harmless only because the prose also hardcodes "<=3" next to it, and max_staleness_hours=48 now survives solely as prose in two files. Restore the block (or relocate the two constants to a real config surface) as part of this row; do NOT mint a separate row for it.

CO-SHIP — THIS ROW AND FIX-COVERAGE-STATE-CROSS-AGENT-LOST-UPDATE ARE ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO.
That row (backlog/P2/M/plan_only, minted 2026-07-16) records the same file being clobbered on the _ssot blob across agents, and its candidate direction (i) reads "serialize the two writers behind a shared coverage-state write helper that does read-modify-merge (not full-doc overwrite)". This row is direct corroboration that (i) is correct and that the live write IS a full-doc overwrite — the vanished sweep_config key is the proof that row was missing. One helper satisfies both ACs; shipping them separately means editing the same write step in the same two flow files twice, with the second edit racing the first. Sequence: this row leads (P1, live coverage loss), the lost-update row closes with it and its AC 1 becomes AC 3 below.

ROUTED DIRECT TO developer, NOT ba, DELIBERATELY. The sibling row was minted plan_only/next_agent=ba on 2026-07-16 because its direction was genuinely open between three candidates. That question is now CLOSED by the sweep_config deletion evidence above, which is the discriminating observation that row lacked. What remains is one shell script, its test, and two flow-doc edits against a fully specified AC — that is a direct FIX, and holding a P1 live-coverage-loss behind a planning hop for a settled design would be disproportionate. The implementer MUST NOT re-open the direction; if implementation reveals the direction is wrong after all, bounce the row back to po with the contradicting evidence rather than re-scoping in place.

REMEDY SHAPE (direction settled, details open to ba/architect):
Replace the prose read-modify-write in BOTH flow files with one deterministic script — proposed scripts/agents-flow/coverage-stamp.sh, invoked as `coverage-stamp.sh --agent <news-scout|market-watcher> --tickers VNM,FPT` — that does a surgical jq patch of ONLY the named tickers, preserves every other key byte-for-byte, and holds a short mutex (task_claim "coverage-state:main", TTL ~30s) around the read-modify-write. review.title: scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-bounded1.jq: (a) no own WIP re-check — re-claims a ready[] row still stamped promoted_by="dev-team (bounded-1 auto-pickup)" while a different row holds the WIP slot; (b) its selector is $auto_promoted[0] = ARRAY POSITION, not priority — starves every higher-priority ready[] row
review.desc: RAW-VERIFIED AT SOURCE (scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-bounded1.jq, 82L). The claim selector is lines 39-42: `[ (.task_board.ready // [])[] | select(.promoted_by == "dev-team (bounded-1 auto-pickup)") ]` — a pure stamp match, with ZERO reference to .task_board.in_progress length anywhere in the file (grep: the only in_progress touches are the line-49 append and the line-58/63 head fields). The file states its own load-bearing assumption in its header comment at lines 13-14: "Under the BOUNDED-1 gate (promote only fires when WIP==0, i.e. ready[] was already empty) there is at most one such row." That assumption holds only while the promote script is the sole writer of the stamp AND nothing ever returns a stamped row to ready[]. It is violated when PO (or any evictor) moves a promoted row back to ready[] WITHOUT clearing promoted_by: the stale stamp then makes the row re-claimable on any later tick regardless of current WIP. The claim trusts the stamp as a proxy for WIP instead of measuring WIP itself. NOTE ON SCOPE — the head-clobber half is already fixed and must not be re-fixed: lines 57-59 compute $head_free and lines 71-79 deliberately preserve a live .head (FIX-DEVTEAM-CLAIM-SCRIPTS-UNCONDITIONAL-HEAD-OVERWRITE, PO ratification ruling-20260730T0906Z STEP po-4). But that guard only protects .head — the row is STILL appended to in_progress[] at line 49 before the head branch is evaluated, so a second concurrent row lands in in_progress[] with no head pointing at it. This is the actual leak. LIVE OBSERVATION 2026-08-06T10:13Z: BOUNDED-1 re-claimed FIX-DEPTHTHIN-B-GATEWAY-TA-PATH-REWRITE via a 2026-08-01 promoted_by stamp. That particular outcome was CORRECT by policy (WIP was <2, re-promotion is intended) — the row is not filed against that dispatch; it is filed against the mechanism, which arrived at a correct answer for the wrong reason and will arrive at a wrong answer when WIP is saturated.
review.source: telegram report id=4495 message_id=4784 from qa (2026-08-06), live-reproduced in scripts/audits/devteam-dispatch-gate-satisfiability.sh case "BOUNDED-1 correctly no-ops when in_progress>=1"
review.status_note: AC1: the claim script measures WIP ITSELF — add an `(.task_board.in_progress // []) | length` guard so the claim is a no-op when WIP is already at cap, independent of any promoted_by stamp. Do NOT implement this as "clear the stamp on eviction" only: that fixes the one known producer of stale stamps and leaves the claim still trusting a field it does not own (feedback_reader_writes_its_own_trigger_field_check_is_vacuous). Stamp-clearing on eviction is a fine ADDITIONAL hardening, not the fix. AC2: the existing live case in scripts/audits/devteam-dispatch-gate-satisfiability.sh titled "BOUNDED-1 correctly no-ops when in_progress>=1" must pass — it currently FAILS, which is how qa found this. AC3: negative control — a fixture with WIP=0 and one stale-stamped ready[] row must still claim normally (do not over-tighten into never claiming). AC4: the header comment at lines 13-14 must be corrected; it currently documents the unsound assumption as if it were an invariant.
review.root_cause: Both defects are the same 3 lines of scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-bounded1.jq:39-46. The file's own header comment states the invariant it relies on: 'Under the BOUNDED-1 gate (promote only fires when WIP==0, i.e. ready[] was already empty) there is at most one such row.' That invariant is FALSE on the live board — ready[] holds 62 rows and TWO of them carry the promoted_by stamp simultaneously. Once the 'at most one' premise fails, `$auto_promoted[0]` silently degrades from 'the one promoted row' to 'whichever promoted row happens to sit at the lowest array index', which is insertion order and carries no priority information at all. There is no sort_by(priority_rank) anywhere in the file (grep-verified: zero sort_by / priority_rank / limit occurrences).
review.evidence: PO measured this live at 2026-08-06T18:21Z, not inferred. (1) TWO stale bounded-1 stamps are resident in ready[] right now: idx=57 FIX-JANITOR-HEALTHRECHECK-IDEMPOTENCY-GUARD-MISSES-PROCESSED-DIR (P2, promoted_at 2026-08-06T17:15:28Z) and idx=61 FIX-NEWSVPS-OVERNIGHT-PUSH-OUTAGE-663M-SILENT (P1, promoted_at 2026-08-06T17:58:35Z) — independently corroborated the same tick by qa via Telegram report 4467, which named both rows unprompted. ac: AC-1 (WIP) claim-bounded1.jq must re-check its own WIP before claiming: if .task_board.in_progress already holds a row, the script is a NO-OP. Today it has no such check and the header's 'promote only fires when WIP==0' premise is the only thing standing in for one — a premise about a DIFFERENT script, which the live board disproves.

qa.root_cause: apps/stock-price/pkg/infrastructure/fetchers.go:303 (SQLitePriceHistoryRepository.GetHistory) and :240 (Tier3Fetcher) build the DSN 'file:%s?mode=ro&_journal_mode=WAL&_busy_timeout=5000'. The live market.db has PRAGMA journal_mode=delete, so the driver issuing PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL over a mode=ro connection fails with SQLITE_READONLY(8) 'attempt to write a readonly database'. The resulting db.Query error is then discarded at fetchers.go:318-320 ('return []domain.DailyOHLCV{}, nil //nolint:nilerr'), with the same swallow at :305-307 for sql.Open — so the handler emits HTTP 200 with an empty history and logs nothing. The two SIBLING repositories in this same package already fixed exactly this: foreign_flow_repository.go:33 and room_event_repository.go:32 both carry the comment 'Note: readonly mode (mode=ro) conflicts with WAL journal mode creation.' and dropped mode=ro from their DSN. The correction was applied to 2 of 4 call sites; fetchers.go:240 and :303 were missed.
qa.evidence: RAW-VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-31T00:25Z — every hop measured, not inferred. (1) The data EXISTS: sqlite3 on data/live/market.db (the bind-mount source of the container's /app/data) gives daily_ohlcv HVN = 775 rows spanning 2023-06-27..2026-07-30, and the handler's exact query (WHERE code='HVN' AND date >= date('now','-30 days')) returns 22. This is NOT the thin-ticker / new-listing data gap the alert text implies. (2) Outage reproduced: curl localhost:5005/reading/HVN -> 503 'insufficient price data ... requires at least 7 price points'; curl localhost:5005/market (VNINDEX) -> the same 503. BOTH kinh-dich routes are dead. (3) Failing hop isolated: gateway localhost:4000/stock/price/history?code=HVN&days=30 -> {code:HVN,history:[]}, identically empty for FPT/VNM/VCB and for days=30/365/3650 (universal and parameter-independent); but mcp-server's own localhost:3000/api/prices/history?code=HVN&days=30 -> count:22 with full rows. Same DB, same window, opposite result => the defect is in stock-price, not in the data. (4) stock-price direct: localhost:5010/price/history?code=HVN&days=30 -> {code:HVN,history:[]} while /health returns {status:ok} — passive health masking dead data. (5) Root cause reproduced in isolation: sqlite3 'file:data/live/market.db?mode=ro' 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;' -> 'Error: stepping, attempt to write a readonly database (8)', and a SELECT appended after that PRAGMA never executes; the same SELECT on a mode=ro connection WITHOUT the WAL pragma returns 22. PRAGMA journal_mode on the live DB = delete. (6) Alternatives ruled out at source: container clocks are exact (stock-price, mcp-server, kinh-dich and api-gateway all match the host to the second, so no date('now') drift); DB_PATH=/app/data/market.db resolves to a present 401MB file inside the container; and only 3 commits touched apps/stock-price since its image was built, none of them on the read path — so this is a live SOURCE defect, NOT a stale-image/deploy-lane problem. qa.blast_radius: P1 — total loss of two product surfaces, not one ticker. (a) kinh-dich-service reads PRICE_HISTORY_URL -> api-gateway -> stock-price, so ComputeScores() receives nil for every code: get_kinhdich_reading 503s for ALL tickers and for the VNINDEX /market reading. (b) apps/frontend/app/lib/api/client.ts:245 calls the same /stock/price/history endpoint, so the frontend price-history chart renders empty. (c) fetchers.go:240 Tier3Fetcher carries the identical broken DSN, exposing the tier-3 price path to the same silent-empty failure.
qa.recommended_action: 1) Drop 'mode=ro&' from the DSN at fetchers.go:240 and :303 so all four call sites in this package match the already-corrected foreign_flow_repository.go:36 / room_event_repository.go:35 form ('file:%s?_journal_mode=WAL&_busy_timeout=5000'). 2) Stop swallowing: fetchers.go:305-307 and :318-320 must return the error — the HTTP layer at router.go:111-116 already has a correct 500 path with slog.Error, and the silent nilerr is precisely what let a total outage present as a per-ticker 503 for an unknown duration. 3) Regression test: assert GetHistory returns a non-empty slice against a fixture DB whose journal_mode is 'delete' — that is the exact condition that fails today and that a WAL-mode fixture would mask.
qa.misleading_alert_note: The kinh-dich 503 text is itself a defect amplifier and deserves a fix in the same pass or an immediate follow-up: price_score.go:32-41 collapses BOTH 'source fetch errored' and 'genuinely fewer than 7 points' into one nil return, which usecases.go:80/85/124/129 convert to ErrInsufficientData and router.go renders as 503 'requires at least 7 price points'. A total upstream outage is therefore reported as a thin-data condition — which is what steered this incident toward a per-ticker data-gap reading instead of a service outage.

po_architect_signoff_20260807T0545.amendment_3_FR1_WINDOWKEY_MIDNIGHT_STRAD: BINDING CORRECTION to brief Section 2, fallback branch 2 (the ACTIVE day-one path, per the brief's own Section 1). As written, WINDOW_KEY = <date portion of live_mcp_fetched_at> + 'T' + CRON_HOUR + '00Z' unconditionally pairs the RUN's UTC calendar date with the SLOT's cron hour. That re-introduces this row's own collision class at the UTC day boundary for any fire that is not same-UTC-day as its own nominal window. Two reachable cases, both live: (a) bctc-analyst-slot-4's cron is '0 0 * * *' = exactly 00:00Z — a backstop/catch-up fire a few minutes EARLY (23:5xZ) keys to the PREVIOUS day's slot-4 window and clobbers a 24h-old file; (b) a slot-3 ('0 21 * * *') run delayed past midnight, or an ordinary operator re-run of slot-3 the following morning, keys to a FUTURE window (D+1 21:00Z) that the real D+1 fire will then collide with. Neither is exotic: FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION documents live off-nominal re-fires, and EC-1 manual re-runs are explicitly in scope. FIX (deterministic, pure, no extra I/O, does not change the function's signature): branch 2 must select the occurrence of CRON_HOUR:00Z NEAREST to live_mcp_fetched_at — evaluate the candidate set {yesterday, today, tomorrow} at CRON_HOUR:00Z and take min |delta| — rather than unconditionally concatenating today's UTC date. 'Nearest' (not 'most recent at-or-before') is required because it is the only rule correct for BOTH the early-fire and late-fire directions. Add to the brief's own Section 8 test strategy a 4th unit case: slot-4 with live_mcp_fetched_at = D at 23:57Z must resolve to (D+1)T0000Z, and slot-3 with live_mcp_fetched_at = (D+1) at 08:00Z must resolve to (D)T2100Z.
